rationale: Mega Blaziken's high Speed and Attack give it a good matchup against metagame staples like Incineroar, Kingambit, and Gholdengo. With Speed Boost, it can essentially guarantee it is the fastest Pokemon on the field after enough turns have passed, outspeeding Mega Aerodactyl and slower Pokemon like Sylveon even if they have a boost from Tailwind. Rock Slide: Rock Slide OHKOes Mega Charizard Y. Combined with Speed Boost, Rock Slide lets Mega Blaziken threaten flinches before foes can move. Detect: Detect is mandatory to safely gain Speed boosts. Other Options Swords Dance: Swords Dance can be used to offset Intimidate from Incineroar and make Mega Blaziken strong enough to OHKO Garchomp with Close Combat at +1 Attack. It can replace Rock Slide on teams that have another way to cover Mega Charizard Y, such as Mega Aerodactyl. SP Spreads 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: Speed Boost allows Adamant Mega Blaziken to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl after one turn. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Opting for a Jolly nature allows Mega Blaziken to always outspeed Sylveon under Tailwind after one turn. Teambuilding Rain Matchup: Mega Swampert threatens to OHKO Mega Blaziken with either STAB attack, and Swift Swim lets it outspeed Mega Blaziken in the rain even after a turn of Speed Boost. Basculegion-M and Pelipper resist both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks and respond with an OHKO from Wave Crash and Hurricane or Weather Ball, respectively; Pelipper also weakens Flare Blitz while enabling Mega Swampert with Drizzle. Other Weaknesses: Garchomp threatens an OHKO with Earthquake, which cannot be redirected by Sinistcha's Rage Powder. Mega Aerodactyl threatens an OHKO with Dual Wingbeat and can use Tailwind before Mega Blaziken gets its Speed Boost to deny Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage. Whimsicott has Tailwind to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage and Encore to punish it for using Detect to gain Speed Boosts. Opposing Trick Room uses Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost against it, and Farigiraf threatens to OHKO it with Psychic. Mega Staraptor enters the field with Intimidate, threatens an OHKO with Brave Bird, and is often paired with Whimsicott to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost with Tailwind. Mega Delphox threatens an OHKO with Psychic or Psyshock. Ceruledge completely walls both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks. Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M has a better matchup against rain teams and Mega Aerodactyl, while Mega Blaziken helps it against Archaludon. Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and Torkoal overwrite rain; Alolan Ninetales handles Garchomp with Blizzard; and Torkoal is useful in Trick Room while providing sun to let Flare Blitz OHKO bulky variants of Sylveon and offensive variants of Farigiraf. Sinistcha can nearly OHKO Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and use Rage Powder to redirect threatening attacks like Pelipper's Weather Ball and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. It can also redirect neutral attacks that threaten Mega Blaziken due to its low bulk, like Sneasler's Dire Claw and Close Combat. Sinistcha helps offset Flare Blitz recoil with Hospitality and can also reverse Trick Room. Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Kingambit, which threatens Sinistcha. Kingambit threatens to OHKO Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch and is comfortable against Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge, as it can survive their attacks and either OHKO them in return or deal enough damage to finish them off with Sucker Punch. Due to Defiant, Kingambit's presence can also deter Incineroar from switching in and activating Intimidate against Mega Blaziken. In return, Mega Blaziken handles Mega Charizard Y for Kingambit with Rock Slide. Sylveon is a strong answer to Garchomp, and Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Steel-types that threaten Sylveon, such as Gholdengo and Mega Metagross. Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Aerodactyl can take the place of Mega Blaziken against teams with nuisances like Garchomp, Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and opposing Mega Aerodactyl. Mega Blaziken complements Mega Aerodactyl by beating its counters: Mega Tyranitar, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile. Mega Froslass has a better matchup against rain teams by setting snow over rain, and it is also strong against Garchomp and the combination of Mega Staraptor and Whimsicott. Mega Blaziken also plays well against Mega Froslass's counters: Mega Charizard Y, Kingambit, and Incineroar.

Gholdengo, thanks to its naturally strong defensive typing, easily walls out common Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and helps beat top Pokemon like Mega Floette, Sylveon, Mega Aerodactyl, and Sinistcha. This typing allows Gholdengo to set up Nasty Plot, letting it sweep through teams with its STAB moves and threaten nearly all metagame staples with at least neutral damage. Make It Rain: Make It Rain hits nearly anything that doesn't resist it for huge damage after a Nasty Plot, having a solid chance to OHKO Mega Tyranitar with Life Orb. When using Make It Rain, Gholdengo must be careful; using it at the wrong time late-game will leave Gholdengo too weak to contribute much . This forces Gholdengo to use Nasty Plot again and leave itself or its partner open to attacks. Life Orb: Life Orb gives Gholdengo potential for large amounts of burst damage, allowing Gholdengo to OHKO most Mega Froslass with Make It Rain and Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball, though it comes at the cost of Gholdengo's longevity. For this reason, builds that use Life Orb Gholdengo tend to run faster and more offensive SP spreads to turn it into a strong and threatening attacker that doesn't require setup turns. Spell Tag and Metal Coat: Spell Tag and Metal Coat save Gholdengo's longevity but only allow it to boost either Shadow Ball or Make it Rain. Spell Tag allows Gholdengo to 2HKO Sneasler, while Metal Coat allows Gholdengo to OHKO Mega Aerodactyl. Good as Gold: Good as Gold gives Gholdengo good chances to switch into attacks like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Grimmsnarl as well as Sleep Powder from Venusaur. Other Options Leftovers: Leftovers allow Gholdengo to focus more on setting up by increasing its longevity, though the item sacrifices power. SP Spreads 32 HP / 8 Def / 7 SpA / 3 SpD / 16 Spe with Timid: The given SP spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M, almost always survive Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Garchomp, and withstand Dark Pulse from Mega Blastoise, with the rest dumped into Special Attack. 7 HP / 32 SpA / 27 Spe with Timid: This SP spread is tailored towards Life Orb sets. It lets Gholdengo outrun Jolly Basculegion-M and survive Wave Crash from Choice Scarf Adamant Basculegion-M, allowing Gholdengo to retaliate with Shadow Ball. The remaining SPs are put into Special Attack. 17 HP / 1 Def / 15 SpA / 1 SpD / 32 Spe with Modest: With the SPs in HP, Defense, and Special Defense, Gholdengo can possibly survive Flare Blitz from Incineroar and has a high chance to survive Heat Wave from Timid Mega Delphox. The SPs in Special Attack allow Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball to OHKO Mega Delphox and +2 Make It Rain to OHKO uninvested Mega Tyranitar, which typically uses Dragon Dance sets. The Speed SPs allow Gholdengo to outspeed all Mega Tyranitar. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Blaziken, Incineroar, and Mega Scovillain threaten huge damage onto Gholdengo with Heat Wave, Weather Ball, Flare Blitz, and Overheat. Incineroar in particular resists both of Gholdengo's STAB options, tanking Make It Rain and Shadow Ball and retaliating with Throat Chop or Flare Blitz. Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo with Last Respects and Shadow Ball. Hydreigon, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar are Dark-types that OHKO Gholdengo with Dark Pulse, Kowtow Cleave, and Knock Off. Additionally, Hydreigon can opt for Snarl instead to slowly chip down Gholdengo and weaken it in the process, and Kingambit can use Sucker Punch to hit Gholdengo before it moves. Ground-types like Mega Swampert and Garchomp threaten Gholdengo with Earthquake. Mega Swampert also resists Make It Rain and is placed on rain teams alongside Pokemon like Hydreigon and Archaludon, which can deal lots of damage to Gholdengo with Dark Pulse and Electro Shot. On the other hand, Garchomp's flexibility enables it to fit on many teams, meaning that it is a hurdle that Gholdengo often has to face. Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp threatens Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain with Earthquake, and it can handle Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. Incineroar and Kingambit can switch into Ghost-types and threaten them with Throat Chop and Kowtow Cleave, while Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can help Gholdengo handle Dark-types with Close Combat. Sinistcha can heal up Gholdengo with Hospitality and redirect many attacks with Rage Powder; it can also switch into Ground-types and threaten Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. Alolan Ninetales can threaten Ground-types with Freeze-Dry and Blizzard.

Grimmsnarl utilizes its access to Prankster and dual screens to become a premier support Pokemon within Regulation M-B, supporting big threats like Archaludon and having a favorable type matchup against the likes of Basculegion-M and Garchomp. Parting Shot: Thanks to Prankster, Parting Shot turns Grimmsnarl into a fast pivot option, allowing it to easily get out of sticky situations like a regular swap with the added benefit of lowering the opponent's offenses. Although it acts before most moves, Parting Shot does occur after players switch or Mega Evolve their Pokemon, allowing Grimmsnarl to bring in an ally weather setter on the same turn the opponent attempts to set up weather by one of the aforementioned methods. Spirit Break versus Foul Play: Spirit Break allows Grimmsnarl to hit Dragon-types like Garchomp and Hydreigon hard while reducing the Special Attack of foes like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Floette, usually when they are switching in due to Grimmsnarl's low Speed. Spirit Break also deals significant damage to Mega Floette. Foul Play, on the other hand, is capable of OHKOing Basculegion-M and 2HKOing Mega Swampert and most Garchomp. Light Clay: Thanks to Light Clay, partners like Archaludon and Gholdengo have more time to set up safely behind dual screens. Other Options Fake Out: Fake Out can be used over its attacking moves, allowing Grimmsnarl to provide further support by giving partners like Gholdengo an opportunity to set up. However, this leaves it vulnerable to moves like Taunt from Maushold. Scary Face: Scary Face can be used over Spirit Break or Foul Play to grant Grimmsnarl an option of speed control, though it leaves Grimmsnarl entirely passive. SP Spreads 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD with Careful: The given SPs allow Grimmsnarl to survive Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M and, when Light Screen is set up, Moonblast from Mega Floette. The Defense SPs allow Grimmsnarl to always survive Dire Claw from Jolly Sneasler. A Calm nature can be run when using Foul Play to decrease damage from confusion and opposing Foul Play. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit, Mega Metagross, Archaludon, and Gholdengo threaten Grimmsnarl with Iron Head, Flash Cannon, and Make It Rain. Kingambit can switch in on Spirit Break to activate Defiant, while Gholdengo is immune to Parting Shot and can use Nasty Plot to offset the Special Attack drops from Spirit Break, which does minimal damage to it. Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten huge damage onto Grimmsnarl through dual screens, especially against sets without Spirit Break. Farigiraf, thanks to Armor Tail, denies Parting Shot and, if it's run, Scary Face from affecting Farigiraf's allies, severely hindering Grimmsnarl's effectiveness. Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar prevent Grimmsnarl from setting up dual screens, leaving it vulnerable to another attack like Moonblast from Mega Floette. Sneasler itself threatens huge damage onto Grimmsnarl with Dire Claw, while Incineroar is immune to Prankster moves and easily tanks any attacks that Grimmsnarl carries. Outside of pressuring a few select targets like Basculegion-M, Grimmsnarl struggles to carry an offensive presence on the field, leaving itself to be rather easily ignored. Good Partners and Synergies: Offensive partners like Gholdengo are recommended to offset Grimmsnarl's passivity. Gholdengo is able to threaten Fairy-types and walls out Farigiraf and Sneasler, as well as having a good matchup against Mega Metagross without Stomping Tantrum. Archaludon fills this role well as well, acting as a bulkier partner that exchanges Gholdengo's good Fairy-type matchup for a better matchup against physical attackers like Kingambit thanks to a combination of Reflect and Stamina. Mega Staraptor threatens Steel-types with Close Combat. In return, Grimmsnarl not only provides dual screens but can also use Parting Shot on Mega Staraptor to make it even stronger thanks to Contrary. Grimmsnarl can also use Spirit Break to offset boosts granted to opposing Archaludon by Electro Shot, allowing Mega Staraptor to feel less threatened. Sinistcha creates a strong supportive core alongside Grimmsnarl, healing up common partners behind dual screens and allowing them to easily set up and sweep games. Mega Swampert can use Earthquake or High Horsepower to hit Steel-types, Sneasler, and Incineroar hard while also threatening big damage onto the format's Fairy-types with Wave Crash. Grimmsnarl, in return, can easily pivot to Pelipper against opposing weather setters with Parting Shot. Archaludon also appreciates this to become a dangerous sweeper thanks to the combination of dual screens, Stamina, (AC) and Electro Shot.

Mega Pyroar is a devastating sun attacker in Regulation M-B, taking advantage of Fire Mane and the sun to deal monstrous amounts of damage. Mega Pyroar's typing makes it immune to Basculegion-M's Last Respects and resistant to Gholdengo's and Mega Charizard Y's main STAB attacks as well as Fairy-type attacks from Mega Floette, Mega Gardevoir, and Sylveon. Overheat: Overheat allows Mega Pyroar to OHKO nearly everything in the metagame with enough damage multipliers, including Pokemon that may resist Overheat, such as Incineroar and Garchomp. Solar Beam: Solar Beam is used to hit Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert for super effective damage. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Pelipper and Politoed can decrease Mega Pyroar's damage output with Drizzle while threatening it with rain-boosted Weather Ball. Rain allows Mega Swampert to outspeed and threaten Mega Pyroar with either STAB attack while denying Solar Beam as a coverage option. Focus Sash Sneasler can survive one attack from Mega Pyroar and OHKO it back with Close Combat. Unburden-boosted Sneasler can also outspeed and OHKO Mega Pyroar. Sneasler's Fake Out can also slow down Mega Pyroar's momentum. Garchomp and Basculegion-M resist Mega Pyroar's Fire-type moves while threatening to OHKO it with Life Orb-boosted Earthquake and Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash, respectively. Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed Mega Pyroar, survive a sun- and Fire Mane-boosted Overheat, block Heat Wave with Wide Guard, 2HKO Mega Pyroar with Rock Slide, and set up Tailwind for other Mega Pyroar checks such as Garchomp to outspeed it. Mega Tyranitar can shut off the sun, reducing Mega Pyroar's damage output while resisting its Fire-type attacks and threatening it with Rock Slide. Ceruledge soaks up Mega Pyroar's Fire-type attacks while resisting Solar Beam. Ceruledge also takes advantage of the sun while setting up with Bulk Up in the face of Mega Pyroar. Notably, at +1 Attack, Bitter Blade in the sun 2HKOes Mega Pyroar. Choice Scarf Hydreigon resists all of Mega Pyroar's moves while outspeeding it and weakening it with Snarl or threatening it with Earth Power. Mega Dragonite also resists all of Mega Pyroar's moves while setting up Tailwind in its face and chunking it with Dragon Pulse. Good Partners and Synergies: Torkoal enables Mega Pyroar's immense damage output with Drought. It also provides a Trick Room mode with Farigiraf as well as Helping Hand support, allowing Mega Pyroar to OHKO no-bulk Garchomp and Impish Incineroar with Overheat and 2HKO most Mega Charizard Y sets with Heat Wave if sun is up. Farigiraf nullifies Fake Out, preventing it from stalling out Mega Pyroar's sun turns or disrupting its momentum, and can set up Trick Room for Mega Pyroar's partner Torkoal. Farigiraf can OHKO Sneasler through Focus Sash with Twin Beam and threaten Water-types like Pelipper, Politoed, and Basculegion-M with Thunderbolt. Venusaur threatens Basculegion-M with Solar Beam and can put foes to sleep with Sleep Powder. Whimsicott gives Mega Pyroar speed control with Tailwind and weather control with Sunny Day. Whimsicott resists both of Garchomp's STAB attacks while chunking it with Moonblast. Vileplume also utilizes Sleep Powder but has access to After You, allowing allied Torkoal to fire off Eruption almost immediately. However, Vileplume is forced to run Focus Sash and does not hit as hard as Venusaur. Mega Floette can threaten the Dragon-types that may hinder Mega Pyroar with Fairy Aura-boosted Dazzling Gleam and Moonblast.

Mega Raichu Y is a great utility Mega Pokemon that is able to support its teammates with the fastest Fake Out currently available in the game and access to perfectly accurate Zap Cannons that heavily pressure metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Aerodactyl, and Basculegion-M, and the guaranteed paralysis acts as speed control for partners with middling Speed against fast threats such as Chlorophyl Venusaur, Mega Delphox, and Sneasler. Lightning Rod: Before Mega Evolving, Raichu can act as a strong option against opposing Raichu and stifle the attempts of opposing Archaludon to steamroll with Electro Shot. Delaying Mega Evolution can let Raichu boost its Special Attack off the attacks of certain opposing Pokemon, letting it set up to get major OHKOs it wouldn't be able to normally such as Chople Berry Kingambit with Focus Blast. Focus Blast: Focus Blast lets Mega Raichu Y beat Pokemon like Archaludon, Hydreigon, and the ever-present Kingambit. It also provides useful neutral coverage into important Pokemon that resist Zap Cannon such as Garchomp. Other Options Grass Knot: Sacrificing utility for coverage, Grass Knot can be a good option for Mega Raichu Y to be able to OHKO Mega Swampert should it receive speed control. While Grass Knot can flip the matchup against Mega Swampert, it is only really valuable versus Mega Swampert. The Fake Out slot is generally considered the flex slot on Mega Raichu Y, so Grass Knot or any other moves considered would replace it. Losing Fake Out will make Mega Raichu Y more one-dimensional, as it will not be able to actively support its teammates and will no longer have much value before Mega Evolving. Volt Switch: Volt Switch can be used as an option to pivot Mega Raichu Y around and keep it healthy to provide late-game pressure once its checks have been dealt with. Encore: Encore is a greatly oppressive tool that can punish passive play, such as Protect, Fake Out, and setup. This can be used over Focus Blast to lean into the support potential of Mega Raichu Y. Threatening the potential of Fake Out, making opposing Pokemon use Protect, and punishing them immediately after with Encore provides teammates such as Kingambit more opportunity to set up. SP Spreads 29 HP / 14 Def / 23 Spe with Timid: The HP and Defense means Raichu can take Black Glasses Kowtow Cleave from Adamant Kingambit, Close Combat from Jolly Sneasler, and almost always survive Psychic Fangs from Jolly Mega Metagross. The HP investment and Mega Raichu Y's natural Special Defense stat lets it take a maximum Special Attack Modest Mega Charizard Y Heat Wave in the sun. The Speed investment will allow Mega Raichu Y to outspeed Jolly Sneasler and Timid Mega Froslass. 32 HP / 21 Def / 5 SpD / 8 Spe with Timid: This spread sacrifices some of the Speed of the previous spread in favor of allowing Mega Raichu Y to survive Earthquake from an Intimidated Jolly Life Orb Garchomp. It will also let Mega Raichu Y survive Life Orb Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Jolly Mega Staraptor's Close Combat. The Special Defense investment will guarantee survival from an Earth Power from Modest Life Orb Venusaur. The Speed outspeeds Modest Mega Froslass and Adamant Sneasler. 32 HP / 1 Def / 1 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: This spread is a lot more simplified to take advantage of Mega Raichu Y's impressive base 130 Speed stat, allowing it to Speed tie Aerodactyl and Mega Gengar. Maximum HP investment with 1 Defense SP will guarantee survival from a Sucker Punch from Life Orb Adamant Kingambit, with the last SP going into Special Attack. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Raichu Y struggles greatly into opposing Ground-type Pokemon. Mega Swampert and Garchomp are especially difficult for Mega Raichu Y to maneuver around safely. Each of them are capable of OHKOing Mega Raichu Y with Ground-type moves such as Earthquake and High Horsepower or Stomping Tantrum, respectively. Mamoswine can be difficult for Mega Raichu Y if it is a Choice Scarf or Focus Sash variant or has redirection support. It does not appreciate taking a Focus Blast, but if it can avoid it the hit by being faster, or having redirection, or surviving the hit with Focus Sash, it will be able to OHKO Mega Raichu Y with High Horsepower. Sand Rush Excadrill can cause issues for similar reasons; the boosted Speed and Focus Sash to guarantee survival from a Focus Blast can be difficult to navigate. Grass-type Pokemon, such as Sinistcha and Venusaur, that resist Focus Blast and Zap Cannon are near-impossible to muscle through. Sinistcha can freely set up Trick Room in front of Mega Raichu Y or enable its partner to freely deal with Mega Raichu Y by redirecting hits with Rage Powder. Venusaur, both Mega and non-Mega, is a great challenge for Mega Raichu Y. The Mega Venusaur variants are able to shrug off any hit and threaten it back with Earth Power or recover the damage with Giga Drain, while the non-Mega variants outspeed with a Chlorophyll boost and either potentially KOing Mega Raichu Y with Life Orb Earth Power or taking advantage of Mega Raichu Y's own No Guard for perfectly accurate Sleep Powders. Whimsicott also resists all of Mega Raichu Y's coverage options but with the added pressure from Encore locking any Fake Out attempts. It can also enable its partners such as Basculegion-M to outspeed and KO Mega Raichu Y after setting up Tailwind. Due to Mega Raichu Y's overall lackluster defensive stats, it can be easily kept in check with strong priority moves such as Sucker Punch from Kingambit and Aqua Jet from Basculegion-M; both of these are capable of 2HKOing even bulky variants of Mega Raichu Y, though Basculegion-M requires a boosting item such as Mystic Water or Life Orb to have a chance at a 2HKO. Good Partners: Teammates that hit popular Ground-type Pokemon such as Garchomp and Mega Swampert are a must. Sinistcha is a great Grass-type partner that can beat Mega Swampert while providing passive recovery and redirection support. Basculegion-M loves the support Mega Raichu Y provides and can pin Garchomp and Mega Swampert with exceptionally powerful Wave Crashes and Aqua Jets. Setup Pokemon such as Kingambit enjoy the Fake Out and paralysis support provided by Mega Raichu Y while keeping problem Pokemon like Sinistcha and Basculegion-M in check. Fairy-type Pokemon such as Sylveon and Whimsicott check the most common Ground-type currently, Garchomp. While not as common anymore, Ice-types such as Mamoswine and Alolan Ninetales will be able to keep Garchomp in check, with the latter being able to handle Mega Swampert if it's running Freeze Dry. Ice-type Pokemon can also keep Grass-type Pokemon in check, while Mega Raichu Y covers the Water-type Pokemon that resist their moves. Farigiraf is able to block priority attacks with Armor Tail to keep Mega Raichu Y safe from being picked off at low HP by Kingambit and Basculegion-M and block Fake Out to allow Mega Raichu Y to keep its momentum going. Farigiraf's Helping Hand can boost Mega Raichu Y to secure big OHKOs such as Chople Berry Kingambit with Focus Blast or +1 Special Defense Mega Staraptor with Zap Cannon. Strong Fire-type options such as Hisuian Arcanine and Incineroar can help Mega Raichu Y deal with the Grass-type Pokemon that it would otherwise struggle with such as Sinistcha, Whimsicott, and non-Mega Venusaur. Synergies: Staraptor and Aerodactyl can function without having to Mega Evolve, being immune to Ground and providing the ever-important Tailwind support. Both have a positive matchup into Garchomp, as the former can Intimidate and the latter often runs Ice Fang or Wide Guard. Mega Raichu Y also complements them both in their more challenging matchups, as it can threaten Mega Charizard Y for Staraptor and Mega Blastoise for Aerodactyl. Mega Floette has also seen success alongside Mega Raichu Y, with Raichu being able to support without Mega Evolving with Fake Out and Mega Floette being a solid option into matchups Mega Raichu Y doesn't do well in such as Mega Swampert versions of rain or teams where Garchomp is the focal point.

Mega Staraptor uses its high Attack, solid Speed tier, and offensive typing to threaten metagame staples such as Kingambit, Incineroar, and Sneasler. With Contrary and Close Combat, it can make itself difficult to remove after multiple boosts to its defenses. It can even support its team with Tailwind and Intimidate prior to Mega Evolving. Contrary and Close Combat: Contrary punishes Incineroar's Intimidate, and combining Contrary with Close Combat allows Mega Staraptor to threaten Incineroar even more while boosting its defenses. Roost versus Tailwind: Roost makes Mega Staraptor even more difficult to remove after a boost to its defenses and helps it take attacks like Electro Shot from Archaludon more effectively. Roost can be used on any team, even if it lacks speed control, and Tailwind is less necessary on teams with another Pokemon like Whimsicott to set Tailwind. Mega Evolving Staraptor: Delaying Mega Evolution can preserve Intimidate to weaken physical attackers like Garchomp and Basculegion-M. It can also preserve Staraptor's Normal typing, keeping it immune to Last Respects from Basculegion-M and Rage Fist from Annihilape. This allows Staraptor to switch into a high-Base Power attack, saving a teammate while weakening Basculegion-M with Intimidate. It can use Protect to scout what a Choice Scarf Basculegion-M locks itself into and delay Mega Evolution if Basculegion-M uses Last Respects. Other Options Dual Wingbeat: Dual Wingbeat can be used over Brave Bird to OHKO Sneasler and Whimsicott through a Focus Sash. Mega Staraptor loses its ability to OHKO Basculegion-M with Brave Bird at +1 Attack if it runs Dual Wingbeat. SP Spreads 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly or Adamant: A Jolly nature will ensure Mega Staraptor outspeeds metagame staples like Garchomp, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Floette while granting a Speed tie with other Mega Staraptor. An Adamant nature can be used in combination with Tickle or Charm from Whimsicott, allowing Mega Staraptor's Close Combat to OHKO bulkier variants of Garchomp or Archaludon with one or more Defense boosts. 32 HP / 9 SpD / 25 Spe with Adamant: The Special Defense and HP investment allow Mega Staraptor to always survive Electro Shot from Archaludon at +1 Special Defense. The Speed investment allows it to outrun Modest Mega Floette. An Adamant nature allows it to OHKO Basculegion-M at +1 Attack with Brave Bird. Teambuilding Fairy-type Weaknesses: Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten to OHKO the less bulky Mega Staraptor set with Moonblast or Hyper Beam, respectively, even at +1 Special Defense. These Pokemon are also not good targets for Close Combat, making it hard for the bulkier set to boost its defense before being hit by a strong Fairy-type move. Other Weaknesses: Gholdengo shrugs off both of Mega Staraptor's STAB attacks and can set up Nasty Plot to try getting an OHKO with Make It Rain or Shadow Ball before Mega Staraptor can use Close Combat or Roost. Mega Raichu Y outspeeds and threatens an OHKO with Zap Cannon, and even if Zap Cannon does not OHKO, the paralysis will make it easier for its teammates to finish Mega Staraptor off. Mega Froslass threatens heavy damage or an OHKO that cannot be redirected with Blizzard, is immune to Close Combat, and boosts its Defense with Snow Warning to survive Brave Bird. Soft Counters: Mega Mawile and Mega Metagross threaten an OHKO with Play Rough or Psychic Fangs, respectively. Mega Mawile in particular is often on Trick Room teams to use Mega Staraptor's Speed against it and can have Hyper Cutter before Mega Evolving to ignore Intimidate. The Mega Metagross matchup is playable with support like Charm from Whimsicott, and Rage Powder and Trick Room reversal from Sinistcha help versus Mega Mawile, but these matchups are still threatening. Perish Trap: Mega Gengar's Perish Song in combination with its Shadow Tag ability can deal with Mega Staraptor before it can ramp up its stat boosts. Mega Gengar's teammates like Incineroar and Maushold can use Fake Out to prevent Whimsicott from boosting Mega Staraptor, or Maushold can redirect Charm with Follow Me. Vivillon can shut down Mega Staraptor with Sleep Powder and save Mega Gengar with Rage Powder. This strategy ignores Mega Staraptor's ability to increase its bulk and can counter a slower setup playstyle. Support Partners: Whimsicott has moves like Charm and Fake Tears to let Mega Staraptor flip its matchups against Mega Floette and Sylveon by making it strong enough to OHKO bulkier variants or making it bulky enough to survive their hits if Close Combat cannot do so. Its Tailwind increases the chance Mega Staraptor will get to use Close Combat to increase its bulk before a foe attacks. Sinistcha increases longevity and offsets Brave Bird recoil with Hospitality and Life Dew and redirects threatening attacks like Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon and Archaludon's Electro Shot. Mega Staraptor handles Incineroar and Kingambit in return with Close Combat. Grimmsnarl makes Mega Staraptor even harder to KO with Reflect and Light Screen, allowing Mega Staraptor to always survive Archaludon's Electro Shot with Light Screen up. It can also quickly boost Mega Staraptor's Attack with Parting Shot. The bulky spread works best with these partners that can boost Mega Staraptor's Attack. Offensive Partners: Garchomp can freely use Earthquake next to Mega Staraptor, hitting threats like Gholdengo and Mega Raichu Y. Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed and OHKO Mega Raichu Y with Wave Crash or 150-Base Power Last Respects and Gholdengo, Mega Froslass, or Mega Metagross with 100-Base Power Last Respects. Gholdengo handles Fairy-types with Make It Rain, ignores Perish Song, and threatens to OHKO Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball.Mega Staraptor handles Incineroar and Kingambit for Gholdengo and Basculegion-M. Alternative Mega Evolutions: Fire-types like Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y have a better matchup against Fairy-types, Steel-types, and Mega Froslass. Mega Delphox in particular is strong against Mega Gengar. Mega Staraptor, in turn, is a better choice against Rock-types like Mega Tyranitar and Hisuian Arcanine and in the rain matchup. Mega Raichu Y can be a stronger choice against opposing Mega Staraptor to avoid possible Speed ties. It can also be brought to a battle alongside Mega Staraptor to use Lightning Rod to save Mega Staraptor from opposing Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon. Mega Staraptor, in turn, is a better choice against Mega Raichu Y's counters: Garchomp and Sinistcha.

Mega Swampert gives rain teams a clear choice of Mega Evolution, using its newly granted access to Wave Crash to hit incredibly hard. It is able to OHKO most Pokemon in Regulation M-B that do not resist Wave Crash in rain, albeit at the cost of a large portion of its own HP. It boasts a strong matchup against Regulation M-B staples such as Incineroar, Mega Metagross, and Sneasler. Swift Swim: Swift Swim allows Mega Swampert to outrun every unboosted Pokemon in the tier when rain is active. This means it outspeeds the likes of Garchomp and Mega Raichu Y, two Pokemon that would otherwise greatly burden its partners. Mega Swampert can OHKO them before Garchomp threatens partner Archaludon with Earthquake or Mega Raichu Y threatens Archaludon and Pelipper with Focus Blast and Zap Cannon, respectively. Ice Punch: Ice Punch allows Mega Swampert to threaten the Grass-types that OHKO it, such as Sinistcha, as well as Garchomp, which would otherwise deal a large amount of damage to Mega Swampert through the combination of Wave Crash recoil and Rough Skin contact damage. Notably, it is able to OHKO Whimsicott after Fake Out breaks its Focus Sash, preventing it from setting Tailwind and allowing Mega Swampert to maintain its Speed advantage in rain. It also allows Mega Swampert to hit the occasional Mega Dragonite for heavy damage. Ground-type moves: While some Mega Swampert opt to run only Earthquake, others run High Horsepower to hit Steel-types such as Kingambit without threatening their partner. High Horsepower can be run instead of Earthquake, replacing it as the only Ground-type move, or instead of Ice Punch, forgoing coverage. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Swampert heavily relies on rain to boost its damage output and Speed. Without it, Mega Swampert can struggle to survive specific attacks such as Solar Beam from Mega Charizard Y or secure certain OHKOs. As such, one of its most problematic foes is Mega Charizard Y. If Mega Charizard Y catches Mega Swampert in sun, it can outspeed and OHKO it with Solar Beam, while Mega Swampert cannot OHKO bulky Mega Charizard Y in sun even after surviving Solar Beam. Grass-type threats: Sinistcha can also be a problem, as Mega Swampert struggles to even 2HKO physically bulky Sinistcha with Ice Punch, while Sinistcha can threaten massive damage to Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and is immune to Fake Out and Rage Powder. Venusaur is also able to survive Ice Punch and retaliate with Giga Drain or another Grass-type move. Basculegion-M: Basculegion-M can take advantage of Mega Swampert's preferred weather and threaten an OHKO with rain-boosted Wave Crash while avoiding an OHKO from High Horsepower or Earthquake. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Swampert synergizes well with Archaludon, as Mega Swampert is able to outspeed and OHKO Archaludon's biggest counters in Garchomp, Mega Raichu Y, and Sneasler, while Archaludon resists the Grass-type moves that threaten Mega Swampert. Archaludon can also take Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and retaliate with Electro Shot in rain while bolstering its Defense with Stamina. However, both Pokemon heavily rely on the weather being in their favor to successfully win these matchups. Drizzle Pokemon: Mega Swampert is run exclusively on teams featuring either Pelipper or Politoed, as it is simply not worth using unless it is on a rain-focused team. It is usually run with Pelipper, as Pelipper can threaten the Grass-types that threaten Mega Swampert with Hurricane while being immune to Mega Swampert's Earthquake. Dual screens setters: Mega Swampert is often paired with Grimmsnarl or Sableye, as their Light Screen and Reflect help Archaludon and Mega Swampert stay on the field. Using Rain Dance with Sableye guarantees that rain will be active that turn, as Sableye moves after Mega Charizard YMega Evolves or switches in and sets sun. Redirection: Sinistcha helps Mega Swampert's common partner Archaludon with its Ground-type resistance and ability to set Trick Room, allowing Archaludon to move before threats such as Garchomp. On top of that, Sinistcha can quickly dispatch opposing Mega Swampert, a matchup that can be volatile for Mega Swampert and partner Archaludon. It is also able to redirect and resist Wave Crash from Basculegion-M.

Toxapex finds itself serving a unique role within the Regulation M-B metagame as a supportive wall thanks to its valuable Water / Poison dual typing and sky-high defensive stats. These allow it to sit in front of and greatly limit offensive threats such as Mega Charizard Y, Garchomp, and Sylveon. Infestation: Infestation enables Toxapex to provide some level of offensive pressure along with trapping foes on the field, messing up attempts to reposition. Wide Guard: Wide Guard can protect Toxapex and teammates like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit from spread moves such as Rock Slide and Earthquake. Toxic: Toxic forces timers onto foes such as Milotic and Mega Staraptor, preventing them from being able to setup and win games safely. Infestation, Toxic, and Baneful Bunker Synergy: This trio of moves synergizes well with each other and turns Toxapex into an active threat, as the combination of Infestation and poison does immense amounts of damage over time, softening up foes for partners to KO them. Regenerator: Regenerator helps keep Toxapex healthy throughout a match to let it maintain pressure with trapping and spreading poison. SP Spreads 32 HP / 16 Def / 18 SpD with Bold: This spread allows Toxapex to take Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M's 200-Base Power Last Respects at full HP in addition to Mega Delphox's Psychic. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Toxapex can be greatly annoyed by Steel- and Poison-types, as their immunity to Toxic prevents them from being worn down quickly and leaves Toxapex with only Infestation to whittle away at them. Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Venusaur can prove especially problematic for Toxapex because they can also threaten it with powerful attacks like Electro Shot, Psychic Fangs, and Earth Power. Psychic- and Ground-types such as Mega Delphox, Farigiraf, and Mega Swampert, while not immune to Toxic, can still scare Toxapex through their STAB moves. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y greatly appreciates Toxapex's Wide Guard blocking Rock Slide from Garchomp and Aerodactyl, and in return, it can melt through Steel-types such as Kingambit and Gholdengo. Kingambit and Incineroar can prey on the Psychic-types that break Toxapex like Mega Delphox and Farigiraf, and they also can deal with Ghost-types such as Mega Gengar and Sinistcha, which can escape Infestation's Bound effect. In return, Toxapex can come in against Fighting-types that handle them such as Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Additionally, Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot complement Toxapex by making it much more troublesome to remove. This combination is particularly useful for making physical attackers, such as Garchomp, useless pairing well with Toxapex's Infestation to prevent them from removing the stat drops by switching. Garchomp removes Poison-types such as Mega Gengar and opposing Toxapex while also helping it handle threats such as Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y. Toxapex for its part can use Wide Guard to prevent Sinistcha and Mega Froslass from reliably threatening Garchomp with Matcha Gotcha and Blizzard. Wide Guard also allows Garchomp to use Earthquake without worrying about it hurting Toxapex. Venusaur can pair well with Toxapex by scaring away Ground- and Water-types that cause Toxapex problems such as Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M with its Grass-type STAB moves. Meanwhile, Toxapex protects Venusaur from Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Mega Froslass's Blizzard with Wide Guard. Yawn from Sylveon in tandem with Toxapex's Infestation is great at shutting down foes completely. Sylveon also synergizes particularly well with Toxapex, threatening Garchomp with Hyper Voice.

Garchomp utilizes its high Attack and good Speed to outspeed and greatly weaken foes with powerful spread damage. Using both Stomping Tantrum and Earthquake allows Garchomp to switch between dealing single-target and spread damage. Earthquake, however, is used most effectively when Garchomp's partner is able to use Protect or is immune to Ground-type attacks. Rock Slide is most commonly used by Choice Band Garchomp to threaten Flying-types like Talonflame and Pelipper. It is used as an alternative spread damage attack that doesn't affect Garchomp's partner and is unhindered by Grassy Terrain set by a partner Rillaboom. Life Orb boosts Garchomp's damage, allowing it to threaten an OHKO onto +1 Defense Sneasler with Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake and Dragonite with Dragon Claw. Clear Amulet is used to block Intimidate and Parting Shot from Incineroar. Choice Band provides a greater damage increase than Life Orb, allowing it to threaten an OHKO onto Gholdengo with Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake at the cost of being unable to switch between attacks. The item choice greatly affects Garchomp. Life Orb and Choice Band sets are subject to having its Attack dropped by Incineroar cycling Intimidate and Parting Shot, while the damage from Clear Amulet sets is less. Tera Steel inverts Garchomp's weaknesses to Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type attacks such as Moonblast from Clefable, Outrage from Dragonite, and Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales; additionally, it allows Garchomp to resist Choice Specs-boosted Tera Steel Make It Rain from Gholdengo. Tera Ground increases the damage of Stomping Tantrum and Earthquake, allowing Garchomp to OHKO Gholdengo. Tera Fire provides similar resistances as Tera Steel while not granting a weakness to Fighting-type attacks, and it provides an immunity to burn.

Teambuilding Garchomp fits well onto a variety of teams. It isn't capable of surviving multiple strong attacks, so it relies on partners that allow it to attack without receiving a lot of damage in return. Priority Tailwind setters like Talonflame and Whimsicott are great partners, and they both provide additional Taunt support to disrupt Trick Room setters like Porygon2. Fake Out users like Incineroar disrupt foes for Garchomp. Incineroar additionally provides damage reduction via Intimidate and Parting Shot. Garchomp also works well on balance teams featuring Porygon2, as Garchomp threatens Gholdengo and Incineroar, both of which Porygon2 and its common partners struggle to damage. Garchomp additionally performs well on beatdown teams featuring Dragonite, as Garchomp can freely attack with Earthquake without damaging it. Amoonguss and Vivillon provide redirection and sleep support; Amoonguss is bulkier and has a more consistent way of putting foes to sleep, while Vivillon is faster and is immune to Garchomp's Earthquake. Garchomp pairs well with Porygon2; Porygon2 setting Trick Room can allow Garchomp to attack before threats like Dragapult. Porygon2 additionally deals significant damage to Grass- and Flying-types with Ice Beam and can comfortably survive Earthquake while regaining the lost HP with Recover. Dragonite also synergizes well with Garchomp. Dragonite can deal strong damage with Extreme Speed, allowing Garchomp to secure KOs with Earthquake and removes Grass-types like Rillaboom, which Garchomp struggles to KO, with Tera Blast Flying. Garchomp is threatened by Dragon-, Fairy-, and Ice-type attacks like Dragon Darts and Outrage from Dragapult, Moonblast from Clefable, and Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales. All of these attacks can be switched into by Steel-type partners such as Gholdengo and Kingambit. Garchomp also struggles to damage Flying-types like Pelipper, especially when it isn't using Rock Slide, so a partner like Alolan Ninetales easily threatens Flying-types with Blizzard and Freeze-Dry. Strategy Comments As a glass cannon, Garchomp's task is to deal as much damage as possible uninterrupted. Garchomp performs best when it outspeeds its foes and when it is supported by redirection, allowing Garchomp to attack freely. Garchomp excels at being an early-game sweeper as well as a late-game cleaner. Garchomp primarily attacks using Earthquake to damage both foes. It uses Stomping Tantrum when Garchomp's partner is vulnerable to the damage from Earthquake or when Grassy Terrain is active. Dragon Claw and Rock Slide are used to damage foes that resist Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum. Dragapult outspeeds and threatens Garchomp. To beat Dragapult, Garchomp needs Tailwind or Trick Room support, allowing it to threaten Dragapult with Dragon Claw before it attacks. A partner Kingambit can also survive an attack from Dragapult and threaten it in return with Kowtow Cleave or before Dragapult attacks with Sucker Punch. Rillaboom is also troublesome for Garchomp, as Grassy Terrain weakens the damage of Earthquake. Garchomp is very reliant on partners like Talonflame and Dragonite to remove Rillaboom, as it struggles to deal threatening spread damage when Grassy Terrain is active.

Kingambit is easily able to steamroll through teams, having a great typing both offensively and defensively and easily defeating metagame staples like Gholdengo as well as decimating foes thanks to Swords Dance. Swords Dance bolsters Kingambit's Attack such that it can pick up OHKOs on bulky Pokemon such as Rillaboom, Ursaluna-B, and Amoonguss using Kowtow Cleave, with the latter two requiring Tera Dark. Sucker Punch compensates for Kingambit's low Speed while also immediately either forcing out or pinning Choice item attackers and Assault Vest users. On top of that, Sucker Punch can cause mind games, with Kingambit potentially just using Kowtow Cleave while forcing a switch with the threat of Sucker Punch. Low Kick can defeat Tyranitar and opposing Kingambit as well as Incineroar. Iron Head can be used as coverage for Dark-resistant Pokemon like Primarina and Sneasler, but it's generally harder to pilot and use. Black Glasses is used to boost the main two moves on Kingambit, Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. It allows +2 Kowtow Cleave to OHKO Rillaboom outright and Archaludon with Tera Dark as well as letting Kingambit pick off Volcarona with a +2 Sucker Punch. Safety Goggles stops Sucker Punch from getting redirected and negated by Rage Powder, which can be a huge issue for Kingambit. Safety Goggles can also deny Spore, allowing Kingambit to use Amoonguss to set up. Safety Goggles can miss key OHKOs on the Pokemon shown in the aforementioned calculations. Tera Dark boosts Kingambit's damage further, allowing for OHKOs on Maushold and Gholdengo with Sucker Punch, as well as removing Kingambit's Fire weakness and 4x Fighting weakness, proving to be useful against threats like Incineroar, which Kingambit otherwise struggles to get rid of, and certain Fighting-type coverage and Pokemon like opposing Kingambit's Low Kick and Annihilape, which otherwise OHKO Kingambit. Kingambit is really difficult to stop after a Swords Dance boost and Terastallizing, OHKOing Ursaluna with Kowtow Cleave. This set struggles with four-moveslot syndrome, as having to pick between the flexibility of Swords Dance and a coverage move is difficult. Another issue that this set has is that it can be really difficult to take Dark-resistant Pokemon down, such as Incineroar. For this, setting up in front of another Pokemon or removing the Dark-resistant Pokemon can help Kingambit thrive.

Teambuilding Coverage for Fighting-, Fairy-, and Dark-types such as Primarina, Incineroar, and Sneasler is almost necessary when teambuilding with Kingambit. Both sets enjoy having redirection on their side, including the likes of Clefable, Electabuzz, and Amoonguss, which can easily take in Fighting-type attacks from threats like Annihilape and Sneasler. Swords Dance Kingambit can take advantage of redirection to a greater extent, since this can open windows for setup opportunities. Rillaboom is a really good partner for Kingambit, providing setup opportunities with Fake Out and threatening Ground-types such as the Ursaluna formes. Dark-resistant Pokemon like Incineroar and even opposing Kingambit can be covered by Primarina, which also has great defensive synergy with Kingambit. Sneasler also works at removing Dark-types while also removing Fairy-types and providing another source of Fake Out support for Kingambit. Kingambit, thanks to its typing, is extremely weak to Fighting-types, including Annihilape, Sneasler, and Flamigo, which prove to be an issue. The aforementioned Amoonguss and Clefable can take in these Fighting-type attacks. Primarina, as mentioned before, has great defensive synergy with Kingambit, taking Fighting- and Fire-type attacks with ease, while Kingambit can cover for it against Grass- and Poison-type attacks. Strategy Comments Kingambit's main role is either a setup sweeper with Swords Dance or a defensive pivot piece with Assault Vest. Swords Dance Kingambit's main goal is to set up and stay healthy; redirection and Fake Out support are usually necessary in achieving this. With Tera Dark and at +2, it's very easy for Kingambit to pick up momentum quickly and blitz through careless players. Don't be greedy with using Swords Dances, as it's easy for Kingambit to be OHKOed or brought to low health with careful positioning around Sucker Punch, especially in a format with Fighting-type coverage everywhere. Kingambit succeeds as a setup sweeper thanks to its typing, bulk, and on Assault Vest sets, coverage. Its typing has many resistances to top types like Dragon, making Kingambit an amazing counter to Dragapult and Hydreigon. Kingambit's bulk, especially when it's paired with Assault Vest, is really good, allowing Kingambit to withstand hits and potentially turn the tables in a losing late-game position. Dark-resistant Pokemon are a huge issue for Kingambit, easily taking Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch even if they're boosted. These Pokemon can be taken care of by partners such as Primarina and Sneasler. Fighting-types, including the likes of Annihilape, can be a massive issue, easily using Kingambit to set up. Sneasler in particular can be a problem, only taking notable damage from Iron Head. Fighting-type coverage moves are also rather prevalent in the metagame, with Pokemon like Low Kick Tyranitar and Body Press Archaludon being common. For this, Ghost-type switch-ins like Dragapult or redirection can be helpful in deterring Fighting-type attacks. Additionally, opposing Sneasler can be picked off by Dragapult. Offensive Fairy-types such as Primarina can scare Kingambit away from Terastallizing into a Dark-type, as Moonblast would otherwise easily chunk Kingambit. Sneasler can easily deal with Fairy-types by hitting them hard with Dire Claw.

Incineroar excels as a support Pokemon and pivot thanks to its vast supportive movepool, Intimidate, and great typing, providing Incineroar with resistances to Gholdengo’s, Rillaboom’s, and Kingambit’s STAB moves. Incineroar can utilize Taunt over Flare Blitz to shut down support Pokemon like Amoonguss and Trick Room from Porygon2. Incineroar can also use Will-O-Wisp over Flare Blitz to weaken physical attackers like Garchomp and especially Kingambit, which punishes Intimidate. Safety Goggles is preferred, so Incineroar can reliably check and ignore Amoonguss. Sitrus Berry’s burst healing helps Incineroar avoid 2HKOs from attacks like Choice Specs Gholdengo’s Make it Rain and Pelipper’s Weather Ball after Terastallization. Tera Ghost is preferred to grant Incineroar an immunity to Sneasler’s Close Combat and Dragonite’s Extreme Speed as well as a crucial immunity to Fake Out from opposing Incineroar and Rillaboom. Tera Grass can be used instead to grant Incineroar resistances to Water- and Ground-type moves such as Basculegion’s Wave Crash and Garchomp’s Stomping Tantrum. Tera Grass also provides an immunity to Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss if Safety Goggles have been removed with Knock Off or Incineroar is using Sitrus Berry. The defensive EVs allow Incineroar to survive Garchomp’s Life Orb-boosted Stomping Tantrum and, after using Tera Ghost, Gholdengo’s Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball and Choice Band Basculegion’s 100-Base Power Last Respects after Intimidate.

Teambuilding Amoonguss works exceptionally well with Incineroar, protecting it from Water- and Fighting-type attacks such as Basculegion’s Wave Crash and Annihilape’s Drain Punch. Amoonguss also provides Incineroar with much appreciated healing. In return, Incineroar can handle Gholdengo and switch into Fire-types like Talonflame and Volcarona as well as removing opposing Safety Goggles with Knock Off. Incineroar also works well with Gholdengo, providing Intimidate and Fake Out support to help it set up safely. Gholdengo also takes advantage of Incineroar’s ability to do great damage to Kingambit, considering Gholdengo can blow up Clefable and Sneasler that may attempt to protect Kingambit. Porygon2 and Ursaluna can set up Trick Room and Substitute more easily thanks to Incineroar’s support. Ursaluna can then blow up Pokemon Incineroar struggles to damage like Archaludon and opposing Incineroar. Incineroar can struggle to do its job against Pokemon that threaten it such as Pelipper, the Ursaluna formes, and Annihilape. Bulky support Incineroar can also feel passive at times because of its lackluster damage output, especially when it can’t use Parting Shot because of redirection or Taunt. Therefore, offensive Pokemon like Gholdengo and Ursaluna that can take on these threats and make up for Incineroar’s poor damage output are greatly appreciated. Strategy Comments Incineroar is an effective support Pokemon and pivot thanks to Fake Out, Intimidate, and its pivoting moves. This makes Incineroar strongest when it can switch in and slow down threats like Sneasler and Rillaboom. When using Taunt or Will-O-Wisp, Incineroar can shut down opposing wincons like Porygon2’s Trick Room and Kingambit. Rage Powder from Amoonguss makes it easier for Incineroar to pivot in and out. Incineroar is strong throughout the entire game; it's usually preserved throughout the game, as even switching it in is impactful, and a late-game Fake Out can be crucial regardless of how injured Incineroar is. Incineroar is notably strongest as a lead where it can threaten Fake Out and weaken opposing threats without risking any damage. Against Annihilape and Kingambit however, Incineroar likes to be paired with pieces that force them out before coming in, such as Gholdengo and Ursaluna. Assault Vest Incineroar can afford to stay in and do invaluable damage as an offensive piece occasionally, though it notably has to be a lot more careful against Amoonguss. Incineroar’s biggest weaknesses are Annihilape and Kingambit, as they take advantage of Intimidate and can prove to be dangerous wincons with support. Pelipper and Ursaluna-B also prove troublesome, as they are powerful attackers unaffected by Intimidate. Incineroar relies on teammates such as the aforementioned Gholdengo and Ursaluna to handle these threats along with Fake Out support. When Incineroar pivots in, it can also lead to a loss of momentum against setup Pokemon that can’t be flinched with Fake Out, such as Bulk Up Annihilape, Nasty Plot Gholdengo, and Substitute Ursaluna, so it must be careful when pivoting. Bulky support Incineroar’s damage output can often feel underwhelming, especially against opposing Incineroar. Assault Vest Incineroar has a tougher time providing support, notably having more trouble getting setup sweepers into position, since it lacks Parting Shot. This can make the mirror matchup tougher, as opposing Incineroar can position their threatening allies better.

Whimsicott is a staple on hyper offense teams due to its ability to set Tailwind with its Prankster ability. Whimsicott also provides valuable support to its team through the use of Encore to disrupt opposing strategies or Helping Hand and Sunny Day to boost its partner's damage output. Encore is generally preferred to be able to pin opposing Pokemon into positions where they cannot use Protect, dissuade setup, and lock opposing Pokemon into moves such as Fake Out or Tailwind. Helping Hand is the preferred last move on Whimsicott for most teams because it provides a damage boost to any of Whimsicott's partners. Sunny Day is used on certain hyper offense teams to boost Hisuian Typhlosion's Eruption and provide weather control against Pelipper. Protect is almost always used on Focus Sash sets to block Fake Out without the need to Terastallize into a Ghost-type. Beat Up is specifically used with Annihilape to boost its Rage Fist; this, in conjunction with Tailwind, makes it into a threat as quickly as possible. Covert Cloak is generally preferred on Whimsicott to block the effects of Fake Out, allowing Whimsicott to get Tailwind off without having to run Protect. However, Focus Sash is sometimes used on teams that want Whimsicott's support on the field for longer. Focus Sash also allows Whimsicott to set Tailwind in front of Talonflame, which would otherwise KO Whimsicott before it can set Tailwind with Brave Bird in conjunction with Gale Wings. Tera Water can be used to give Covert Cloak Whimsicott an extra turn on the field against common Pokemon such as Incineroar, Hisuian Typhlosion, and Gholdengo, though it must watch out for Rillaboom's now supereffective priority Grassy Glide. Tera Ghost gives Whimsicott an immunity to common priority moves, namely Fake Out and Extreme Speed and is usually seen on Focus Sash sets, as they are susceptible to Fake Out. Tera Fire offers similar defensive benefits to Tera Water while still resisting Rillaboom's Grassy Glide after Terastallization. However, Tera Fire makes Whimsicott weak to common moves such a as Primarina's Liquid Voice Hyper Voice and Pelipper's Weather Ball under rain. Tera Dark is a niche option on Focus Sash sets that gives Whimsicott an immunity to opposing Prankster moves from the likes of Murkrow and opposing Whimsicott. The first spread for Covert Cloak Whimsicott maximizes HP investment over damage output to live attacks that would otherwise prevent it from setting Tailwind. Focus Sash sets, on the other hand, invest more into Special Attack.

Teambuilding Whimsicott generally works well on hyper offensive teams that appreciate its ability to provide speed control and shut down opposing setup threats with Encore. Pokemon that have middling or high Speed tiers and strong offenses pair especially well with Whimsicott. Whimsicott can also work well on sun-centric teams, utilizing its ability to overwrite Pelipper's Drizzle with Sunny Day to maintain speed and weather control. Whimsicott pairs especially well with strong special attackers, namely Hisuian Typhlosion, Glimmora, Power Herb Archaludon, Gholdengo, and Garchomp. Their middling Speed tiers benefit greatly from Tailwind, and Hisuian Typhlosion in particular also appreciates Whimsicott's ability to set sun, boosting its Eruption further while mitigating its Water weakness. Annihilape can be used on some teams that want to employ Beat Up strategies, which can also be effective. Whimsicott can struggle into teams that can handle its partner's offensive onslaught or mitigate Whimsicott's Tailwind Speed advantage. However, by changing up Whimsicott's partner, it can break through some defensive cores that may stop one pairing but not the other. For example, while Incineroar may be able to beat Whimsicott and Hisuian Typhlosion, it loses to Meteor Beam Glimmora. Since Whimsicott generally pairs with strong, fast offensive threats, its playstyle is very vunerable to Trick Room, especially teams that have Psychic Terrain, which blocks Whimsicott's Prankster Encore. Due to this, Whimsicott generally likes to pair with Incineroar to shut down Trick Room teams while also allowing Whimsicott's frailer partners to pivot in safely. Strategy Comments Whimsicott exists as a support Pokemon, providing speed control through Prankster Tailwind and amplifying its partner's damage output through Helping Hand or Sunny Day. Whimsicott is almost always a lead Pokemon, with a hard-hitting partner that takes advantage of its Tailwind support. It almost always wants to be clicking Tailwind to gain the Speed advantage immediately, unless it is facing a Trick Room team that can turn that advantage on its head. Against bulkier cores that may not have speed control or care about moving first, Whimsicott may choose to use Helping Hand or Sunny Day to try to break through those cores with its partner's sheer power. Whimsicott is mainly weak to strong priority that can take it out before it can set Tailwind, mainly Tera Normal Extreme Speed from Dragonite and Brave Bird from Talonflame. Pokemon that can stomach many hits and slow down the level of offense coming from Whimsicott's side can also be a problem, since Whimsicott is so frail that it can usually only afford to set Tailwind or Sunny Day once. By choosing certain partners for Whimsicott, this matchup problem can be turned on its head. Pokemon such as Glimmora can beat common counters to Whimsicott, including Talonflame, Dragonite, and Incineroar. Pokemon that block priority moves can also support Whimsicott, such as Indeedee with Psychic Terrain and Farigiraf with Armor Tail.

Pelipper functions as a weather setter thanks to Drizzle, enabling powerhouses like Archaludon and Basculegion-M to dish out enormous damage as well as providing support in the form of speed control or Wide Guard. Its Flying- and Water-type STAB options combined with its decent Speed help Pelipper to fill in the role of an attacker as well, taking advantage of its own rain to buff its offensive options. Weather Ball is a flexible attack that gains a STAB boost in rain while providing decent coverage under opposing weather like sun. Tailwind provides speed control for the team, whereas Wide Guard protects the team from Gholdengo's Make it Rain, Ursaluna-B's Hyper Voice, Expanding Force in Psychic Terrain, and Garchomp's Earthquake. Focus Sash allows Pelipper to survive an attack due to the set's frailty, increasing its long-term value as a weather setter and allowing it to get an extra attack off. Tera Stellar further boosts its damage, allowing Pelipper to OHKO Amoonguss and Annihilape with Hurricane and Tera Normal Ursaluna-B and Assault Vest Incineroar with rain-boosted Weather Ball. Meanwhile, Tera Ghost provides an immunity to Fake Out, enabling an early Tailwind uninterrupted while keeping Focus Sash intact. A maximized Special Attack stat with a Modest nature secures an OHKO on Incineroar with rain-boosted Weather Ball and on Amoonguss with Tera Stellar Hurricane, while a Timid nature can be opted for faster speed control and securing KOs on weakened Pokemon, and it comes in handy in rain mirror matches.

Teambuilding Pelipper excels in teams capable of taking advantage of Drizzle while also having sufficient defensive options to switch around to regain control of the weather late-game. Archaludon, with its signature move Electro Shot, works exceptionally well in rain, and it provides a defensive backbone to the team thanks to its immense bulk and ability, capable of switching into threats such as Tyranitar's Rock Slide and Maushold's Population Bomb. It quickly becomes an offensive threat once it starts stacking up Electro Shot boosts in rain. Basculegion-M's ability Swift Swim makes it desirable on rain teams both as an early-game powerhouse with its fast rain-boosted Wave Crash and as a late-game sweeper with Last Respects. Its immense Speed and power help it form a well-rounded balanced core with Archaludon and Pelipper, taking on threats such as Garchomp and Gholdengo, while Pelipper threatens the Grass-types that resists Wave Crash like Amoonguss and Rillaboom with Hurricane. Pelipper struggles against opposing weather setters like Tyranitar, which not only tanks Pelipper's STAB moves in sand but also breaks its Focus Sash with sand chip damage and KOs it with Rock Slide. Archaludon takes advantage of Pelipper's rain to fire off Electro Shots as well as completely walling Pelipper's STAB attacks. Amoonguss is an excellent disruptive option, taking advantage of its bulk to survive attacks like Knock Off from Tyranitar and Draco Meteor from Archaludon and put the aforementioned threats to sleep with Spore. Basculegion-M is a great check against Tyranitar as well, outspeeding and OHKOing it with Wave Crash. Strategy Comments As a rain setter, Pelipper is often used to enable Archaludon snowball with Electro Shots while handling threats like Amoonguss with Hurricane. Speed control with Tailwind is desirable due to Archaludon's slow Speed, and it helps tremendously against balance archetypes. Pelipper is often lead with Basculegion-M or Archaludon to immediately take advantage of rain, provided the opposing team lacks a method to change the weather. A more flexible approach would be to lead the weather-reliant Pokemon like Archaludon and prepare Pelipper as a switch-in to swiftly take control of the game with a well-timed weather change. It is pivotal to keep Pelipper intact for late-game weather control, as lack of such could potentially end up severely weakening the board and result in a loss of momentum. Rivaling weather setters like Tyranitar and Alolan Ninetales threaten Pelipper's rain. It's advisable to preserve Pelipper and switch it in to thwart Aurora Veil setups from Alolan Ninetales, while Archaludon or Basculegion-M should take out Tyranitar first. Opposing Archaludon can end up being a powerful threat due to being capable of walling Pelipper while taking advantage of its rain. The ideal option here would be to use Amoonguss to force it to Terastallize into a Grass-type, and then have Pelipper deal a massive amount of damage to it with Hurricane.

Sinistcha is a great support Pokemon providing recovery and redirection for its partners. Sinistcha's Ghost typing makes it immune to Fake Out, so it can't be disrupted from the likes of Incineroar and Rillaboom. Additionally, Sinistcha's Grass typing makes it immune to moves like Spore from Amoonguss. Matcha Gotcha can be used to threaten the Ursaluna formes while restoring Sinistcha's HP. Life Dew can consistently provide more HP for Sinistcha and its partner in front of a threat like Volcarona or Gholdengo. Rage Powder provides redirection support so that a partner like Annihilape can set up more freely. Sitrus Berry helps Sinistcha stay on the field for a long time in conjunction with Matcha Gotcha and Life Dew. Tera Dark helps Sinistcha survive Ghost- and Dark-type attacks like Shadow Ball from Gholdengo, Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit, and Knock Off from Incineroar while making it immune to Prankster Taunt and Encore from Whimsicott. Tera Water helps Sinistcha survive against Fire-type moves like Heat Wave and Flamethrower from Volcarona and Flare Blitz from Incineroar. Tera Water can also help Sinistcha better stomach Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales. The physical bulk on Sinistcha helps it survive a 150-Base Power Rage Fist from Annihilape and Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit, while the special bulk lets it survive Shadow Ball from Gholdengo and Flamethrower from Volcarona.

Teambuilding Setup Pokemon like Annihilape and Trick Room sweepers like Ursaluna appreciate the recovery and redirection Sinistcha provides so that they can feel more safe when setting up or attacking. Dark-types like Kingambit can threaten Ghost-type threats like Gholdengo and Basculegion-M. Sinistcha provides recovery for Ursaluna's burn damage while setting up Trick Room to get Ursaluna to move first. Ursaluna, in return, can counter threats like Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Incineroar with Headlong Rush. Sinistcha can threaten Water-types like Primarina and redirects Fighting-type moves like Drain Punch and Close Combat from Annihilape and Close Combat from Sneasler to further support Ursaluna. Ursaluna can switch into Ghost-type moves like Last Respects from Basculegion-M to prevent any damage dealt to Sinistcha. Annihilape can counter Incineroar with its ability Defiant and STAB Fighting-type moves like Drain Punch and Close Combat, which also threatens Kingambit and Archaludon. The recovery Sinistcha provides helps Annihilape stay on the field longer and use a stronger Rage Fist against threats like Gholdengo. Sinistcha can redirect damage away from Annihilape to help it set up Bulk Up to make it even more threatening for the foes. Archaludon appreciates the recovery brought by Sinistcha to increase its time on the field and potentially build Stamina boosts to further take hits from physical attackers like Dragonite, Annihilape, and Sneasler. Archaludon can threaten Dragonite with Dragon-type STAB moves like Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse. Sinistcha can redirect Fighting- and Ground-type moves away from Archaludon like Close Combat from Sneasler and Earth Power from Ursaluna-B. Archaludon can threaten Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar with Body Press as well as Alolan Ninetales and Whimiscott with Flash Cannon. Pelipper can set up rain for Sinistcha so that it takes less damage from Fire-type moves like Flare Blitz from Incineroar and Hisuian Arcanine, and it also threatens to OHKO Incineroar and Hisuian Arcanine with Weather Ball. Pelipper can use Hurricane to threaten Grass-type Pokemon like Rillaboom, which ignores Rage Powder from Sinistcha, and Annihilape, a foe Sinistcha struggles against. Furthermore, Pelipper can block spread moves like Heat Wave with Wide Guard. In return, Sinistcha can support Pelipper by redirecting Electric-type moves like Thunderbolt from Electabuzz and Kilowattrel. Sinistcha has a poor defensive typing in the current metagame with threats like Charizard, Basculegion-M, and Tyranitar becoming more common. Heat Wave from Charizard is usually paired with sun from Torkoal and is enough to OHKO Sinistcha, Basculeigon-M can threaten Sinistcha with Last Respects, and Knock Off from Tyranitar can threaten Sinistcha while removing the ability to recover its HP with Sitrus Berry. Pelipper can help Sinistcha against Charizard and Tyranitar with rain and Weather Ball. Electro Shot from Archaludon helps Sinistcha against opposing Pelipper and Basculegion-M. Sinistcha is very passive, so an offensive partner like Archaludon or Annihilape can threaten foes while being supported by it. The Ursaluna formes can threaten Steel-types like Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Archaludon, which wall Sinistcha. Strategy Comments Sinistcha is very strong next to an offensive Trick Room partner like Ursaluna, as it can support it with Life Dew and Rage Powder to keep it alive longer. Sinistcha prefers to be brought in the back so that it can switch in and heal its partner with Hospitality. When it's against faster foes like Sneasler, Dragapult, and Archaludon, Sinistcha can focus on setting up Trick Room and supporting its slow partners with Life Dew and Rage Powder. Against slower foes like the Ursaluna formes, Kingambit, and Amoonguss, Sinistcha doesn't have to worry about setting up Trick Room; it can focus on chipping down foes HP with Matcha Gotcha and supporting its partners with Rage Powder and Life Dew. Sinistcha struggles against Incineroar due to its typing, and Matcha Gotcha struggles to absorb any HP from Incineroar. Kingambit can benefit from Sinistcha's Trick Room while also dealing significant damage to it with Kowtow Cleave; Sinistcha also struggles to recover any HP from using Matcha Gotcha against it. Annihilape can help Sinistcha in the matchups against Incineroar and Kingambit with the combination of Defiant and Drain Punch, and it can threaten other Dark-types like Tyranitar. Archaludon with Body Press can also help Sinistcha against Kingambit. Fire-types like Volcarona, Charizard, and Torkoal can threaten to OHKO Sinistcha. Pelipper can help against Fire-types by setting up the rain and attacking with Weather Ball, and Basculeigon-M threatens Fire-types like Charizard as well as Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Annihilape. Opposing Pelipper can threaten to OHKO Sinistcha with Hurricane, while Dragonite's defensive typing makes it difficult for Sinistcha to damage it. Archaludon can take advantage of rain to OHKO Pelipper with Electro Shot while resisting Pelipper's STAB moves, and it can threaten to OKHO Inner Focus Dragonite with Draco Meteor. Gholdengo threatens Sinistcha with Shadow Ball; Ursaluna's Ghost immunity and access to Headlong Rush helps Sinistcha deal with it. These traits also let Ursaluna be a great answer to other Ghost-, Fire-, and Steel-type threats like Dragapult, Hisuian Arcanine, and Kingambit. Sinistcha can heal Ursaluna's burn damage taken from Flame Orb, boosting its longevity on the field to deal with Sinistcha's threats. Alolan Ninetales can ignore Rage Powder with Blizzard and do significant damage to Sinistcha, and it can set up Aurora Veil to reduce the damage Matcha Gotcha can deal to it and its partner.

Basculegion-M uses its high-Base Power STAB attacks like Wave Crash and Last Respects to claim knockouts in the early-game and secure wins in the late-game, respectively, as well as its Swift Swim ability to outspeed nearly the whole unboosted metagame under rain, giving it positive matchups against metagame staples such as Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Volcarona. Last Respects can reach an incredible Base Power of 200, threatening nearly every Pokemon that does not resist Ghost-type attacks with an OHKO. Aqua Jet allows Basculegion-M to pick off a foe at low health while avoiding Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Flip Turn allows it to deal damage and retreat to safety before being attacked. Choice Band maximizes Basculegion-M’s damage, notably improving the chance for Last Respects with two fainted teammates to OHKO Rillaboom. Tera Water maximizes the damage output of Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks, guaranteeing an OHKO against almost any Gholdengo set, and removes its weakness to Dark-type attacks such as Kingambit’s Sucker Punch. Tera Grass allows Basculegion-M to survive any attack from Rillaboom, resist Electro Shot from Archaludon, and ignore Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss. The defensive investment allows Basculegion-M to survive a Grassy Glide from Rillaboom. With the Attack investment, Basculegion-M will always OHKO Incineroar in the rain with Wave Crash even after Intimidate. The Speed investment allows it to always outspeed Primarina. Choice-locked sets are inherently more risky to use, as being locked into the wrong move can lose an endgame. The Swift Swim set is riskier in terms of speed control, as it relies on its team to set up rain. This set has the potential to be faster than the Choice Scarf set, but without rain, its Speed and damage output can be underwhelming. It has the advantage of Choice Band providing a higher damage boost than Adaptability. This set, as well as the Choice Scarf set, are risky to use over the Focus Sash set as they can be knocked out with one hit.

Teambuilding Swift Swim sets only appear on rain teams, as otherwise Basculegion-M would be playing without an ability. The Choice Scarf Adaptability set typically appears on balance teams that benefit heavily from getting a quick OHKO against foes like Incineroar. The Focus Sash set can fit on either balance teams or on rain teams with speed control options, as it appreciates rain boosting the weaker Liquidation. Both the Choice Scarf and Focus Sash Adaptability sets can still benefit heavily from being on a rain team thanks to the Water-type damage amplification, despite not having Swift Swim. Pelipper’s Drizzle ability allows Swift Swim Basculegion-M to outspeed nearly the entire metagame, as well as boosting the damage of its Water-type attacks, while Pelipper itself can pressure opposing Grass-types with Hurricane. Archaludon can cover Basculegion-M’s weakness to Dark-type Pokemon such as Kingambit using Body Press, round out the offensive core of a rain team, and serve as a bulky pivot to be sent out after using Flip Turn, resisting attacks from Rillaboom and Kilowattrel. Incineroar can be used to ensure Rillaboom’s Grassy Glide will never OHKO even if Rillaboom has Miracle Seed and stop opposing Basculegion-M from getting an OHKO with unboosted Last Respects. Amoonguss and Sinistcha can use Rage Powder to redirect attacks that threaten to OHKO Basculegion-M, such as Kingambit’s Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave, while improving the team’s matchup against Trick Room. Additionally, Sinistcha's Hospitality and Life Dew can be used to bring Basculegion-M back to full health to make use of Focus Sash, stay out of range of attacks like Grassy Glide from Rillaboom, and heal recoil damage from Wave Crash. Grass-type Pokemon like Amoonguss and Rillaboom stop Basculegion-M from sweeping through teams with Wave Crash, as Amoonguss can redirect and resist the attack, while Rillaboom is always threatening an OHKO with Wood Hammer. Pelipper can use Hurricane to hit these Pokemon for massive damage, or Basculegion-M outside of rain teams can be paired with Fire-types like Volcarona and Talonflame. Dark-type Pokemon like Incineroar and Kingambit threaten an OHKO against Basculegion-M and prevent it from sweeping with Last Respects, making Close Combat Sneasler a worthwhile partner. A Commander-boosted Dondozo can survive multiple Last Respects and resist any Water-type attacks. Archaludon can threaten Dondozo with Electro Shot, and Pelipper can punish Tera Grass Dondozo with Hurricane. Alternatively, teams can use Incineroar and Rillaboom along with Basculegion-M's Flip Turn to cycle Intimidate and Fake Out, or Multiscale Dragonite to safely remove Dondozo's stat boosts with Haze. Alolan Ninetales pairs well with the Choice Scarf set because it can hit Grass-types with Blizzard and Water-types like Dondozo with Freeze-Dry, while Basculegion-M covers for Alolan Ninetales's weakness to Fire-type Pokemon such as Incineroar. Opposing Archaludon are unlikely to be knocked out even by a maximum power Last Resepcts, so Fighting-type coverage from Annihilape and Sneasler and Ground-type coverage from Ursaluna-B is appreciated. Strategy Comments Basculegion-M functions as a late-game cleaner or early-game wallbreaker with high Speed and damage. The Swift Swim sets need its team to set up rain to activate Swift Swim, or else it can be taken out by a quicker foe. It can secure endgames with high-Base Power Last Respects if its teammates have done enough damage to the opposing team. It can bail out of positions with Flip Turn while its teammates take out the foes that are preventing it from sweeping. In the early-game, it can remove the Ursaluna formes, which can allow a teammate like Archaludon to sweep. Basculegion-M can be used early or late in a battle, but it must be saved for the late-game if maximizing the damage of Last Respects is necessary. It can be used effectively in the early-game by knocking out a Pokemon such as Incineroar, which can allow a teammate like Gholdengo to sweep the opposing team. The Focus Sash set can clinch an endgame using combinations of Liquidation and Last Respects, but the Choice item sets must be more careful to leave foes that can be swept by one move for last. Sun teams can mitigate Basculegion-M’s Speed and offense, particularly for the Swift Swim set. Pokemon that set up sun upon switching in like Torkoal can be countered by keeping Pelipper in the back and switching it in when sun is up to overwrite it. Manual sun setters like Whimsicott must be taken out by a teammate like Incineroar with Flare Blitz or Archaludon with Flash Cannon, as switching in Pelipper will set up rain first, which will be canceled by Whimsicott’s Sunny Day. Alolan Ninetales can change rain to snow, take a hit from Basculegion-M and return damage with Freeze-Dry, and use Disable to nullify a Choice item set or Aurora Veil to mitigate its damage output.
