Basculegion-M can use Flip Turn to reposition until rain is set, and Pelipper can be lead into Alolan Ninetales because it is slower and so will activate Drizzle after Snow Warning, though an Alolan Ninetales in the back can still switch in to cancel rain. Tyranitar can overwrite rain with Sand Stream and can switch into Last Respects while breaking Focus Sash. Pelipper should expect to be faster than Tyranitar, so sand will be set up after rain. Thus, Pelipper is more likely to successfully set rain if it is reserved in the back or if Tyranitar is knocked out by Basculegion-M's teammates.

Focus Sash Sneasler aims to eliminate key threats in the metagame such as Kingambit and Rillaboom with powerful STAB options while also outspeeding most Pokemon on the field. Additionally, it provides a supportive role with options like Fake Out and Coaching. Dire Claw and Close Combat are Sneasler's main STAB options, hitting key metagame threats such as Whimsicott and Tyranitar for huge damage, respectively. Fake Out creates openings for allies such as Gholdengo to set up while also breaking Focus Sash on opposing Sneasler before they can move if they do not tread carefully. Coaching boosts the power of physical attackers such as Baxcalibur while also boosting their Defense, allowing them to take more hits from the likes of Incineroar and Garchomp. Protect, on the other hand, can be run to keep Sneasler's Focus Sash intact against opposing Fake Out users and help stall out Trick Room turns, so Sneasler can continue to be the fastest on the field. Focus Sash helps combat Sneasler's frail stature, letting it survive attacks such as Expanding Force from Indeedee-M and retaliate with Close Combat or Dire Claw. Tera Stellar is preferred on Sneasler to let it achieve OHKOs on Rillaboom and Assault Vest Archaludon with Dire Claw and Close Combat, respectively. Tera Ghost is recommended on sets without Protect to avoid Fake Out from foes such as Incineroar and Rillaboom. Jolly is the most common nature on Focus Sash Sneasler, letting it outspeed and OHKO fast Pokemon such as Maushold and Whimsicott. Adamant Sneasler, on the other hand, is able to get the guaranteed OHKO with Dire Claw on Tera Grass or Fairy Volcarona and Primarina. Although Focus Sash allows for more flexibility, this Sneasler variant struggles heavily against Ghost-types like Gholdengo, notably having little to hit them. Focus Sash Sneasler also falls victim to four-moveslot syndrome, oftentimes warranting a need for both Coaching and Protect.

Teambuilding Focus Sash Sneasler is generally used as a supportive Pokemon, using Fake Out to help allies such as Volcarona set up or to protect partners like Ursaluna to give them opportunities to deal loads of damage. Unburden sweeper Sneasler sets that carry either Grassy Seed or Psychic Seed tend to take a more offensive approach, with enablers of their items being must-haves. Additionally, partners that can properly take advantage of Sneasler's coverage, such as Indeedee-M, can form a strong and solid offensive core with it. Rillaboom is an amazing partner for Sneasler, forming a double Fake Out core that can easily overwhelm common team structures such as Dondozo + Tatsugiri teams while also threatening Ground-types that would otherwise heavily threaten Sneasler, notably the Ursaluna formes. In return, Sneasler threatens Pokemon such as Incineroar and Archaludon, Pokemon that Rillaboom struggles to break through. Kingambit is another great partner for almost any Sneasler set. Kingambit can threaten Gholdengo, one of the top checks to Sneasler, and take out Pokemon naturally faster than Sneasler with Sucker Punch, most importantly Dragapult. Kingambit, due to its low Speed, can also exploit Trick Room, which may be used to nullify Sneasler's presence. In return, Sneasler can use Fake Out and Coaching to support Kingambit. Sneasler is very susceptible to multi-hit moves such as Population Bomb from Maushold and Scale Shot from Dragonite and Baxcalibur. For this, partners such as Alolan Ninetales and Incineroar are recommended to threaten the most common multi-hit move users or, in Incineroar's case, weaken the damage instead. Additionally, Sneasler struggles against Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Annihilape without Throat Chop or Acrobatics; because of this, allies like Incineroar and Pelipper are recommended to scare away Gholdengo and Annihilape, respectively. Strategy Comments Sneasler's objective is to overall be a nuisance to the opposing team with moves such as Dire Claw, which has the chance to apply game-ending status conditions, as well as supporting its team or dealing heavy damage. Because of this, Sneasler thrives in board states where Dire Claw is easy to use and sometimes spam. Unburden sweeper sets that use either Psychic Seed or Grassy Seed need their Terrain setter to be active, so they generally aim to break holes in opposing teams early-game for allies such as Gholdengo to later clean up. Focus Sash and White Herb sets have more versatility and can be brought in the lead slot or saved in the back instead. Generally, it's advised to not bring Sneasler against Trick Room teams, as under the impairment of Trick Room, Sneasler is far more susceptible to getting KOed due to its high Speed. Gholdengo is the largest thorn in the side for Sneasler, as it is immune to both of Sneasler's STAB moves and is only threatened by Throat Chop. Allies like Kingambit and Incineroar can easily take care of Gholdengo with Kowtow Cleave and Knock Off, respectively. Annihilape and Dragonite can be an even bigger struggle if Sneasler doesn't tread carefully, as Annihilape is only threatened by Acrobatics, and Dragonite can use Scale Shot to OHKO Sneasler, even through Focus Sash. Alolan Ninetales threatens both of these Pokemon with Moonblast while also having access to Aurora Veil to allow Sneasler to survive attacks such as Scale Shot from Dragonite.

Due to its respectably high Special Attack and slow Speed stat, Hatterene serves as a formidable sweeper under Trick Room on Psychic-type spam teams due to maximizing damage output with its Psychic-type attacks, most noticeable Expanding Force. It serves as one of the most reliable Trick Room setters due to Magic Bounce, blocking status moves such as Taunt, Spore, and Sleep Powder. Dazzling Gleam serves as a sufficient secondary STAB move that can cover for Dark-types that are immune to Expanding Force. Protect discourages double-ups into Hatterene, as they would let a partner Pokemon set up Trick Room or pivot out for better positioning without letting Hatterene get heavily damaged. However, Hatterene can favor Mystical Fire over Protect as a coverage move that threatens Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Kingambit and Grass-types like Rillaboom, which can override Psychic Terrain. Life Orb enables the flexibility of being able to use Trick Room or Protect while allowing Hatterene to still 2HKO most Pokemon neutral to Expanding Force, assuming Psychic Terrain is set up. Tera Fire provides defensive flexibility against Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Archaludon, which gives it a higher chance of survivability for one turn and allows Hatterene to set up Trick Room in some cases. It also boosts the damage output of Mystical Fire, guaranteeing a 2HKO on Assault Vest Rillaboom and almost always OHKOing maximum HP Gholdengo and Kingambit. Tera Psychic, on the other hand, aims to maximize the damage output of Expanding Force, allowing it to OHKO Garchomp, Ursaluna-B, and Basculegion-M, as well as holding some defensive merits in removing weaknesses to Poison- and Steel-type attacks. The EV spread lets Hatterene survive a Wave Crash from Adaptability Basculegion-M, a Dire Claw from Sneasler, and an Eruption from Timid Choice Specs Hisuian Typhlosion and give it an extremely favorable roll against a Torkoal Eruption. Hatterene at its lowest possible Speed stat can move before Amoonguss under Trick Room.

Teambuilding Hatterene is really only prominently used in Trick Room teams due to its extremely inflexible Speed stat. However, once Trick Room is set up, Hatterene is there to deal as much damage as possible. It may also set up Trick Room, which paves the way for fellow Trick Room sweepers such as Torkoal and Ursaluna to clean up the game. Indeedee-F serves as Hatterene's ideal partner, setting up Psychic Terrain to maximize the power of Expanding Force and make it into a spread move . It also provides redirection, allowing Hatterene to safely set up Trick Room while increasing Hatterene's survivability, and Helping Hand support to further accentuate Hatterene's damage output. Hatterene is heavily threatened by Steel-types such as Kingambit and Gholdengo, which can deal considerable damage to it and comfortably tank its attacks. Ursaluna complements Hatterene as a fellow Trick Room sweeper where its STAB Ground-type attacks such as Earthquake and Headlong Rush can cover for Hatterene’s weaknesses while Hatterene can switch into and threaten the Fighting-types that threaten Ursaluna. Torkoal is another partner that provides offensive support with its Fire-type STAB moves against Steel- and Grass-types such as Rillaboom, which can override Psychic Terrain but is highly threatened by Eruption, deterring switch-ins. Another partner is Gallade, as it provides Wide Guard support, which is valuable against Eruption and Make It Rain from Hisuian Typhlosion and Gholdengo, respectively. Gallade's Fighting-type STAB moves are favorable in covering for Hatterene's Steel weakness, as well as hitting Dark-types such as Kingambit and Incineroar. Strategy Comments As a Trick Room sweeper, Hatterene ideally aims to set Trick Room and deal as much damage as possible. It works best when under Psychic Terrain, as it enables Expanding Force to deal its maximum potential output while protecting Hatterene from priority attacks such as Fake Out, Extreme Speed, and Sucker Punch. As a result of being a more reliable Trick Room setter than others, Hatterene works well early in the game, setting up Trick Room on the first turn ideally while Indeedee-F redirects attacks before sweeping with Expanding Force. It can also choose to be in the back and let Indeedee-F or Gallade set Trick Room, allowing Hatterene to clean up the endgame once Trick Room is set up. Rillaboom is one of the most threatening Pokemon against Hatterene, as not only can it threaten Hatterene with Wood Hammer, but it can also override Psychic Terrain, allowing priority attacks like Fake Out to bypass Trick Room. This also severely cuts Hatterene’s Expanding Force damage, making it more difficult for Hatterene to remove Rillaboom. Ways to mitigate Rillaboom could be to add Torkoal, which can threaten Rillaboom with Eruption. Indeedee-F can set Psychic Terrain after Rillaboom in the first turn; it is also possible to keep Indeedee-F in the back and switch it in after Rillaboom has entered the field.

Assault Vest patches up Archaludon's low Special Defense, and when this is paired with Stamina's Defense boosts and Electro Shot's Special Attack boosts, Archaludon can easily snowball. Central to this snowball strategy is Electro Shot, as it allows Archaludon to simultaneously boost while threatening Water-types such as Basculegion-M and Dondozo. Body Press takes advantage of Stamina boosts, threatening other Assault Vest Pokemon and Dark-types such as Incineroar and Kingambit. Flash Cannon helps Archaludon deal with Fairy-types such as Alolan Ninetales and Whimsicott. Snarl is an option to help mitigate damage from special attackers such as Gholdengo, which may wall Archaludon outside of rain otherwise, and Ursaluna-B, as well as hampering opposing Archaludon should Body Press be ineffective due to Terastallization or redirection. Dragon Pulse is a consistent STAB move, while Draco Meteor without boosts secures OHKOs against other Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Dragonite without Multiscale, which Dragon Pulse misses out on without prior boosts. Tera Grass allows Archaludon to avoid Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss, as well as resisting Ground-type moves from Ursaluna and Garchomp. Tera Bug grants a resistance to both Sneasler's Close Combat and both Ursaluna formes' Ground-type moves while maintaining neutralities to other types such as Ice, which is relevant against Porygon2 and Alolan Ninetales. Tera Fighting grants a resistance to Dark, denying Kingambit its chance to OHKO Archaludon before Stamina comes into play, while also powering up Body Press. The EVs focus on making Archaludon bulky while allowing it to outspeed Modest Pelipper, and the rest is dumped into Special Defense to maximize value from Assault Vest.

Teambuilding Archaludon's Electro Shot doesn't require a turn to charge while in rain, so Pelipper is a staple partner because of its ability Drizzle. Pelipper can help Archaludon deal with Fighting- and Ground-type threats such as Sneasler, Annihilape, Ursaluna, and Ursaluna-B with its STAB moves and provide speed control with Tailwind. Basculeigon-M is a common Swift Swim Pokemon used with Archaludon, mainly due to its synergy with Pelipper. Basculegion-M offers immediate damage to an otherwise slow-paced core of Pelipper and Archaludon, and it can goad Rillaboom into using Grassy Glide into a Stamina Archaludon switching in. Dragonite and Maushold commonly use multi-hit moves like Scale Shot, Population Bomb, and Beat Up. As allies, they can target Archaludon with these moves to instantly gain multiple Defense boosts with Stamina. Dragonite can also provide speed control with Tailwind and pressure targets such as Sneasler and Flamigo, which threaten Archaludon with Close Combat. Sinistcha and Amoonguss can both heal and redirect dangerous Fighting- and Ground-type attacks away from Archaludon. Sinistcha offers immediate healing on a switch in and an additional layer of speed control in Trick Room, while Amoonguss's Spore is generally disruptive, and Pollen Puff heals Archaludon more than Hospitality and Life Dew from Sinistcha can. These two Grass-types also benefit from Pelipper's rain, as it reduces Fire-type damage. Incineroar's Intimdate and Fake Out help with Archaludon's physical weaknesses to Sneasler and Ursaluna, and Knock Off removes items such as Assault Vest and Eviolite, which then allows Archaludon to better combat threats such as Porygon2 and opposing Archaludon. Strategy Comments Assault Vest Archaludon's goal is to gain stat boosts and then sweep with powerful Body Presses or STAB options. Archaludon's superb defensive typing makes it worthwhile to switch in on resisted hits to get a Stamina boost. It is particularly complementary with Pelipper, which resists Fighting and is immune to Ground, while Archaludon resists Pelipper's Electric weakness. When boosted, Archaludon may have problems with Haze users, particularly Haze Dragonite, which often outspeeds bulkier Archaludon. While the common Loaded Dice set does not enjoy using Scale Shot on Stamina Archaludon, it can later remove all of Archaludon's accumulated boosts. Archaludon can hit Dragonite itself with STAB Dragon Pulse or Draco Meteor, as well as the common Tera Fairy Dragonite with Flash Cannon, though for clean KOs without boosts, Multiscale should be broken first. Archaludon can be OHKOed by a strong Close Combat, the most common user of which is Sneasler. Strategies for dealing with Stamina Archaludon in this way involve either targeting around it for fear of giving it too many Defense boosts or chipping Archaludon enough to keep it in range of Close Combat even after a few boosts. Terastallization and utilizing Amoonguss or Sinistcha's redirection and healing are good defensive tools to combat this. Special attackers, particularly Ursaluna-B and Tera Blast Fighting Porygon2, threaten Archaludon's more vulnerable Special Defense while not taking much damage in return. Archaludon's own Snarl can help keep these threats at bay, particularly when combined with Terastallization. Changing the weather on Archaludon preparing an Electro Shot is a good way to reposition around it. Torkoal, Tyranitar, and Alolan Ninetales are the premier opposing weather setters of the format. Athough Archaludon itself can threaten all three with Body Press or an appropriate STAB move, their presence alone helps their partners, such as Charizard and Excadrill, handle Archaludon and other members of its rain core. Jumpluff and Whimsicott stand out as common users of Sunny Day, which prevents Archaludon from firing single-turn Electro Shots and has the added benefit of weakening any Water-types paired with Pelipper and Archaludon such as Basculegion-M. When facing these Pokemon, it is important to preserve Pelipper until opposing weather setters are dealt with. Sturdy Archaludon is more straightforward to use, as it relies less on constant boosting in favor of utilizing one boost to its fullest. Opposing teams will aim to outspeed it, deal chip damage to get around Sturdy, then land a powerful move such as Sneasler's Close Combat or Ursaluna-B's Earth Power to KO it, so Tailwind from Pokemon such as Pelipper or Icy Wind from Alolan Ninetales can help Archaludon outspeed and KO such threats.

Drought turns Mega Charizard Y into one of the most ferocious wallbreakers in the game, as well as effective support against Water-types such as Primarina and Rotom-Wash! Flamethrower versus Weather Ball: Flamethrower is Mega Charizard Y's most reliable Fire-type STAB move. Weather Ball offers a bit more power and gives Mega Charizard Y some extra coverage when the weather is changed, but this isn't always beneficial depending on the team you're facing. Solar Beam: The blistering sun removes Solar Beam's biggest drawback, making it great coverage against common Water-types like Primarina and Rotom-Wash. Just be weary of weather changers like Hippowdon, Tyranitar, and Pelipper, which not only weaken Solar Beam's power but change it back to being a two-turn move! Overheat: Overheat gets boosted to the heavens with the sunlight, with even Fire-resistant foes like Rotom-Wash and Garchomp taking over half their health from it! Just beware that the hit-and-run tactics Overheat encourages are heavily impacted by your opponent's team placing down Stealth Rock. Flame Charge: Flame Charge transforms Mega Charizard Y into an effective late-game cleaner, with the bonus of destroying Focus Sash and Disguise. Air Slash: Air Slash is a good secondary STAB move regardless of the current weather, especially against Mega Venusaur, whose Thick Fat can make it tricky to break through without risking an Overheat. Timid versus Modest: Charizard is common enough where Speed ties can make or break games, but Modest does enhance Mega Charizard Y's wallbreaking power, with Overheat now having a small shot of OHKOing specially defensive Hippowdon. Blaze versus Solar Power: Solar Power actually gives Charizard more power than its Mega Evolution, which can come in handy against opposing Mega Charizard Y teams. However, the damage it takes in the sun is unwelcome when Stealth Rock is in play, making Blaze the safer ability. Sand Stream Partners: Since Mega Charizard Y relies on the warmth of the sun, resetting it with another weather ensures it keeps on roasting foes! Hippowdown is the star teammate here, having excellent defensive synergy with Mega Charizard Y and supporting it with Stealth Rock. Tyranitar doesn't work quite as well defensively, but it's still a worthy teammate as well thanks to its less predictable array of movesets. Dealing with Stealth Rock: Mega Charizard Y should always run an odd HP stat to avoid getting 2HKOed by its archnemesis, Stealth Rock. Removing Stealth Rock is rather tricky in the current format, but if needed, Glimmora is the best Pokemon for that job with Mortal Spin, with the bonus of having Stealth Rock to further support Mega Charizard Y. Other Options Roost: While not a defensive Pokemon, Mega Charizard Y forces out enough Pokemon to justify using Roost. This can be especially helpful when Stealth Rock is up, giving Mega Charizard Y another chance to switch in. Focus Blast: While not a reliable attack, Focus Blast deals massive damage to Tyranitar, which is otherwise one of Mega Charizard Y's strongest checks. Dragon Pulse: Dragon Pulse is Mega Charizard Y's strongest attack against Dragon-types like Garchomp and Mega Dragonite, though note that Garchomp still takes massive damage from Fire-type attacks as long as the sun is shining. Ancient Power: Ancient Power is a surprising attack to prevail in mirror matches against other Mega Charizard Y.

Garchomp's excellent Speed tier and power make it one of the premier offensive choices for setting up Stealth Rock. Outrage: Despite this set usually being used early-game to set up Stealth Rock, Outrage still gives Garchomp good cleaning potential and makes it a decent revenge killer if Focus Sash is still intact. Rock Tomb versus Poison Jab: Rock Tomb is a perfect fit for the early-game playstyle of this set, ensuring foes like Mega Gyarados and Dragonite won't be able to set up Dragon Dance freely after Garchomp's Focus Sash is broken, in addition to being a great response to both Mega Charizard formes. Focus Sash: Despite Garchomp's above average bulk, its sheer prominence means enough Pokemon are aiming to OHKO it, which makes Focus Sash worth using for the more reliable Stealth Rock setup. Other Options Poison Jab: If Mega Meganium is a serious issue for your team, Poison Jab can potentially flip that matchup. Dragon Tail: While usually better sorted towards more defensive Garchomp sets, Dragon Tail still has merit due to preventing bulky Steel-types like Iron Defense Corviknight and Swords Dance Mega Scizor from setting up.

Garchomp's good bulk and coverage place it near the top of the food chain of Swords Dance sweepers! Scale Shot: Scale Shot's reliability issues and reduction of Garchomp's bulk may make it seem like a strange choice for a sweeper, but the Speed boost makes Garchomp so much harder to revenge kill that it's worth it overall. Poison Jab versus Fire Fang: Poison Jab punctures through Mega Meganium, which otherwise can wall and revenge kill Garchomp fairly easily, as well as dealing with the rare Mega Clefable. Fire Fang, however weak it may be, is Garchomp's best shot of chewing through a weakened Corviknight, which otherwise is a strong Garchomp check. Other Options Outrage: Outrage makes Garchomp very vulnerable to being revenge killed, but its perfect accuracy and sheer power make it worth considering. Outrage pairs especially well with Lum Berry to cure confusion and block Yawn from Hippowdon, which is almost always 2HKOed by boosted Outrage even when it chomps down on a Sitrus Berry! Items Focus Sash: Focus Sash severely punishes teams that are unable to set up Stealth Rock, in addition to enhancing Garchomp's revenge killing capabilities. The vulnerability to entry hazards does sometimes conflict with this set's preference for late-game sweeping, though. Lum Berry: Lum Berry is an excellent response to common status users like Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash, leaving even less defensive answers for Garchomp. Life Orb: Life Orb gives Garchomp a tremendous power boost, now being able to OHKO offensive Mega Metagross without a boost! This comes at the cost of the recoil making Garchomp more vulnerable to priority attacks. Haban Berry: Choice Scarf Dragon-types such as opposing Garchomp and Hydreigon are common enough where Haban Berry can be useful to put less pressure on boosting Speed with Scale Shot. Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry can be a deadly surprise for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and bulky Primarina that are expecting to revenge kill Garchomp.

Garchomp's impressive power, Speed, and bulk make it arguably among the apex Choice Scarf revenge killers of Pokemon Champions Singles! Outrage: While locking Garchomp into a Rampaging state makes it easy prey for Fairy-types like Primarina and Mimikyu, the power Outrage offers turns Garchomp into a ferocious late-game cleaner and an effective revenge killer of most Dragon-type foes. Poison Jab: Poison Jab is Garchomp's preferred Fairy-type deterrent, OHKOing offensive Mega Meganium after Stealth Rock and usually 2HKOing the rare Mega Clefable as well. Rock Tomb versus Dragon Claw: Rock Tomb not only OHKOes Mega Charizard Y but also ensures that fast setup sweepers that may come in after the KO such as Dragon Dance Dragonite and opposing Swords Dance Garchomp will be easier to revenge kill thanks to the Speed drop. Dragon Claw, on the other hand, is Garchomp's most reliable Dragon-type STAB move, perfect for revenge killing weakened Dragon-types without fearing the wrath of Fairy-types getting a free KO. Jolly versus Adamant: Opposing Choice Scarf Garchomp are common enough that Jolly is the safer nature to use; Jolly also lets Garchomp outspeed Jolly Mega Dragonite. However, Adamant's power boost does make Garchomp a better late-game cleaner, granting it a good chance of OHKOing Mega Delphox with Outrage for example. Other Options Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock may seem nonsensical on a revenge killer, but it does give Garchomp some early-game utility if fitting in a more dedicated Stealth Rock setter is difficult for your team, at the cost of some revenge killing prowess. It also can be used to fool your opponent into thinking this set doesn't have Choice Scarf. Rock Slide: While it offers less utility than Rock Tomb, Rock Slide's flinch chance has the potential to flip a bad matchup. Iron Head: Poison Jab is usually preferred due to OHKOing Mega Meganium, but Iron Head's flinch chance could flip matchups against Fairy-types Garchomp can't OHKO, such as Mega Clefable, Mega Floette, and Sylveon. Additionally, Iron Head KOes Mimikyu after Disguise is broken without Stealth Rock support.

Garchomp uses its fantastic bulk to inflict double trouble, placing entry hazards and using Dragon Tail to disrupt and rack up damage on opposing teams. Spikes: Combining Spikes with Stealth Rock can make it much harder for defensive staples like Hippowdon to stay healthy throughout a match. Rock Slide: Even without Attack investment, Rock Slide is still strong enough to OHKO offensive Mega Charizard Y. SP Spread: The given SP spread has enough physical bulk to avoid the OHKO from opposing Jolly Garchomp's Outrage as well as Mega Kangaskhan's Ice Punch if using Sitrus Berry. The special bulk investment allows Garchomp to dodge the OHKO from Modest Primarina's Moonblast and Mega Gengar's Icy Wind. The leftover SPs are put into Speed. Items Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery helps Garchomp stay healthy and continue to be a nuisance. Particularly after big attacks like Primarina's Moonblast, Garchomp can heal out of range of a follow-up Aqua Jet. Haban Berry: Haban Berry is the most reliable method of letting Garchomp tank Draco Meteor from the likes of Archaludon and Hydreigon.

With excellent typing, Supreme Overlord, and Sucker Punch, Kingambit is a powerful revenge killer and bulky attacker. Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave: Sucker Punch helps pick off weakened attackers and is excellent insurance against late-game Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M and Garchomp. Kowtow Cleave is usually needed as a second Dark-type attack, though, particularly for Substitute users like Mega Gengar that can play around Sucker Punch. Swords Dance: Kingambit's amazing bulk allows it to consistently survive big hits such as Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, letting it set up a Swords Dance and fire back with +2 Sucker Punch. Iron Head versus Low Kick: Iron Head provides the best all-around power and coverage, allowing Kingambit to better threaten Primarina, Mimikyu, and Mega Floette. Low Kick is less flexible and leaves Kingambit vulnerable to Primarina, but it's the best way to take on opposing Kingambit and has a high chance to OHKO offensive Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage. Items Black Glasses: Black Glasses doubles down on making Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave as deadly as possible. When combined with Supreme Overlord, +2 Sucker Punch + Black Glasses will always OHKO offensive Garchomp. Lum Berry: If Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance ahead of time, Lum Berry will prevent Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W from switching in and completely ruining its momentum. Chople Berry: Chople Berry allows Kingambit to withstand some weaker Fighting-type attacks, such as Close Combat from Aegislash and Scizor and unboosted Body Press from Corviknight. With maximum HP investment, Kingambit also has a high chance to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and an average chance to survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast. Alternate EV Spread 8 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def / 24 Spe with Adamant: This spread maintains enough bulk to almost always survive Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's +2 Play Rough after Stealth Rock damage as well as Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake from full health. After maximizing Attack, the remaining SPs are invested into Speed, allowing Kingambit to outrun threats such as Mega Clefable with 2 Speed SPs.

Speed SP Benchmarks Moving first means Kingambit can improve certain matchups like Primarina. Generally speaking, it is recommended to sacrifice bulk instead of offensive power if wanting to reallocate to Speed. 3 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed negative Speed nature Aegislash. 11 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested base 60 Speed targets such as Clefable before Mega Evolution, Primarina, and Aegislash. 12 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar. 16 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Scizor before Mega Evolution. 18 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Corviknight, though its superior bulk and access to Body Press mean that it is still overwhelmingly favored in the matchup. 21 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Clefable, though keep in mind that Mega Clefable often receives Speed boosts from Baton Pass Espathra. 26 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

Basculgion-M is enjoying a fantastic offensive type combination in the current metagame, which, when combined with Adaptability, makes it a standout pick as a late-game sweeper with Last Respects and a potent early-game scout with Flip Turn. Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf gives Basculegion-M the Speed it needs to chunk foes and get out safely early-game while also allowing you to bring it in late-game without spending a turn to set up Agility. However, Basculegion-M's pitiful base 78 Speed means that it will be outsped by most of the other Choice Scarf users in the format, as well as most Dragon Dance users, so you need to be careful when positioning Basculegion-M. Wave Crash: Wave Crash will be Basculegion-M's primary early-game damage option if you elect to not pivot it out. Last Respects: Even after just one team member is KOed, Last Respects becomes an extremely potent move that's very difficult to switch into, and it gives Basculegion-M immense sweeping power once both allies have fainted. Flip Turn: Adaptability allows Flip Turn to deal notable damage for a pivoting move. Aqua Jet: Adaptability-boosted Aqua Jet does a considerable amount of damage and can get Basculegion-M out of trouble against other priority users or Speed-boosted foes. Other Options Ice Fang: Ice Fang provides coverage against Dragon-types and threatens Garchomp and Dragonite right out of the gate. Head Smash: Head Smash gives Basculegion-M a heavily damaging coverage option that threatens Gyarados and Dragonite.

This Agility set gives Basculegion-M the freedom to outspeed and threaten the majority of its metagame-relevant foes while enabling it to use multiple moves. Opposing Priority Users: While setting up Agility can make Basculegion-M an absolutely terrifying sweeper, late-game checks such as Aegislash, Mimikyu, and Kingambit are quite popular in the current metagame, so be careful when you see these during Team Preview. Adamant Nature: Agility's boost is going to give Basculegion-M plenty of Speed to set up its sweep. As Basculegion-M lacks an Attack-boosting setup move, an Adamant nature is preferred over Jolly. Adamant Basculegion-M is already outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp with an Agility boost, while a Jolly nature won't allow it to outspeed the likes of Choice Scarf Jolly Meowscarada. Items Mystic Water versus Spell Tag: These items will allow Basculegion-M's STAB moves to do hilariously high damage. Mystic Water allows Basculegion-M to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon with Wave Crash and has the added bonus of juicing up Aqua Jet's damage when it needs to rely on priority. On the other hand, Spell Tag will allow Last Respects to tear through walls, letting it OHKO maximum HP Mega Scizor after Stealth Rock at 150 Base Power. Focus Sash: Focus Sash ensures that Basculegion-M is going to tank a hit while it sets up Agility, but because entry hazards are very popular in the current metagame, saving your Focus Sash user for last can be a risky venture.

This Agility set gives Basculegion-M the freedom to outspeed and threaten the majority of its metagame-relevant foes while enabling it to use multiple moves. With the powerful Unburden ability, Sneasler can become a dangerous cleaner that wrecks havoc on frailer teams. Throat Chop versus Shadow Claw : When covering Psychic- and Ghost-types, Throat Chop is usually preferred for its higher power over Shadow Claw. However, Adamant Sneasler with Shadow Claw has about a 50/50 chance to knock out offensive Mimikyu after Disguise breaks. Swords Dance : If allowed to set up a Swords Dance, Sneasler can quickly spiral out of control and even overpower Hippowdon and Corviknight if they have been chipped. Fake Out: Fake Out can help get targets into KO range of its more powerful attacks, and the priority helps Sneasler catch faster foes prior to activating Unburden. Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is usually preferred to maximize sweeping potential, and with Unburden active, Sneasler can effortlessly outrun even Choice Scarf Dragapult. WIth maximum investment, Adamant Sneasler also maintains enough Speed to outrun threats like Mega Glimmora and unboosted Garchomp before Unburden's boost. Jolly gives Sneasler a little more consistency, allowing it to outrun more threats such as Mega Starmie and Focus Sash Gengar before Unburden activates. Other Options Acrobatics: Acrobatics is Sneasler's best move against threats like Mega Venusaur, Volcarona, and opposing Sneasler, though the move's damage is reliant on Sneasler consuming its item beforehand. Rock Slide: Rock Slide landing a clean OHKO on Mega Charizard Y is huge, but its uses are otherwise limited. Fling: Fling with King's Rock or Light Ball is the most flexible method of triggering Sneasler's Unburden, but the sacrifice to damage and coverage makes it a hard sell. Items White Herb: White Herb synergizes fantastically with Sneasler, allowing it to activate Unburden through its best attack Close Combat while also nullifying the defense drops once. White Herb can also function as insurance against Intimidate users. Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can give the somewhat frail Sneasler a bit more survivability, especially against priority attacks. However, it does make Sneasler reliant on the opponent to trigger Unburden for it. Lum Berry: Lum Berry puts Sneasler into a more niche role for its team, focused on countering status users like Yawn Umbreon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash.

Archaludon is one of the best walls in the entire game thanks to its incredible bulk and Stamina. With access to Stealth Rock, phazing support, and Draco Meteor, Archaludon can efficiently wear down lineups that lack dedicated checks to it. Thunderbolt versus Flash Cannon: Thunderbolt is Archaludon's best complementary move to Draco Meteor for its ability to hit key bulky targets Primarina and Corviknight, which comfortably check Archaludon otherwise, as well as hitting many other Steel-types neutrally. Flash Cannon is a more consistent damage source overall, but it doesn't help Archaludon against Steel-types like Corviknight, Scizor, and Aegislash. Roar versus Dragon Tail: Roar is the preferred phazing option for racking up Stealth Rock damage, as Pokemon immune to it are extremely uncommon, and it works through Substitute. Dragon Tail is more generally oppressive by dealing direct damage and phazing at the same time, and it additionally cannot be shut down by Taunt. However, Dragon Tail can make Archaludon struggle against Substitute users and does not work at all on Mega Floette, which can set up on Archaludon and threaten to snowball out of control. Mirror Coat: Archaludon's bulk makes it a viable user of Mirror Coat, which allows it to deal significant damage or completely take out targets such as Primarina and Mega Gengar. Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery is more effective at helping Archaludon survive multiple hits from big attacks, including super effective ones like Garchomp's Earthquake. On the other hand, Leftovers is superior when Archaludon can capitalize long-term on Stamina boosts from favorable defensive matchups against foes such as Meowscarada and Mega Starmie. Other Options Foul Play: Foul Play gives Archaludon a direct option against difficult physical attackers like Aegislash and Mega Metagross. Rest and Chesto Berry: Restoring Archaludon to full health after receiving several Stamina boosts can completely ruin physically offensive lineups that rely on attrition to beat Archaludon. SP Spreads All 2HKOs mentioned below factor in Archaludon having a +1 Defense boost from Stamina for the second hit. 32 HP / 23 Def / 11 SpD with Bold: With this spread, Archaludon is guaranteed to avoid the 2HKO from Jolly Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects and, when using Sitrus Berry, Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake. Leftover SPs are put into Special Defense. 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Calm: Maximum special bulk investment allows Archaludon to avoid the 2HKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball and Modest Primarina's Moonblast, assuming no Fairy Feather on the latter. This spread works particularly well with Mirror Coat, as Archaludon also has a significant chance to survive +1 Moonblast from offensive Mega Floette.

Archaludon can perform consistently as an offensive lead thanks to Sturdy, which lets it take full advantage of its respectable Speed and high-power attacks. Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides strong overlapping coverage with Draco Meteor, in particular pressuring defensive mainstays Primarina and Corviknight. Flash Cannon versus Steel Beam: Flash Cannon is the safest option for a Steel-type STAB attack and is more than sufficient against the likes of offensive Mimikyu and Glimmora. However, Steel Beam's massive Base Power makes dealing with bulkier threats like Hippowdon much more viable, even if it comes at the cost of survivability. Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere helps Archaludon win the mirror matchup while avoiding Draco Meteor usage, keeping its Special Attack stable and making it less likely to become setup bait. Even specially defensive Archaludon has a high chance to be 2HKOed. Aura Sphere is also the best option for taking on Kingambit. Stealth Rock: The combination of Archaludon's Speed and Sturdy allows it to reliably set Stealth Rock. Roar: Roar can disrupt dangerous setup sweepers like Iron Defense Mega Metagross and Swords Dance Mega Blaziken. Timid versus Modest: Many offensive threats such as Adamant Mimikyu, Jolly Basculegion-M, Jolly Hisuian Samurott, and Jolly Mega Gyarados are at or just below Archaludon's positive-nature Speed tier. As such, a Timid nature is usually preferred. However, the power increase from a Modest nature is still worth considering; for example, it gives Archaludon a decent chance to OHKO offensive Mega Gengar with Draco Meteor. Other Options Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is offensive Archaludon's best means of pressuring Aegislash and Gholdengo directly. Mirror Coat: Sturdy allows for more confident Mirror Coat usage, especially against targets like Gholdengo that boost their Special Attack, but it limits the direct offensive nature that this set likes to utilize and is very reliant on Sturdy being active. Items White Herb: White Herb allows Archaludon to fire off Draco Meteor once without worrying about the subsequent Special Attack drop, giving it incredible burst potential and generally making it less exploitable by setup attackers. Sitrus Berry: Archaludon's defensive typing and stats are so strong naturally that Sitrus Berry can still be worth running on an offensive set. Sitrus Berry will also always activate after using Steel Beam, giving Archaludon an extra health buffer as well as the potential to fire off a second Steel Beam without fainting.

When paired with a rain setter like Pelipper, Archaludon can build dangerous offensive momentum with Electro Shot. Electro Shot : Thanks to the Special Attack boost, even the first Electro Shot used can be difficult to switch into without an Electric resistance, and it can also OHKO frailer targets like Mega Lucario. Draco Meteor : Electro Shot may be the star of the show, but Draco Meteor is often Archaludon's best option when you're trying to play around Ground-type switch-ins such as Garchomp. Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere provides consistent coverage independent from the weather, pressuring Dark-types like Kingambit and opposing Archaludon. Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is an alternative Electric-type option to use outside of rain, which can be especially relevant for keeping pressure on Mega Charizard Y. SP Spreads and Items 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A standard offensive spread for use with Choice Scarf. A Timid nature is mandatory, as Archaludon wants to outrun Choice Scarf Jolly Basculegion-M. 32 HP / 11 Def / 15 SpA / 8 Spe with Modest: Going with a bulkier spread along with a Sitrus Berry sacrifices immediate offensive pressure, but it eases the need for prediction and allows Archaludon more flexibility in and out of rain. Enough Special Attack investment is maintained to guarantee that Electro Shot OHKOes offensive Mega Gyarados, and the Speed investment is enough to outrun fully invested base 60s like Primarina. The remaining SPs go into HP and Defense, giving Archaludon a decent chance of avoiding the 2HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake after Sitrus Berry healing and a Stamina activiation.

Mega Aerodactyl is an incredible Tailwind setter and offensive threat thanks to its massive Speed stat, outspeeding all unboosted Pokemon and some Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M. With its coverage, it is able to OHKO Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Garchomp. Rock Slide: Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. Rock Slide is also a strong spread damaging option for opposing Mega Aerodactyl and opposing Fire-types, and it can threaten foes with flinches due to Mega Aerodactyl's high Speed. Dual Wingbeat: Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat is able to OHKO some of the most common Focus Sash users in the format, such as Sneasler, Whimsicott, and Venusaur. It can also deal huge damage to Mega Staraptor and Sinistcha. Ice Fang: Mega Aerodactyl's Ice Fang is able to OHKO Garchomp and Inner Focus Dragonite. With Rock Slide and Ice Fang, Mega Aerodactyl is incredible against sun teams, since it can outspeed both Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp and OHKO them. Mega Evolving Aerodactyl: Aerodactyl can still function as a fast Tailwind setter in its base forme, so it can be brought to a battle to support another Mega Evolution. Aerodactyl can also make use of its ability Unnerve, shutting off Sitrus Berry healing on Pokemon like Incineroar and Farigiraf, as well as Kingambit's Chople Berry. Other Options Protect: Protect can be run instead of Ice Fang, making Mega Aerodactyl less vulnerable to Fake Out. Without Ice Fang, however, Mega Aerodactyl's matchup against Garchomp is tough due to the latter's access to Rock Slide and its Rough Skin activating twice if Mega Aerodactyl hits it with Dual Wingbeat. Wide Guard: Wide Guard is another option that can be run over Ice Fang, letting Mega Aerodactyl protect its teammates from the many strong spread attacks of the format like opposing Mega Aerodactyl's Rock Slide and Mega Froslass's Blizzard. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Aerodactyl has no way to threaten Steel-types like Mega Metagross, Kingambit, and Archaludon, which can all OHKO Mega Aerodactyl in return with Iron Head and Flash Cannon. Mega Aerodactyl is also susceptible to Fake Out from foes like Sneasler and Mega Raichu Y unless it's running Protect. Incineroar can be an especially problematic Fake Out user, since it also lowers Mega Aerodactyl's Attack with Intimidate. Rain teams can be problematic for Mega Aerodactyl, since they commonly use Archaludon and Mega Swampert, the latter of which being able to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl thanks to Swift Swim and OHKO it with Wave Crash. Rain teams also commonly use Grimmsnarl, which can reduce Mega Aerodactyl's damage output with Reflect and Parting Shot. Pelipper can also be annoying for Mega Aerodactyl to deal with, able to threaten it with Weather Ball and use Wide Guard to protect Mega Charizard Y from Rock Slide, allowing the latter to OHKO Mega Aerodactyl with its own Water-type Weather Ball. Sand teams are also problematic for Mega Aerodactyl, since Mega Tyranitar can tank any of Mega Aerodactyl's attacks and threaten it back with Rock Slide. Sand teams also commonly feature Sand Rush Excadrill, which can outspeed Mega Aerodactyl in the sand and OHKO it with Iron Head. Venusaur can outspeed Mega Aerodactyl with Chlorophyll and, if it's holding a Life Orb, OHKO it with Leaf Storm or Solar Beam. Venusaur can also put Mega Aerodactyl to sleep with Sleep Powder, allowing a partner like Garchomp to safely attack it with Rock Slide. Corviknight can tank any of Mega Aerodactyl's attacks and threaten it with Iron Head, set itself up with Bulk Up, or set its own Tailwind. Rotom-Wash can similarly tank Mega Aerodactyl's attacks and threaten it back with Hydro Pump, Thunderbolt, and Will-O-Wisp. Trick Room from Farigiraf can turn Mega Aerodactyl's huge Speed stat against it and allow Pokemon like Kingambit to outspeed it and OHKO with Iron Head. Farigiraf can also 2HKO Mega Aerodactyl with Thunderbolt. Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp is Mega Aerodactyl's strongest partner. It can freely use Earthquake next to Mega Aerodactyl to threaten the Steel- and Rock-types that Mega Aerodactyl hates facing and has an excellent matchup against sand teams. In return, Mega Aerodactyl provides Garchomp with Tailwind, letting it outspeed and OHKO Pokemon like Mega Raichu Y, which could otherwise outspeed Mega Aerodactyl and OHKO it before Garchomp could move. Mega Charizard Y is a great Mega Evolution to use alongside Aerodactyl with Aerodactylite. It can threaten Steel-types with Heat Wave and Weather Ball, OHKO Mega Swampert, deal significant damage to Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam, and shut off opposing weather. Mega Charizard Y also appreciates base forme Aerodactyl's ability to set Tailwind and heavily damage opposing Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp. Mega Aerodactyl is strong against some of Mega Charizard Y's worst matchups, such as against Mega Dragonite and Mega Delphox, while Mega Charizard Y is strong against Mega Mawile and Mega Metagross. Kingambit benefits greatly from Tailwind allowing it to outspeed Basculegion-M, opposing Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar, threatening the former with Kowtow Cleave and the latter two with Low Kick. Sylveon is another good beneficiary of Tailwind, using it to outspeed Pokemon like Sneasler and pose a threat with its strong Hyper Voice, while Mega Aerodactyl can threaten checks to Sylveon like Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. Both of these Pokemon's naturally slow Speed stats let them punish Trick Room strategies, with Kingambit even being able to OHKO Farigiraf with Kowtow Cleave. Incineroar can threaten Farigiraf with Throat Chop and can use Fake Out to let Mega Aerodactyl set up Tailwind in front of Pokemon like Venusaur. Farigiraf can block opposing Fake Out thanks to Armor Tail and negate opposing Trick Room. Farigiraf can also use Thunderbolt to OHKO Pelipper and deal solid damage to Pokemon like Basculegion-M and Corviknight.

Annihilape uses its excellent offensive coverage, solid Speed, and immunity to common defensive tools like Intimidate and Fake Out to dismantle opposing teams and create awkward situations for the opponent with Phantom Force. It also has incredible matchups against metagame staples like Incineroar, Sneasler, and Kingambit. Phantom Force: Phantom Force forces common setup Pokemon like Mega Delphox, Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar to either switch out or take devastating damage. Phantom Force also breaks Protect, which can allow a slower partner to attack Annihilape's target even if they use Protect. Rock Tomb vs. Rage Fist: Rock Tomb can be used for speed control and allows Annihilape to deal big damage to Mega Charizard Y. Rage Fist can be used as an alternate Ghost-type attack. Its damage output is slightly higher than Phantom Force after Annihilape gets hit once, and at 150 Base Power, Rage Fist can OHKO Sinistcha, Gholdengo, and Sneasler. Focus Sash: Focus Sash is needed to let Annihilape check Pokemon like Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar that could otherwise outspeed and OHKO it with moves like Psychic and Shadow Ball respectively. Defiant: Defiant makes Annihilape great at deterring Intimidate users. When combined with Annihilape's Fake Out immunity and Close Combat, it makes Annihilape a perfect counter to Incineroar. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Fast Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Whimsicott, and Sylveon under Tailwind can 2HKO Annihilape while tanking a Phantom Force or Rage Fist. Mega Staraptor can similarly outspeed and threaten Annihilape with Brave Bird while also being able to tank any of its attacks; however, it can take big damage from Phantom Force or a boosted Rage Fist combined with Brave Bird's recoil. Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed and OHKO Annihilape through its Focus Sash with Dual Wingbeat. Redirection: Maushold and Mega Scovillain are particularly bad redirectors for Annihilape to deal with. Maushold can nullify Phantom Force's damage due to its Ghost immunity, while Mega Scovillain can burn Annihilape thanks to Spicy Spray, which not only reduces Annihilape's offensive prowess but also breaks its Focus Sash. Farigiraf: Farigiraf can safely switch into Phantom Force while also being able to tank a Close Combat. Farigiraf can also remove Annihilape's Speed advantage with Trick Room and 2HKO it with Psychic. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is one of Annihilape's best partners due to its Fairy resistance and ability to deal big damage to Annihilape's checks. Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave ignores redirection and can 2HKO Maushold and Mega Scovillain, while Weather Ball can 2HKO Farigiraf through its Sitrus Berry healing. In return, Annihilape can force out Basculegion-M and Incineroar, which are common checks to Mega Charizard Y. Poison-types: With Chlorophyll, Venusaur in the sun can outspeed and threaten Fairy-types with Sludge Bomb. If given a Life Orb, it can outspeed and OHKO Mega Aerodactyl with Solar Beam. Toxapex can sit in front of Fairy-types and take them down over time with the combination of Toxic and Infestation. Toxapex can also trap Pokemon on the field with Infestation, forcing them to get hit by Phantom Force. Phantom Force combined with Protect can let Annihilape stall out turns, letting Toxapex's Infestation and Toxic rack up damage before Phantom Force KOes the target. Incineroar and Garchomp: Incineroar can use Fake Out to let Annihilape set up a Phantom Force and can threaten Farigiraf with Throat Chop. Intimidate also drops Mega Aerodactyl's Attack low enough so that it can't OHKO Annihilape with Dual Wingbeat. Incineroar appreciates Annihilape's good matchups against Sneasler and Basculegion-M. Choice Scarf Garchomp can outspeed and deal big damage to Mega Aerodactyl with Rock Slide, and it appreciates Annihilape's ability to threaten Hydreigon.

Hisuian Arcanine is capable of threatening many of the top Pokemon in the format such as Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Charizard Y with its super powerful STAB moves in combination with Rock Head; it's so powerful that it is even able to easily 2HKO Pokemon such as Sneasler that resist its Rock-type STAB move. Head Smash: Head Smash, in conjunction with Rock Head, becomes a devastating no-drawback attack capable of almost always OHKOing Mega Froslass through Aurora Veil in the snow; weaker options like Rock Slide don't come close to this power. Extreme Speed: Extreme Speed allows Hisuian Arcanine to pick off low-HP foes like a Sneasler or Whimsicott that has been brought down to Focus Sash by an ally or by Hisuian Arcanine itself. Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Hisuian Arcanine to survive attacks such as Earth Power from Venusaur, retaliating with Flare Blitz. Other Options Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Hisuian Arcanine to deal spread damage and possibly fish for flinches, though it does come at the cost of Extreme Speed, leaving Hisuian Arcanine unable to beat Sneasler. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Water-type Pokemon like Mega Swampert in the rain and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed Hisuian Arcanine and easily survive its attacks or bring it down to Focus Sash with Flip Turn to leave it vulnerable to any attacks, respectively. Milotic with Coil can set up and heal off Hisuian Arcanine's damage with Recover, while Focus Sash Basculegion-M, thanks to its immunity to Extreme Speed, can use two Aqua Jets to dispatch of Hisuian Arcanine. Ground-type Pokemon: Ground-type Pokemon like Garchomp and Excadrill in the sand can outspeed and bring Hisuian Arcanine down to Focus Sash with Earthquake. Garchomp in particular resists both of Hisuian Arcanine's STAB moves and breaks Hisuian Arcanine's Focus Sash with Rough Skin if it attempts to attack Garchomp. Problematic Mega Pokemon: With the combination of Fake Out and Focus Blast, Mega Raichu Y can KO Hisuian Arcanine without allowing it to make a move. Mega Tyranitar can easily tank Hisuian Arcanine's attacks, dealing lots of damage with Rock Slide while enabling its ally Excadrill. Mega Staraptor outspeeds and 2HKOes Hisuian Arcanine with Close Combat, using Roost to recover the big chunks of damage that Hisuian Arcanine could deal to it. Good Partners and Synergies: Sylveon is able to target down Garchomp and Mega Staraptor, and it boasts huge burst damage potential in Hyper Beam to help break through bulky Pokemon like Archaludon, appreciating the help it gets into Steel- and Fire-types from Hisuian Arcanine. Hisuian Arcanine also pairs nicely with Kingambit, taking out Mega Charizard Y and other Fire-types with ease while receiving help into Basculegion-M and Mega Tyranitar. A Basculegion-M can also be of help to Hisuian Arcanine, threatening Mega Swampert under the rain, Mega Tyranitar, and Ground-types with Wave Crash while swapping in on Fighting-type attacks like Close Combat from Sneasler and Mega Staraptor for Hisuian Arcanine. Mega Pokemon: Mega Staraptor does well into Mega Tyranitar and opposing Fighting- and Ground-type Pokemon, using Tailwind to allow Hisuian Arcanine to outspeed and OHKO or deal major damage to Pokemon like Mega Floette with Head Smash. Mega Charizard Y and Ceruledge are dealt with by Hisuian Arcanine, while Mega Staraptor deters Intimidate from Incineroar thanks to Contrary, allowing Hisuian Arcanine to deal as much damage as possible. Mega Raichu Y is another good Mega Pokemon to pair with Hisuian Arcanine, threatening the Water-type Pokemon that scare Hisuian Arcanine with Zap Cannon.

Acting as rain's main powerhouse in Regulation M-B, Archaludon has the ability to easily snowball out of control if left alone, thanks to Electro Shot, Leftovers, Stamina, and its naturally high physical bulk. Archaludon has a good matchup against Mega Aerodactyl, Basculegion-M, and Toxapex thanks to Electro Shot and its typing. Leftovers: Archaludon utilizes Leftovers to increase its longevity. This allows Archaludon to sweep more effectively while making some attacks, such as Choice Scarf Garchomp's Earthquake, 3HKOs instead of 2HKOs. Stamina: Archaludon can accumulate Stamina boosts to become nearly physically impenetrable. This allows Archaludon to take attacks such as bulky Garchomp's Earthquake and Kingambit's and Mega Tyranitar's Low Kick more effectively over time. Electro Shot: Electro Shot allows Archaludon to snowball through teams while threatening the common Pelipper, Milotic, and Basculegion-M. However, Electro Shot is reliant on rain, which makes it easily punishable by changing the weather with Pokemon like Mega Froslass. Positioning with Archaludon: Archaludon can switch into weaker attacks such as Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Mega Raichu Y's and Incineroar's Fake Out to accumulate Stamina boosts. Because Archaludon's Stamina and longevity permit it to stay on the field as long as possible, it is important to position Archaludon correctly so that it faces foes that don't threaten it to swap and drop its boosts such as Sneasler and Mega Charizard Y. SP Spreads 27 HP / 5 Def / 5 SpA / 26 SpD / 3 Spe with Calm: This is Archaludon's primary spread, allowing it to survive Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Weather Ball and Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M in Tailwind, and optimize HP for Leftovers recovery. The rest of the SPs are put into Special Attack to maximize offense. 32 HP / 1 Def / 5 SpA / 25 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest: This more offensive spread allows Archaludon to survive the aforementioned Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat and outspeed the aforementioned Choice Scarf Basculegion in Tailwind. The Modest nature allows Archaludon to almost always OHKO Calm Milotic with Electro Shot. 27 HP / 11 Def / 8 SpA / 17 SpD / 3 Spe with Bold: This physically defensive spread allows Archaludon to hit the same Speed benchmark, HP optimization, and Special Attack dump as the primary spread while letting it survive Mega Swampert's Helping Hand-boosted Earthquake, Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M's 200-Base Power Last Respects, and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Archaludon's middling Special Defense leaves it open to strong special attacks such as Mega Floette's Moonblast, Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Hydreigon's Draco Meteor and Earth Power. Archaludon is extremely exploitable without any Stamina or Electro Shot boosts, and its reliance on rain can make it tough to use in weather wars against opposing setters like Mega Charizard Y. Archaludon is overwhelmed by double targeting with special attacks, such as the combination of Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Weather Ball and Venusaur's Life Orb-boosted Earth Power. Without rain, Electro Shot is extremely exploitable, leaving Archaludon to double targeting. Despite Archaludon's great physical bulk, Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can threaten huge damage with Close Combat. Mega Raichu Y can stall out its own Mega Evolution to soak up Archaludon's Electro Shot thanks to Lightning Rod and can threaten it with Focus Blast after Mega Evolving. Excadrill resists all of Archaludon's moves and threatens it back with High Horsepower and Earthquake. Mega Swampert can turn Archaludon's own rain against it by outspeeding Archaludon, even if it's under Tailwind, and threatening huge damage with Earthquake. Garchomp can threaten huge damage on an unboosted Archaludon with Life Orb-boosted Earthquake, outspeeding and safely 2HKOing it if Archaludon is not already at +1 Special Attack. Venusaur resists Archaludon's Electro Shot while threatening Archaludon with Life Orb-boosted Earth Power or thwarting its momentum with Sleep Powder. Mega Venusaur utilizes its bulk to outlast Archaludon that lack Electro Shot boosts. Good Partners and Synergies: Pelipper is the far more common rain setter for Archaludon; it handles Pokemon that give Archaludon trouble such as Sinistcha, Mega Staraptor, and Excadrill with Hurricane and rain-boosted Weather Ball. Pelipper can utilize Tailwind for speed control and Wide Guard to block Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave, Mega Swampert and Garchomp's Earthquake, and Sylveon's Hyper Voice. Politoed does not have access to STAB Hurricane but has greater bulk and Speed, and it also has access to Encore and Perish Song. Encore can lock Sneasler into Fake Out, while Perish Song can remove bulky threats to Archaludon such as Mega Staraptor and Mega Venusaur. Basculegion-M acts as a switch-in to any Fighting-type move that may threaten Archaludon and threatens Ground-types like Garchomp and Excadrill. Basculegion-M has access to the powerful Last Respects to clean up games with ease once Archaludon has chipped foes down, and it can chunk foes early-game with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash, allowing Archaludon to clean up. Mega Swampert's Earthquake and High Horsepower can chunk opposing Archaludon and OHKO Sneasler and Mega Raichu Y, and its Ice Punch can OHKO Garchomp. Mega Swampert can also outspeed and OHKO Mega Floette and Sylveon with rain-boosted Wave Crash, preventing them from dealing huge damage to Archaludon. Sinistcha provides Archaludon with recovery in Hospitality and Life Dew, speed control in Trick Room, and redirection in Rage Powder. Sinistcha can also act as a switch-in to attacks Archaludon is weak to, handling Garchomp's Earthquake and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast comfortably. Furthermore, Sinistcha can check Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. By providing dual screens support and Special Attack drops to with Spirit Break, Grimmsnarl can maximize Archaludon's bulk and weaken moves such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Mega Floette's Moonblast. Parting Shot can bring in Archaludon safely, weaken foes, and allow it to take moves that may threaten Grimmsnarl, namely Basculegion-M's Wave Crash and Kingambit's Iron Head, while gaining a Stamina boost. Mega Charizard Y can threaten problematic foes like Venusaur and Excadrill with Weather Ball in and out of the rain, respectively. Hurricane can be used at times to threaten Grass-types that trouble Archaludon such as Sinistcha, Venusaur, and Mega Scovillain inside of rain. Under sun, Mega Charizard Y can utilize Weather Ball and Heat Wave to threaten Alolan Ninetales and Mega Froslass to win weather wars; these attacks also threaten Excadrill and Gholdengo to pave the way for Archaludon to sweep. In exchange for this utility, Archaludon can cover for the Rock-types that give Mega Charizard Y trouble, such as Mega Aerodactyl and Lycanroc-D. However, Archaludon cannot use Electro Shot as easily when brought alongside Mega Charizard Y.

Basculegion-M boasts incredible offensive prowess due to Adaptability, capable of dealing heavy damage to almost every Pokemon in the metagame. Wave Crash is able to take most of neutral foes' health or even OHKO them, while Last Respects allows Basculegion-M to sweep once its partners have fainted as long as it can outspeed its opponents. It also boasts an excellent matchup against Sneasler. Wave Crash: Wave Crash allows Basculegion-M to threaten heavy damage right off the bat without needing to wait for its partners to faint, notably threatening foes such as Mega Charizard Y and Farigiraf. Wave Crash also allows it to hit foes that resist Last Respects, such as Kingambit and Incineroar. Last Respects: This move allows Basculegion-M to threaten foes without damaging itself, relevant when facing foes such as Kingambit, which can bring Basculegion-M to very low HP with Sucker Punch to the point where the recoil from Wave Crash would knock it out. Last Respects also allows Basculegion-M to hit the Grass- and Water-types of the format, such as Sinistcha, Venusaur, and Toxapex. Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet allows Basculegion-M to pick off foes at low HP, such as Lycanroc-D after activating Focus Sash. Aqua Jet also allows it to threaten significant damage onto foes such as Mega Charizard Y even without the speed advantage. Life Orb versus Mystic Water: Life Orb gives Basculegion-M a power boost on all moves, allowing it to take out opposing Basculegion-M even with Last Respects at 50 Base Power, as well as threaten a consistent OHKO on no bulk Garchomp with Wave Crash. However, Life Orb has considerable consequences for Basculegion-M's longevity, particularly preventing it from sticking around for multiple turns after taking a Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Mystic Water gives Basculegion-M a slight power boost on only its Water-type moves, notably allowing it to threaten Mega Charizard Y in the sun and bulky Mega Floette prior to Intimidate while maintaining its health. SP Spreads 32 Atk / 14 Def / 20 Spe with Adamant: Basculegion-M uses this spread in order to survive Sucker Punch from non-Black Glasses Kingambit, allowing Basculegion-M to consistently beat it in an endgame where Kingambit is chipped and Basculegion-M is at full health. The remainder of the spread maximizes Basculegion-M's Attack and optimizes Basculegion-M's Speed, allowing it, with Tailwind support, to outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Basculegion-M is prone to being outsped by foes such as Venusaur, which is able to OHKO it with Leaf Storm. Additionally, it struggles against Kingambit, which is able to survive Wave Crash and Last Respects, before retaliating with Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch, both of which are able to OHKO Basculegion-M when Kingambit is holding Black Glasses. Sinistcha is also able to redirect attacks from Basculegion-M, withstanding Wave Crash thanks to its own Water resistance and allowing a partner to take it out. As such, Basculegion-M relies on Last Respects to threaten Sinistcha, meaning it cannot effectively threaten Sinistcha at the start of the game. Finally, Archaludon is able to OHKO Basculegion-M with Electro Shot while being able to switch in on Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks, like Wave Crash, to gain a Defense boost. Threatening Mega Evolutions: Many Mega Evolutions are able to threaten Basculegion-M with heavy damage if they outspeed it, such as Mega Gengar, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Raichu Y with Shadow Ball, Solar Beam, and Zap Cannon, respectively. Additionally, Mega Scovillain can protect a partner with Rage Powder and hamper Basculegion-M's damage output thanks to Spicy Spray, which leaves additional chip damage on Basculegion-M; this can add up quickly when combined with Wave Crash or Life Orb's recoil damage. Mega Scovillain can also deal significant damage to Basculegion-M with Giga Drain. Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M appreciates speed control such as Tailwind and Trick Room from allies such as Whimsicott and Farigiraf, as these allow it to outspeed other, faster threats such as Mega Charizard Y, Venusaur, and Mega Raichu Y. However, Basculegion-M can also rely on its partners to take care of these foes. Notably, Lycanroc-D is able to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Accelerock, while Mega Froslass is able to overwrite the sun, removing the threat of Solar Beam from Mega Charizard Y and allowing Basculegion-M to outspeed Venusaur while hitting it with Blizzard. Additionally, Garchomp is able to switch in on Mega Raichu Y when it uses Zap Cannon and OHKO it. Other good partners: Mega Floette is able to threaten Kingambit and Archaludon and even OHKO them with Light of Ruin. Additionally, Kingambit with Low Kick is able to cover for Basculegion-M's weakness to opposing Kingambit, while Basculegion-M deters foes from bringing Sneasler thanks to a great defensive matchup and ability to OHKO it. Additionally, Kingambit covers for opposing Ghost-types such as Mega Gengar, Mega Froslass, and opposing Basculegion-M. Lastly, Mega Charizard Y is able to hit the Grass-types such as Sinistcha and Venusaur that Basculegion-M struggles with, while Baculegion-M is able to hit opposing Rock-types in return. Basculegion-M is also able to take care of opposing Basculegion-M if Mega Charizard Y does not have Solar Beam.
