The set for Ceruledge does not significantly change from Regulation M-A to M-B, nor does its teammates and method of play. To see the analysis information, please refer to the Regulation M-A analysis.

Mega Charizard Y is a ruthless sweeper dealing immense damage with its Fire-type attacks. It threatens OHKOs and 2HKOs on the majority of the metagame such as Mega Floette, Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Metagross. Mega Charizard Y opts to run bulk rather than maximizing its offense and Speed to help it survive longer in contrast to Regulation M-A. Three Attacks Sweeper: Mega Charizard Y dominates simply using three attacks: Heat Wave, Weather Ball, and Solar Beam. Heat Wave provides powerful spread Fire-type damage. Weather Ball deals insane Fire-type damage while sun is active or provides handy coverage depending on the weather, and it is unaffected by Wide Guard. Solar Beam is necessary to threaten Water-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert. Drought: The sun set by Drought increases the damage of Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type attacks, guaranteeing that Heat Wave will OHKO Kingambit and Sinistcha. It also allows Solar Beam to be used in a single turn, enables Venusaur's Chlorophyll, and reduces the damage of Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert. Mega Evolving Charizard: Mega Charizard Y should not Mega Evolve right away unless there are no foes that can override the sun. It is best to wait until the opponent has sent out or Mega Evolved their weather setter like Pelipper and Mega Froslass before Mega Evolving Mega Charizard Y to ensure sun is not overridden. Other Options Helping Hand: Helping Hand can be run over Solar Beam when Mega Charizard Y is paired with Venusaur. Helping Hand-boosted Solar Beam from Life Orb Venusaur OHKOs Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl, dealing significantly more damage than Mega Charizard Y's own Solar Beam. Ancient Power: Ancient Power is a niche move used instead of Solar Beam primarily as a surprise attack to OHKO opposing Mega Charizard Y and to let it threaten Ceruledge and Hisuian Arcanine. An omni boost from Ancient Power is also extremely beneficial for Mega Charizard Y, letting it survive Rock Slide and giving it a chance to OHKO Mega Floette with Weather Ball. SP Spreads 16 HP / 25 Def / 12 SpA / 13 Spe with Modest: The given spread lets Mega Charizard Y survive Rock Slide from non-Life Orb Garchomp and gives it a good chance to survive Mystic Water-boosted Wave Crash from Adaptability Jolly Basculegion-M in the sun. 13 Speed SPs let Mega Charizard Y outspeed maximum Speed Modest Venusaur without active Chlorophyll, and the remaining SPs are invested into Special Attack to maximize Mega Charizard Y's damage output. 30 HP / 31 Def / 1 SpA / 4 Spe with Modest: This bulkier SP spread provides Mega Charizard Y with a high chance to survive Rock Slide from Life Orb-boosted Jolly Garchomp and Aerodactyl and grants a favorable chance to survive Wave Crash from Life Orb-boosted Adaptability Basculegion-M in the sun. The Speed investment ensures Mega Charizard Y outruns Adamant Mega Swampert and Mega Tyranitar in the sun, and the remaining SPs are put into Special Attack. 16 HP / 17 Def / 10 SpA / 23 Spe with Timid: This faster SP spread allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed Excadrill in the sun as well as Glimmora and Hisuian Arcanine. The defensive investment allows Mega Charizard Y to survive Rock Slide from -1 Lycanroc-D, and the leftover SPs maximize Mega Charizard Y's Special Attack. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Charizard Y's biggest adversaries are Rock-types such as Mega Tyranitar, Mega Aerodactyl, Lycanroc-D, and Glimmora. They all easily threaten OHKOs with Rock Slide, Accelerock, and Power Gem respectively while Mega Charizard Y struggles to KO them. Mega Raichu Y outspeeds Mega Charizard Y and easily threatens an OHKO with Zap Cannon. Rain teams are difficult for Mega Charizard Y to defeat. Rain significantly reduces the damage of Heat Wave and Solar Beam, and it enables Mega Swampert's Swift Swim, allowing it to outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash. Pelipper, Archaludon, and Sinistcha are also difficult for Mega Charizard Y to remove while rain is active. Pelipper and Archaludon threaten to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Weather Ball and Electro Shot, respectively. Sinistcha can also set up Trick Room, allowing Pelipper and Archaludon to attack first, and it can provide them with redirection as well as healing thanks to Hospitality. Although Mega Charizard Y can survive their attacks, Garchomp and Basculegion-M are still threats to it. Mega Charizard Y is naturally outrun by Garchomp and is unable to KO it with Solar Beam before Garchomp attacks twice with Rock Slide. Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Charizard Y with Tailwind support from Whimsicott, giving Basculegion-M an opportunity to KO Mega Charizard Y before it can attack. While it is an uncommon pick, Ceruledge walls all of Mega Charizard Y's attacks, so it can easily take advantage of this to set up with Bulk Up and proceed to snowball. Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp and Basculegion-M are Mega Charizard Y's best partners, easily threatening Rock-types and Ceruledge as well as opposing Garchomp and Basculegion-M. Garchomp in particular can remove Mega Raichu Y. They are also great at pressuring opposing Mega Charizard Y. While Mega Floette cannot be used in the same battle as Mega Charizard Y, it synergizes well as an alternative Mega Evolution when Mega Charizard Y has an unfavorable matchup. Mega Floette is great at removing Garchomp and deals devastating damage to Pokemon commonly found on rain teams like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Archaludon. In return, Mega Charizard Y can easily threaten Mega Metagross, Gholdengo, Mega Gengar, and Mega Mawile, all of which Mega Floette is threatened by. Incineroar is great at providing damage mitigation with Intimidate, ensuring that Mega Charizard Y survives Rock Slide from the Rock-types and Garchomp. It also provides Fake Out support to let Mega Charizard Y dish out damage safely. Venusaur threatens Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp, which Mega Charizard Y struggles to damage, as well as common Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert. Sleep Powder can also disrupt foes, letting Mega Charizard Y stick around for longer.

Mega Delphox serves as a strong setup threat in the M-B metagame. Its excellent Speed enables it to outspeed and check key targets such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Sneasler and Toxapex, and it also makes good use of its solid special bulk and typing to combat opposing Mega Evolutions like Mega Metagross and Mega Floette. Psyshock vs. Psychic: Psyshock enables Mega Delphox to always 2HKO Mega Floette and Sylveon, while Psychic deals higher damage, 2HKOing Garchomp and being able to OHKO Mega Staraptor with little bulk investment before it gets a Special Defense boost. Both options cleanly handle Poison-types like Sneasler and Toxapex. SP Spreads 5 HP / 32 SpA / 29 Spe with Timid: Mega Delphox's SP spread enables it to outspeed Mega Gengar while slightly increasing its bulk, giving it good odds of surviving Kingambit's non-Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch with Friend Guard support and always surviving Mega Aerodactyl's Rock Slide. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Delphox is terrified of Pelipper, as Drizzle shuts down its ability to do reliable spread damage with Heat Wave, while its partners like Mega Swampert and Archaludon can easily eliminate Mega Delphox. Dark-types like Incineroar and Mega Tyranitar easily take Mega Delphox's attacks and threaten to OHKO it with Darkest Lariat and Knock Off. Mega Delphox struggles greatly under Trick Room, which leaves it easily picked off by the likes of Mega Mawile. Kingambit can prove to be an especially dangerous Trick Room attacker, as even outside of Trick Room, it can pick Mega Delphox off with Sucker Punch. Basculegion-M can effortlessly remove Mega Delphox before it can do anything, as Basculegion-M can either use a Life Orb-boosted Aqua Jet or hit it with Wave Crash if Basculegion-M is holding Choice Scarf. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Blastoise and Mega Floette can handle the matchups Mega Delphox struggles against, with both doing wonders against Trick Room and rain teams. After a Shell Smash, Mega Blastoise easily decimates the likes of Mega Swampert and Mega Mawile, while Mega Floette obliterates Farigriaf and Archaludon with Light of Ruin. In return, both enjoy Mega Delphox handling their checks such as Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Mega Metagross. Mega Staraptor can focus down Dark-types such as Incineroar and Kingambit for Mega Delphox while appreciating its ability to scare away foes like Toxapex, Mega Gengar, and Gholdengo. Sinistcha and Maushold provide vital redirection support for Mega Delphox, enabling it to set up Nasty Plot and protecting it from Kingambit's Sucker Punch. Sinistcha can also check Water-type foes such as Mega Swampert and Milotic. Kingambit can provide support with Sucker Punch to pick off faster threats aiming to eliminate Mega Delphox such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. It can also help Mega Delphox deal with Trick Room by removing Farigiraf before it can set up Trick Room or by outspeeding it if Trick Room goes up. Garchomp can serve as an excellent partner, as it is capable of freely using Earthquake thanks to Mega Delphox's Levitate while also threatening the likes of Incineroar and Mega Tyranitar. In return, Mega Delphox can eliminate foes such as Sinistcha and Mega Froslass that pose a problem for Garchomp. Sneasler can provide Fake Out support to help Mega Delphox get a Nasty Plot off; it can also use Quick Guard to block Kingambit's Sucker Punch, enabling Mega Delphox to remove it with Heat Wave.

Dragonite is a strong anti-metagame pick with respectable offensive coverage into common threats and access to a strong priority move in Extreme Speed. Its well-rounded offensive and defensive profile gives it favorable matchups into metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit, while its two viable abilities let it adapt to their common teammates, such as Incineroar and Garchomp. Extreme Speed: Extreme Speed is valuable not only to finish off weakened foes; with a Life Orb, it can threaten 2HKOs on opposing Fairy-types such as Mega Floette and Sylveon after an ally has used Fake Out. Extreme Speed's ability to meaningfully threaten these Fairy-types is important because they are immune to Dragon Claw and resist Low Kick. Low Kick versus Fire Punch: Low Kick provides Dragonite a reliable way to threaten metagame staples such as Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Incineroar. Fire Punch, while not being able to OHKO Kingambit, allows Dragonite to hit a wider variety of threats, notably incuding Gholdengo, Whimsicott, and Alolan Ninetales. Inner Focus versus Multiscale: Inner Focus grants Dragonite an immunity to common defensive tools like Intimidate and Fake Out, allowing Dragonite to power through teams that rely on Fake Out from Incineroar and Sneasler to protect an offensive sweeper like Mega Delphox and Mega Blastoise. A bulkier spread with Multiscale allows Dragonite to have a better matchup against faster Dragon-types like Garchomp while also providing a safety net against other threats such as boosted Kingambit. Life Orb versus Dragon Fang: Life Orb is the preferred item on Inner Focus sets as it significantly powers up all of Dragonite's moves, allowing Dragonite to 2HKO Incineroar with Low Kick even after Sitrus Berry recovery and pick up 2HKOs on most neutral targets with the combination of Dragon Claw and Extreme Speed. On Multiscale sets, Dragon Fang is used instead to secure the OHKO on most variants of Garchomp while not incurring the recoil from Life Orb that would break Multiscale. Other Options Superpower: On Inner Focus sets, Superpower's increased power over Low Kick allows Dragonite to OHKO Incineroar while also putting bulkier Steel-types such as Chople Berry Kingambit and Archaludon in KO range of an ally's attack such as Moonblast from Whimsicott. However, the Defense drop does put Dragonite in range of some moves like 100 Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion. Lum Berry: Multiscale sets running Fire Punch over Low Kick can run Lum Berry to better deal with Sleep Powder from Venusaur and Zap Cannon from Mega Raichu-Y, as well as burns from Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha and Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray. Dragonite can then pick them off before they can spread their status further. However, this does leave Dragonite unable to KO bulkier variants of Garchomp with the combination of Dragon Claw and Extreme Speed. Tailwind: Tailwind can be used on a Multiscale set to provide speed control to the team while allowing Dragonite to outpace Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon without allied support. However, this does come at the expense of an important coverage move or Protect. SP Spreads 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread allows Dragonite to outrun Adamant non-Choice Scarf Basculegion and Mega Blastoise. Basculegion is immune to Extreme Speed and can threaten huge damage with Last Respects. Outspeeding Mega Blastoise allows Dragonite to weaken its Water Spout with Dragon Claw; even if Mega Blastoise has already used Shell Smash, Dragonite will attack first if it has Tailwind support. 18 HP / 32 Atk / 16 Spe with Adamant: Since Dragonite has access to a strong priority attack in Extreme Speed, maximum Speed investment is not strictly necessary. This spread allows Dragonite to outpace even the fastest Kingambit while also outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon under Tailwind. If running Multiscale, the added bulk allows Dragonite to survive Mega Floette's Moonblast and Mega Froslass's Blizzard, giving Dragonite a turn to retaliate. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Due to its typing and Speed tier, Dragonite can often struggle into faster Fairy and Ice-types like Mega Floette, Mega Froslass, and Alolan Ninetales; the latter two are also able to set up Aurora Veil to further dampen Dragonite's damage. However, Dragonite can hit bulkless variants of Mega Floette and Alolan Ninetales with Fire Punch to put them into range of Extreme Speed if holding Life Orb. Without Multiscale, opposing Dragon-types like Hydreigon and Garchomp can easily outspeed and threaten a KO on Dragonite. Garchomp partnered with another faster attacker can break Dragonite even through Multiscale. As Dragonite heavily utilizes Extreme Speed to finish off foes, Farigiraf can stop Dragonite from fulfilling its role as a cleaner due to Armor Tail. As a physical attacker lacking spread moves, Dragonite can struggle to pick off its intended targets if they are protected by Rage Powder from partners like Sinistcha and Mega Scovillain. Due to Spicy Extract, Mega Scovillain completely throws off Dragonite's offensive presence; not only does the resultant burn severely weaken Dragonite's physical attacks, but it also breaks Multiscale, allowing its partner to set up and finish Dragonite off. Good Partners and Synergies: Poison-types like Mega Gengar and Sneasler can eliminate faster Fairy-types for Dragonite, while Dragonite complements them defensively with its immunity to Ground. Sneasler in particular can offer Fake Out pressure to allow Dragonite more easily deal with faster threats like Garchomp while also possibly using Coaching to boost Dragonite. Steel-types like Kingambit likewise help Dragonite pressure opposing Fairy-types and excel into opposing Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, giving Dragonite more freedom to run Low Kick over Fire Punch. Due to its powerful Dark-type STAB moves and low Speed, Kingambit is also a great deterrent for opposing Farigiraf from switching into Dragonite to block Extreme Speed or setting up Trick Room. In return, Dragonite helps eliminate opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, and Sneasler. Dragonite also greatly appreciates Tailwind, which allows it to outspeed other Dragon-types and also lowers its reliance on Extreme Speed to pick up KOs. Whimsicott is a natural partner, as it resists STAB moves from the likes of Garchomp and Hydreigon, allowing it to come in on attacks intended for Dragonite or, if Dragonite uses Protect, its partner Whimsicott also capitalizes on Fairy Aura from opposing Mega Floette and can assist in putting it in the range of Extreme Speed with Moonblast.

Mega Floette's high Special Defense and Special Attack stats allow it to be a strong Calm Mind sweeper, with decent physical bulk to patch matchups against Pokemon such as Sneasler and Kingambit. Its Fairy Aura ability allows it to threaten Garchomp, Mega Tyranitar, and Dragonite even without any boosts. Mega Floette's respectable base Speed can also allow it to outspeed Mega Charizard Y and Speed tie with Garchomp. ** Moonblast vs. Draining Kiss**: Moonblast allows Mega Floette to OHKO uninvested Sneasler most of the time, as well as 2HKOing Archaludon. It consistently deals high damage, whereas Draining Kiss needs Calm Mind boosts to really be effective, notably failing to OHKO Garchomp without any boosts. However, Draining Kiss can allow Mega Floette to recover some health after spending time setting up. This can allow it to take an attack like Dire Claw from Sneasler without being permanently crippled. Calm Mind vs. Light of Ruin: Calm Mind allows Mega Floette to become very hard to remove for metagame threats such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Raichu Y, and Archaludon. The offensive boost allows Mega Floette to OHKO Kingambit with Moonblast at +1 and almost always 2HKO specially defensive Incineroar with Dazzling Gleam at +1. Light of Ruin can allow it to OHKO threats such as Archaludon and Kingambit, as well as dealing devastating damage to even resisted targets, such as Mega Gengar. Light of Ruin deals similar damage to +1 Moonblast but has considerable consequences to Mega Floette's longevity on the field due to the large amount of recoil damage. SP Spreads 10 HP / 32 Def / 15 SpA / 9 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Mega Floette to outspeed all Adamant non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and almost always OHKO bulky Basculegion-M with Moonblast at +1. It is also able to OHKO Kingambit with Moonblast at +1 while always surviving Iron Head from the aforementioned Kingambit and Dire Claw from Sneasler. 10 HP / 17 Def / 23 SpA / 16 Spe with Modest: The extra Speed investment allows Mega Floette to outrun Modest Archaludon and Jolly Mega Tyranitar while still surviving Dire Claw from Jolly Sneasler. 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Timid: This spread pairs well with Whimsicott's Tailwind, as Mega Floette needs to move first to account for the lack of defensive investment. Whimsicott is usually chosen over a different Tailwind setter like Aerodactyl due to Whimsicott's synergy with Mega Floette's Fairy Aura. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Given Mega Floette's lack of coverage, it struggles to deal with Poison- and Fire-types such as Glimmora and Mega Charizard Y, the former of which is also able to 2HKO it with Sludge Bomb. Physical threats such as Kingambit and Sneasler, which have their Fairy-type weakness covered by their secondary typing, can provide issues for Mega Floette due to its mediocre Defense. Basculegion-M, especially Mystic Water variants, are able to deal massive damage to Floette-E with Wave Crash. Opposing Mega Evolutions: Mega Charizard Y can overpower Mega Floette despite any boosts provided by Calm Mind due to the power boost from the sun, while Mega Delphox is able to resist its attacks and hit through Special Defense boosts with Psyshock. Mega Metagross can OHKO Mega Floette with Iron Head, and Mega Gengar can trap it on the field and 2HKO it with Sludge Bomb. Mega Mawile resists Floette-E's moves and can retaliate with Iron Head while also being able to use Fairy Aura against its partners with Play Rough. Mega Swampert can deal huge damage to Floette-E with rain-boosted Wave Crash. Other Threats: Toxapex is able to use its high Special Defense alongside its Poison typing to stall out Mega Floette, dealing fixed damage with Infestation and Toxic. This is especially strong against Calm Mind sets, as they usually lack an immediately strong single-target move in the form of Light of Ruin, which could deal a respectable chunk of damage to Toxapex. Calm Mind sets also need to worry about Whimsicott, as its Encore can lock Mega Floette into an unfortunate move choice such as Calm Mind or an unboosted Draining Kiss. Whimsicott's Encore also cannot be redirected by an allied Rage Powder user such as Sinistcha. Furthermore, Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Excadrill are able to play around Calm Mind's Special Defense boosts through either Nasty Plot or physical attacks and OHKO Mega Floette with Make It Rain and Iron Head while resisting its attacks. Good Partners and Synergies: Calm Mind Mega Floette appreciates partners that can support its longevity, such as Incineroar with Intimidate and Fake Out and Sinistcha with Hospitality and Life Dew. Sinistcha is also able to set Trick Room, which can allow Mega Floette to outspeed faster threats such as Sneasler, Mega Swampert in the rain, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. Meanwhile, Incineroar is able to use Flare Blitz to OHKO most Gholdengo and Whimsicott. In addition to its offensive presence, Incineroar's defensive typing allows it to take on Mega Delphox, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Metagross or weaken them with Parting Shot and, in Metagross's case, Intimidate. Specialized Needs: Non-Calm Mind Mega Floette wants to be paired up with other offensive Pokemon, such as Basculegion-M and Kingambit, which are able to cover for Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar, respectively. Both of them also boast a good matchup against Mega Metagross. This set also appreciates speed control, such as Tailwind from Whimsicott. Whimsicott shares an extra synergy with Mega Floette, as Fairy Aura can allow Whimsicott to reach benchmarks such as a 2HKO on uninvested Basculegion-M with Moonblast. Additionally, Fairy Aura-boosted Moonblast from Whimsicott combined with Light of Ruin from Mega Floette can KO Glimmora before it can move if Tailwind is up. Other strong partners are Farigiraf, which also provides speed control and covers Poison-types, and Glimmora, which is able to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Power Gem. Partner Mega Evolutions: Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox are great partners for Mega Floette, as they can be used in matchups that it struggles with such as Mega Metagross, Mega Mawile, and Mega Venusaur. Floette-E can be used against Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar, Mega Staraptor, and Mega Dragonite, Pokemon that Charizard or Delphox would struggle against. Mega Raichu Y fulfills a similar role, being able to take on opposing Mega Charizard Y, Toxapex, and non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

Garchomp, thanks to its strong offense, good coverage against the current format's major threats, and nice Speed tier, cements itself as a top threat in Regulation M-B, offensively checking the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, Incineroar, and Kingambit with ease. Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to threaten Flying-type Pokemon, namely Mega Charizard Y and Mega Aerodactyl. It can also deal considerable damage to Mega Delphox and is Garchomp's only way to hit Whimsicott, which are immune to Earthquake and resist it, respectively. Rock Slide, thanks to Garchomp's high Speed, can be used to fish for flinches, though it is generally an unreliable path to victory. Life Orb: Life Orb allows Garchomp to always OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and OHKO opposing Garchomp with Dragon Claw. Rough Skin: Rough Skin allows Garchomp to punish Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar, while also breaking the Focus Sash of physical attackers such as Kingambit, Sneasler, and Basculegion-M. Other Options Stomping Tantrum: Stomping Tantrum can be run on teams that don't have many Earthquake-immune Pokemon, allowing Garchomp to deal consistent Ground-type damage without threatening its partners. This comes at the cost of either Earthquake or Rock Slide, either limiting Garchomp's offensive capabilities or preventing it from OHKOing Mega Charizard Y. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Ice-type Pokemon like Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales threaten big damage with Blizzard and can lessen Garchomp's damage output with Aurora Veil. Pokemon that commonly run Ice-type coverage, like Mega Metagross and Mega Swampert, also cause issues, as both can outspeed Garchomp — whether it be naturally or through Swift Swim — and OHKO it with Ice Punch, while Mega Swampert is also bulky enough to tank two Dragon Claws. Mega Aerodactyl can do similarly with Ice Fang. Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten Garchomp with Moonblast and Hyper Voice, while Mega Floette has the chance to Speed tie with Garchomp. Whimsicott in particular is problematic, as it is also resistant to Ground-type attacks and can use Tailwind to allow Pokemon that Garchomp usually outspeeds, like Sylveon and most Mega Floette, to KO it before it can move. Mega Scovillain provides issues for Garchomp, easily redirecting its attacks and burning it. Incineroar can also weaken Garchomp with Intimidate, while Fake Out significantly hinders Garchomp's potential momentum. Opposing Dragon-type Pokemon like Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can either outspeed Garchomp or withstand it for a turn and OHKO it with Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is immune to Garchomp's Earthquake and pressures Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Weather Ball, OHKOing the Ice-type Pokemon and outdamaging the Fairy-types. Mega Charizard Y also threatens Mega Metagross with Weather Ball or Heat Wave and, when the sun is up, Mega Swampert with Solar Beam. Mega Charizard Y can also pressure Mega Scovillain without fear of being burnt. Garchomp, in return, hits the many Rock-type Pokemon that threaten Mega Charizard Y, like Mega Tyranitar and Glimmora, with Earthquake while also threatening opposing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. Whimsicott provides Tailwind, allowing Garchomp to outspeed other Garchomp as well as Hydreigon and threaten to OHKO them with Dragon Claw. Moonblast can also be used to threaten Dragon-type Pokemon, as a double target with Moonblast and Dragon Claw OHKOes Mega Dragonite. In return, Garchomp pressures the likes of Gholdengo and Kingambit, which would otherwise threaten Whimsicott with Make It Rain and Iron Head, respectively. Kingambit threatens Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Iron Head, while both it and Basculegion-M threaten Incineroar with Low Kick and Wave Crash, respectively.

Given its relatively high Attack and Speed stat, Garchomp can afford to use a bulky set. This allows it to stay on the field longer and deal damage consistently throughout a game, all the while still answering top Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit. Earthquake versus Stomping Tantrum: Earthquake deals consistent spread damage but requires Garchomp's ally to either be immune to Earthquake or have Protect in order for it to be safe. Stomping Tantrum avoids this issue, though it limits Garchomp's ability to spread damage. Rock Slide: Rock Slide heavily hits Mega Charizard Y, as well as other Flying-types like Pelipper. Garchomp can fish for flinches, though doing so is unreliable with a set like this because of its lower Speed investment. Sitrus Berry versus Roseli Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing helps Garchomp take hits better, turning the 2HKO from Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat into a 3HKO. Roseli Berry, on the other hand, provides Garchomp the ability to stay on the field against Fairy-types. It lets Garchomp more safely 2HKO the likes of Mega Floette with low bulk investment by using Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum, as Garchomp can now survive Mega Floette's Moonblast. Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar, the former of which will have its Focus Sash broken and become vulnerable to Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum. Rough Skin also punishes Dual Wingbeat from Mega Aerodactyl. Other Options Poison Jab: Poison Jab can be used on Roseli Berry Garchomp to consistently 2HKO Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon, though it calls for dropping Protect, making defensive play harder for a Pokemon that wants to consistently swap around and position well to optimize its time on the field. SP Spreads 23 HP / 18 Atk / 3 SpD / 22 Spe with Adamant: This SP spread, which is designed for Sitrus Berry sets, makes Garchomp capable of surviving Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette and Wave Crash from Adamant Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion-M. It also lets Garchomp have a chance to survive Dragon Claw from opposing Jolly Life Orb Garchomp while optimizing HP for Sitrus Berry recovery. The Speed investment allows Garchomp to outspeed all non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and the rest is dumped into Attack for maximum offense, enabling Dragon Claw to 2HKO Basculegion-M with low bulk investment. 17 HP / 27 Atk / 22 Spe Adamant: This SP spread is meant to be used with Roseli Berry, allowing Garchomp to survive +2 Sucker Punch from Black Glasses Kingambit and turning the 2HKO from Mega Delphox's Psyshock into a 3HKO. Garchomp hits the same Speed benchmark as the above spread. The remaining SPs are dumped into Attack, giving Garchomp's Ground-type STAB moves good odds at 2HKOing uninvested Basculegion-M and guaranteeing them the 2HKO on uninvested Mega Floette. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon give Garchomp trouble, as both examples can easily OHKO non-Roseli Berry variants and can still do so against Roseli Berry variants by using Light of Ruin and Hyper Beam. Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon like Sinistcha and Whimsicott defensively check Garchomp. The former can redirect its attacks with ease and potentially burn it with Matcha Gotcha, while the latter can threaten it with Moonblast and lock it into Protect or an unfavorable move with Encore. Mega Scovillain is another problematic Grass-type, forcing a burn onto Garchomp with the combination of Spicy Spray and Rage Powder. Ice-type Pokemon and Coverage: Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales easily OHKO Garchomp with Blizzard. Mamoswine, although less popular, does so with Icicle Crash and can take out a damaged Garchomp with Ice Shard. Though it's not an Ice-type, Mega Aerodactyl commonly runs Ice Fang specifically to OHKO Garchomp. Dragon-types: Faster Dragon-type Pokemon like offensive or Choice Scarf variants of opposing Garchomp and Choice Scarf variants of Hydreigon threaten huge damage or even an OHKO onto bulky Garchomp with Dragon Claw and Draco Meteor while surviving its Dragon Claw in return. Although it's slower than Garchomp in most cases, Adamant Dragonite OHKOes Garchomp with Dragon Claw, while Mega Dragonite has a chance to do so with Dragon Pulse. Mega Dragonite is even able to tank Garchomp's Dragon Claw thanks to Multiscale. Other Problematic Foes: Corviknight resists Rock Slide and Dragon Claw and is immune to Garchomp's Ground-type attacks, which enables it to set up with Bulk Up right in front of Garchomp. Rotom-Wash does a similar thing; although it doesn't resist Rock Slide and Dragon Claw, it can burn Garchomp with Will-O-Wisp. Mega Staraptor, being immune to Garchomp's Ground-type attacks, can easily switch into one and start using Close Combat, which makes itself much harder to remove, especially for Garchomp. Wide Guard from foes like Toxapex can also be problematic, as they block Earthquake and Rock Slide. Good Partners and Synergies: Whimsicott helps with Garchomp's lack of Speed investment, using Tailwind to let it outspeed Mega Charizard Y and opposing Garchomp and threaten them with Rock Slide and Dragon Claw. Whimsicott also can use Moonblast to hit Mega Staraptor and Dragon-types, OHKOing Hydreigon and Kommo-o. Encore is useful to punish moves such as Calm Mind from Mega Floette and Aurora Veil from Mega Froslass, allowing Garchomp to attack them without worry of being OHKOed. In return, Garchomp hits the many Steel- and Fire-types that threaten Whimsicott such as Gholdengo and Hisuian Arcanine. Basculegion-M helps immensely against the Fairy-types of the format, considering their low Defense. It also deals huge burst damage against walls like Corviknight and Rotom-Wash with Last Respects late-game. Garchomp handles Kingambit for Basculegion-M as well as Mega Charizard Y, which can use Solar Beam to remove Basculegion-M. Dark-types: Kingambit puts pressure on Fairy- and Ice-types with Iron Head while removing Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave. Incineroar is another strong Dark-type partner, using Fake Out to stop Choice Scarf Pokemon like Hydreigon and opposing Garchomp from KOing Garchomp immediately. Incineroar can also hit Grass- and Ice-types hard with Flare Blitz, notably ignoring Spicy Spray from Mega Scovillain thanks to its Fire typing, and can safely bring in Garchomp with Parting Shot without forcing it to expend its Sitrus or Roseli Berry. In return, Garchomp handles Ground-types like Excadrill, as well as opposing Kingambit and Sneasler, relatively well for both of them. Mega Evolutions: Mega Charizard Y is the best Mega Evolution to pair with Garchomp, being immune to Earthquake and threatening the Fairy-, Ice-, and Grass-types that all annoy Garchomp. Garchomp is able to, in return, help against opposing Mega Charizard Y, Mega Delphox, and Mega Tyranitar. Mega Floette is another good partner for Garchomp, dealing with all the Dragon-types that Garchomp dislikes, while Garchomp handles Poison- and Steel-types like Glimmora and Gholdengo that Mega Floette can't.

Given its relatively high Attack and Speed stat, Garchomp can afford to use a bulky set. This allows it to stay on the field longer and deal damage consistently throughout a game, all the while still answering top Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit. Earthquake versus Stomping Tantrum: Earthquake deals consistent spread damage but requires Garchomp's ally to either be immune to Earthquake or have Protect in order for it to be safe. Stomping Tantrum avoids this issue, though it limits Garchomp's ability to spread damage. Rock Slide: Rock Slide heavily hits Mega Charizard Y, as well as other Flying-types like Pelipper. Garchomp can fish for flinches, though doing so is unreliable with a set like this because of its lower Speed investment. Sitrus Berry versus Roseli Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing helps Garchomp take hits better, turning the 2HKO from Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat into a 3HKO. Roseli Berry, on the other hand, provides Garchomp the ability to stay on the field against Fairy-types. It lets Garchomp more safely 2HKO the likes of Mega Floette with low bulk investment by using Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum, as Garchomp can now survive Mega Floette's Moonblast. Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar, the former of which will have its Focus Sash broken and become vulnerable to Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum. Rough Skin also punishes Dual Wingbeat from Mega Aerodactyl. Other Options Poison Jab: Poison Jab can be used on Roseli Berry Garchomp to consistently 2HKO Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon, though it calls for dropping Protect, making defensive play harder for a Pokemon that wants to consistently swap around and position well to optimize its time on the field. SP Spreads 23 HP / 18 Atk / 3 SpD / 22 Spe with Adamant: This SP spread, which is designed for Sitrus Berry sets, makes Garchomp capable of surviving Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette and Wave Crash from Adamant Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion-M. It also lets Garchomp have a chance to survive Dragon Claw from opposing Jolly Life Orb Garchomp while optimizing HP for Sitrus Berry recovery. The Speed investment allows Garchomp to outspeed all non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and the rest is dumped into Attack for maximum offense, enabling Dragon Claw to 2HKO Basculegion-M with low bulk investment. 17 HP / 27 Atk / 22 Spe Adamant: This SP spread is meant to be used with Roseli Berry, allowing Garchomp to survive +2 Sucker Punch from Black Glasses Kingambit and turning the 2HKO from Mega Delphox's Psyshock into a 3HKO. Garchomp hits the same Speed benchmark as the above spread. The remaining SPs are dumped into Attack, giving Garchomp's Ground-type STAB moves good odds at 2HKOing uninvested Basculegion-M and guaranteeing them the 2HKO on uninvested Mega Floette. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon give Garchomp trouble, as both examples can easily OHKO non-Roseli Berry variants and can still do so against Roseli Berry variants by using Light of Ruin and Hyper Beam. Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon like Sinistcha and Whimsicott defensively check Garchomp. The former can redirect its attacks with ease and potentially burn it with Matcha Gotcha, while the latter can threaten it with Moonblast and lock it into Protect or an unfavorable move with Encore. Mega Scovillain is another problematic Grass-type, forcing a burn onto Garchomp with the combination of Spicy Spray and Rage Powder. Ice-type Pokemon and Coverage: Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales easily OHKO Garchomp with Blizzard. Mamoswine, although less popular, does so with Icicle Crash and can take out a damaged Garchomp with Ice Shard. Though it's not an Ice-type, Mega Aerodactyl commonly runs Ice Fang specifically to OHKO Garchomp. Dragon-types: Faster Dragon-type Pokemon like offensive or Choice Scarf variants of opposing Garchomp and Choice Scarf variants of Hydreigon threaten huge damage or even an OHKO onto bulky Garchomp with Dragon Claw and Draco Meteor while surviving its Dragon Claw in return. Although it's slower than Garchomp in most cases, Adamant Dragonite OHKOes Garchomp with Dragon Claw, while Mega Dragonite has a chance to do so with Dragon Pulse. Mega Dragonite is even able to tank Garchomp's Dragon Claw thanks to Multiscale. Other Problematic Foes: Corviknight resists Rock Slide and Dragon Claw and is immune to Garchomp's Ground-type attacks, which enables it to set up with Bulk Up right in front of Garchomp. Rotom-Wash does a similar thing; although it doesn't resist Rock Slide and Dragon Claw, it can burn Garchomp with Will-O-Wisp. Mega Staraptor, being immune to Garchomp's Ground-type attacks, can easily switch into one and start using Close Combat, which makes itself much harder to remove, especially for Garchomp. Wide Guard from foes like Toxapex can also be problematic, as they block Earthquake and Rock Slide. Good Partners and Synergies: Whimsicott helps with Garchomp's lack of Speed investment, using Tailwind to let it outspeed Mega Charizard Y and opposing Garchomp and threaten them with Rock Slide and Dragon Claw. Whimsicott also can use Moonblast to hit Mega Staraptor and Dragon-types, OHKOing Hydreigon and Kommo-o. Encore is useful to punish moves such as Calm Mind from Mega Floette and Aurora Veil from Mega Froslass, allowing Garchomp to attack them without worry of being OHKOed. In return, Garchomp hits the many Steel- and Fire-types that threaten Whimsicott such as Gholdengo and Hisuian Arcanine. It also deals huge burst damage against walls like Corviknight and Rotom-Wash with Last Respects late-game. Garchomp handles Kingambit for Basculegion-M as well as Mega Charizard Y, which can use Solar Beam to remove Basculegion-M. Mega Floette is another good partner for Garchomp, dealing with all the Dragon-types that Garchomp dislikes, while Garchomp handles Poison- and Steel-types like Glimmora and Gholdengo that Mega Floette can't.

Incineroar is able to use its stellar supportive moves and ability, strong defensive typing, and solid stats to be one of the best Pokemon in Regulation M-B, tanking attacks from the likes of Kingambit and Mega Charizard Y while shutting down and even offensively threatening Sinistcha and Mega Delphox. Throat Chop: Throat Chop is able to not only deal solid damage but also shut off Hyper Voice from Sylveon, forcing it to either use Hyper Beam, Quick Attack, or Detect. Throat Chop also blocks Parting Shot from opposing Incineroar and Grimmsnarl, preventing them from gaining momentum or breaking out of Shadow Tag from Mega Gengar. Parting Shot: Thanks to Incineroar's relatively low Speed, it can usually move last to safely bring in frailer allies like Mega Gengar and Venusaur with Parting Shot. Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry increases Incineroar's longevity, letting it almost always avoid a 2HKO from Calm Mind Mega Floette's Moonblast. Intimidate: Intimidate allows Incineroar to survive Close Combat from Sneasler while keeping foes like Mega Metagross and Mega Mawile under control. Other Options Helping Hand: Helping Hand lets Incineroar boost the damage of partners like Mega Blastoise. However, Incineroar would have to drop Throat Chop, which worsens its matchup against Ghost-types, especially Ceruledge, a Pokemon that it normally performs well against, and makes it harder to damage foes like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox. Passho Berry: Passho Berry is a good option against the variety of Water-type Pokemon like Basculegion-M, Mega Swampert, and +2 Special Attack Milotic, though it harms Incineroar's longevity significantly in other matchups. Darkest Lariat: Darkest Lariat can replace Throat Chop to deal slightly more damage, having higher odds to OHKO uninvested Mega Delphox, and ignore Archaludon's Defense boosts from Stamina, though Incineroar loses the utility of shutting down Hyper Voice from Sylveon as well as Parting Shot from opposing Incineroar. Protect: Protect is generally only used alongside Mega Gengar, as it allows Incineroar to help stall out turns of Perish Song. This comes at the cost of dropping either Flare Blitz or Throat Chop. Protect can also be used alongside Toxapex to rack up chip damage from Toxic poison and Infestation. SP Spreads 32 HP / 11 SpD / 23 Spe with Careful: The Speed investment on this spread allows Incineroar to outspeed Focus Sash Kingambit as well as most opposing Incineroar, allowing it to use Fake Out first most of the time. With the bulk investment, it survives +1 Moonblast from Calm Mind Mega Floette and rain-boosted Weather Ball from bulky Pelipper sets, all while having optimized HP for Sitrus Berry recovery. 32 HP / 23 Def / 11 SpD with Impish: This spread leans more into Incineroar's Defense, letting it survive Close Combat from Jolly Sneasler and +2 Low Kick from Kingambit. The rest of the SPs are dumped into Special Defense to give Incineroar better odds at surviving Hyper Beam from Sylveon. 30 HP / 17 Def / 19 SpD with Sassy: With the given SP spread, Incineroar is able to survive Light of Ruin from Modest Mega Floette, avoid a 2HKO from Life Orb Garchomp's Earthquake when accounting for Sitrus Berry, and almost always survive Wave Crash from Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M after it's affected by Intimidate. A Sassy nature is used to make Incineroar a more effective slow pivot, enabling it to safely get in allies like Mega Gengar for Perish Trap strategies. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Fighting-types like Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can easily threaten Incineroar with Close Combat. Sneasler commonly holds the White Herb, which reverts the Attack drops from Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot and enables it to OHKO Incineroar with Close Combat, while Mega Staraptor can turn Intimidate's and Parting Shot's Attack drops into boosts thanks to Contrary. Kingambit and Annihilape can use Defiant to gain an Attack boost from Intimidate or Parting Shot. The former can retaliate with Low Kick, which, assuming Incineroar moves first, has good odds to KO Incineroar when accounting for Flare Blitz's recoil damage, and the latter always OHKOes it with Close Combat. Mega Raichu Y can use Fake Out before Incineroar can use its own Fake Out and then can use Focus Blast to threaten huge damage onto it. Water-type Pokemon: Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert are able to deal big damage to Incineroar with Wave Crash or OHKO it when the rain is set up. Basculegion-M can even OHKO Incineroar without the rain when holding Mystic Water or Life Orb, and it's also immune to Fake Out. Not only can Pelipper and Politoed set up the rain to enable the aforementioned foes to OHKO Incineroar, but they can also deal heavy damage to it with Weather Ball. Milotic can take Intimidate or Parting Shot and receive a Special Attack boost thanks to Competitive, which lets it easily 2HKO Incineroar with a +2 Scald or Muddy Water, while Rotom-Wash can use Hydro Pump to 2HKO Incineroar. Mega Blastoise is able to easily OHKO Incineroar with Water Spout, especially after Shell Smash is used, while shrugging off any damage that Incineroar can deal. Toxapex can poison Incineroar with Toxic, heavily lowering its longevity and putting it on a timer, while not being too annoyed by Parting Shot. Ground-type Pokemon and Moves: Ground-types like Garchomp and Excadrill are able to threaten big damage into Incineroar with Earthquake, Stomping Tantrum, and High Horsepower. Garchomp even punishes Incineroar using Fake Out thanks to Rough Skin. Mega Venusaur can use Earth Power to deal solid damage to Incineroar while having Thick Fat to reduce the damage of Flare Blitz, and it is commonly run alongside rain or dual screens, both of which further reduce Flare Blitz's damage output. Rock-type Pokemon: Rock-type Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Tyranitar, and Hisuian Arcanine all solidly threaten Incineroar with Rock Slide and Head Smash, even if they are affected by Intimidate. Mega Tyranitar in particular resists both of Incineroar's STAB attacks and can potentially offset Attack drops from Intimidate with Dragon Dance. Glimmora, as opposed to other Rock-type Pokemon in the format, is not affected by Intimidate and can use Power Gem to threaten Incineroar. Good Partners and Synergies: Despite sharing a Fighting-type weakness with Incineroar, Kingambit is an excellent ally able to threaten Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch before it can move. Additionally, it does huge damage to Rock-type Pokemon with Iron Head and handles opposing Kingambit with Low Kick. Incineroar can, in return, weaken the damage output of Pokemon like Garchomp and opposing Incineroar while beating Ceruledge. Sneasler is able to threaten opposing Kingambit and Rock-types with Close Combat while forming a strong Fake Out core with Incineroar. Garchomp is another great partner against Rock-type Pokemon, and it even does well against Kingambit, Excadrill, Toxapex, and, when provided with proper speed control, opposing Garchomp. Speed Control Setters: Sinistcha is able to 2HKO most Water-type Pokemon with Matcha Gotcha and can redirect Water-, Ground-, and Fighting-type attacks with Rage Powder. Thanks to Incineroar's Fake Out, Sinistcha can easily set up Trick Room. Incineroar also threatens Steel-type Pokemon like Gholdengo and Mega Mawile, both of which may give Sinistcha trouble. Whimsicott is another Grass-type partner that can swap into Water-, Ground-, and Fighting-type attacks while having Moonblast to threaten Garchomp and Encore to punish foes that use Protect to avoid Incineroar's Fake Out. Farigiraf is able to threaten Fighting-type Pokemon like Sneasler with Psychic while using Thunderbolt to threaten Water-type Pokemon like Basculegion-M and Pelipper. In return, Incineroar's Fake Out to can help Farigiraf set up Trick Room, while Flare Blitz and Throat Chop threaten Gholdengo and Mega Metagross, Pokemon that threaten Farigiraf with huge damage while taking little from it. Mega Evolutions: Mega Charizard Y sets up the sun, enabling Incineroar to OHKO Kingambit and survive Wave Crash from even Life Orb Adaptability Basculegion-M. It also carries Solar Beam, which threatens Water-type Pokemon like the aforementioned Basculegion-M. In return, Incineroar provides Intimidate support, letting Mega Charizard Y survive attacks like Rock Slide from Life Orb Garchomp and Accelerock from Lycanroc-D. Mega Floette is able to threaten Mega Tyranitar, Garchomp, and Fighting-type Pokemon like Annihilape with Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam while blasting through neutral targets like Rotom-W. In return, Fake Out and Intimidate from Incineroar can help Mega Floette attack safely or set up with Calm Mind, Parting Shot can bring in Mega Floette safely, and Flare Blitz can threaten the Steel-type Pokemon that Mega Floette fears. Thanks to Incineroar's incredible defensive profile, it is an amazing partner for Mega Gengar. Incineroar can help it stall out Perish Song turns by pivoting around and weakening foes with Parting Shot and Intimidate while preventing them from taking out Mega Gengar by using Fake Out. Many of the big threats to Mega Gengar, like Basculegion-M and Garchomp, are weakened by Intimidate. Gengar also appreciates its support against Psychic-type attacks like Psychic from Farigiraf, which Incineroar can easily swap into. In return, Mega Gengar is an amazing answer to the plethora of Fighting-type Pokemon that threaten Incineroar. Incineroar can perform various tricks with Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag; for example, Incineroar can use Parting Shot on the same turn Gengar swaps out to pivot it back in, enabling Gengar to keep the trap going while protecting it from harm. Setup Pokemon like Mega Delphox and Mega Blastoise heavily appreciate the support from Incineroar, as Intimidate and Fake Out make it easier for them to set up with Nasty Plot and Shell Smash.

Kingambit is one of the top threats of Regulation M-B, trading damage comfortably and threatening many top threats such as Basculegion-M, Gholdengo, and Mega Floette. Additionally, Kingambit's typing allows it to defensively answer both Gholdengo's and Mega Metagross's STAB moves as well as making it immune to Toxapex's Toxic. Items: Black Glasses allows Kingambit to deal more damage with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch always OHKOes Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and can OHKO Mega Froslass in the snow most of the time. Focus Sash allows Kingambit to sacrifice its defenses to patch up its lackluster Speed, and it enables Kingambit to survive strong attacks such as Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball. Focus Sash Kingambit is utilized on Tailwind teams to take advantage of any Speed investment. Chople Berry lets Kingambit retain its great bulk and utilize Trick Room better while surviving Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar, and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast. Chople Berry Kingambit can also survive Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, but this isn't guaranteed. Abilities: Defiant allows Kingambit to punish Incineroar's and Staraptor's Intimidate, Milotic's Icy Wind, and even the Special Attack drops from Mega Floette's and Whimsicott's Moonblast. Defiant's boost lets Kingambit always OHKO Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave. Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch makes up for Kingambit's poor Speed and threatens faster Pokemon such as Basculegion-M. Sucker Punch is also useful for late-game one-on-ones, as it pressures the opponent to guess whether Kingambit will choose Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch. Iron Head versus Swords Dance versus Low Kick: Iron Head is used to threaten Mega Floette and Sylveon while dealing decent damage to Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and chunking Tyranitar. Swords Dance turns Kingambit into a setup sweeper; it's typically seen with Black Glasses to add another damage multiplier. A Black Glasses- and Swords Dance-boosted Sucker Punch can OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp. Low Kick is used to threaten opposing Kingambit, Incineroar, and Tyranitar. However, Kingambit cannot damage Fairy-types or Sneasler much if it opts for Low Kick. Protect versus Low Kick: Low Kick is an alternative coverage move if Kingambit doesn't necessarily need Protect on its team. This comes at the cost of Kingambit being unable to shield itself from Fake Out and attacks that may threaten it. Focus Sash and Chople Berry are typically seen with this option, because it allows Kingambit to trade damage more comfortably. Other Options Life Orb: Life Orb pushes Kingambit's power to the absolute limit, at the cost of some recoil. A Life Orb-boosted Sucker Punch OHKOes some Gholdengo. SP Spreads 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def with Adamant: This is Kingambit's primary SP spread. Chople Berry and Black Glasses are typically seen with this spread. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread is used with a set utilizing four attacks and Focus Sash, allowing Kingambit to outspeed bulkier Pelipper and some Incineroar. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Even with Chople Berry, Kingambit does not have the best matchup against Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar threaten to OHKO Kingambit as well, and without speed control, Tyranitar will beat Black Glasses Kingambit. Despite Kingambit's ability acting as a check to Incineroar's Intimidate, its Flare Blitz still threatens Kingambit. Without Iron Head or a Swords Dance boost, Mega Floette and Sylveon will outlast Kingambit in damage trades. Additionally, Mega Floette's Light of Ruin will OHKO non-Focus Sash Kingambit. Mega Charizard Y is faster than Kingambit and will threaten to OHKO it, while Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Garchomp are Ground-types that threaten Kingambit super effectively while also outspeeding it. Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M and Sinistcha can block Sneasler's Close Combat, and the former can OHKO Sneasler with Wave Crash while resisting Dire Claw. Furthermore, Basculegion-M also threatens Incineroar for huge damage even with Intimidate. Sinistcha can set up Trick Room for Kingambit, allowing Kingambit to outspeed and beat threats to Sinistcha, such as non-Focus Sash Basculegion and Mega Froslass. Sneasler can threaten opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat and provide Fake Out support so that Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance safely. Kingambit can deal with Gholdengo and Mega Metagross in return. Mega Charizard Y can support Kingambit teams with its immunity to Garchomp's Earthquake and resistance to Incineroar's Flare Blitz, opposing Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Mega Staraptor's Close Combat while pressuring opposing Kingambit and Mega Scovillain. In return, Kingambit can cover Mega Aerodactyl for it. Garchomp can threaten opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Tyranitar. Kingambit boasts an excellent matchup against Mega Froslass, as well as Alolan Ninetales if it is running Iron Head, both of which Garchomp usually struggles with. However, Garchomp cannot safely use Earthquake next to Kingambit. Mega Floette and Sylveon can threaten opposing Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Mega Staraptor. Their weakness to Poison-type moves such as Sneasler's Poison Jab and Venusaur's Sludge Bomb is in turn patched up by Kingambit's Steel typing.
