Kingambit is one of the top threats of Regulation M-B, trading damage comfortably and threatening many top threats such as Basculegion-M, Gholdengo, and Mega Floette. Additionally, Kingambit's typing allows it to defensively answer both Gholdengo's and Mega Metagross's STAB moves as well as making it immune to Toxapex's Toxic. Items: Black Glasses allows Kingambit to deal more damage with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch always OHKOes Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and can OHKO Mega Froslass in the snow most of the time. Focus Sash allows Kingambit to sacrifice its defenses to patch up its lackluster Speed, and it enables Kingambit to survive strong attacks such as Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball. Focus Sash Kingambit is utilized on Tailwind teams to take advantage of any Speed investment. Chople Berry lets Kingambit retain its great bulk and utilize Trick Room better while surviving Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar, and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast. Chople Berry Kingambit can also survive Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, but this isn't guaranteed. Abilities: Defiant allows Kingambit to punish Incineroar's and Staraptor's Intimidate, Milotic's Icy Wind, and even the Special Attack drops from Mega Floette's and Whimsicott's Moonblast. Defiant's boost lets Kingambit always OHKO Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave. Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch makes up for Kingambit's poor Speed and threatens faster Pokemon such as Basculegion-M. Sucker Punch is also useful for late-game one-on-ones, as it pressures the opponent to guess whether Kingambit will choose Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch. Iron Head versus Swords Dance versus Low Kick: Iron Head is used to threaten Mega Floette and Sylveon while dealing decent damage to Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and chunking Tyranitar. Swords Dance turns Kingambit into a setup sweeper; it's typically seen with Black Glasses to add another damage multiplier. A Black Glasses- and Swords Dance-boosted Sucker Punch can OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp. Low Kick is used to threaten opposing Kingambit, Incineroar, and Tyranitar. However, Kingambit cannot damage Fairy-types or Sneasler much if it opts for Low Kick. Protect versus Low Kick: Low Kick is an alternative coverage move if Kingambit doesn't necessarily need Protect on its team. This comes at the cost of Kingambit being unable to shield itself from Fake Out and attacks that may threaten it. Focus Sash and Chople Berry are typically seen with this option, because it allows Kingambit to trade damage more comfortably. Other Options Life Orb: Life Orb pushes Kingambit's power to the absolute limit, at the cost of some recoil. A Life Orb-boosted Sucker Punch OHKOes some Gholdengo. SP Spreads 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def with Adamant: This is Kingambit's primary SP spread. Chople Berry and Black Glasses are typically seen with this spread. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread is used with a set utilizing four attacks and Focus Sash, allowing Kingambit to outspeed bulkier Pelipper and some Incineroar. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Even with Chople Berry, Kingambit does not have the best matchup against Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar threaten to OHKO Kingambit as well, and without speed control, Tyranitar will beat Black Glasses Kingambit. Despite Kingambit's ability acting as a check to Incineroar's Intimidate, its Flare Blitz still threatens Kingambit. Without Iron Head or a Swords Dance boost, Mega Floette and Sylveon will outlast Kingambit in damage trades. Additionally, Mega Floette's Light of Ruin will OHKO non-Focus Sash Kingambit. Mega Charizard Y is faster than Kingambit and will threaten to OHKO it, while Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Garchomp are Ground-types that threaten Kingambit super effectively while also outspeeding it. Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M and Sinistcha can block Sneasler's Close Combat, and the former can OHKO Sneasler with Wave Crash while resisting Dire Claw. Furthermore, Basculegion-M also threatens Incineroar for huge damage even with Intimidate. Sinistcha can set up Trick Room for Kingambit, allowing Kingambit to outspeed and beat threats to Sinistcha, such as non-Focus Sash Basculegion and Mega Froslass. Sneasler can threaten opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat and provide Fake Out support so that Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance safely. Kingambit can deal with Gholdengo and Mega Metagross in return. Mega Charizard Y can support Kingambit teams with its immunity to Garchomp's Earthquake and resistance to Incineroar's Flare Blitz, opposing Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Mega Staraptor's Close Combat while pressuring opposing Kingambit and Mega Scovillain. In return, Kingambit can cover Mega Aerodactyl for it. Garchomp can threaten opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Tyranitar. Kingambit boasts an excellent matchup against Mega Froslass, as well as Alolan Ninetales if it is running Iron Head, both of which Garchomp usually struggles with. However, Garchomp cannot safely use Earthquake next to Kingambit. Mega Floette and Sylveon can threaten opposing Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Mega Staraptor. Their weakness to Poison-type moves such as Sneasler's Poison Jab and Venusaur's Sludge Bomb is in turn patched up by Kingambit's Steel typing.

The set for Lycanroc-D does not significantly change from Regulation M-A to M-B, nor does its teammates and method of play. To see the analysis information, please refer to the Regulation M-A analysis.

Mamoswine is a very threatening attacker due to its high Attack, immunity to Intimidate, and STAB combination that allows it to threaten many common Pokemon including Incineroar, Sinistcha, Garchomp, and Mega Aerodactyl. Ice Shard: Ice Shard is a very powerful priority option against Garchomp. It isn't able to OHKO Garchomp, but it can put Garchomp in range of its own Life Orb recoil. Ice Shard is also able to threaten 2HKOs on common Pokemon that are hard to outspeed such as Whimsicott, Mega Aerodactyl, Venusaur, and Choice Scarf Hydreigon. Focus Sash: Focus Sash lets Mamoswine tank the many strong super effective attacks in the format that would OHKO it such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast and retaliate with High Horsepower. Other Options Earthquake: Earthquake can be used over High Horsepower as an alternative Ground-type attack that can deal consistent spread damage and get around redirection. Earthquake should always be used alongside partners with Protect or Ground-immune partners such as Mega Charizard Y and Hydreigon so Mamoswine doesn't hit its partner. Rock Slide: Rock Slide can be used over Icicle Crash, sacrificing strong Ice-type damage for the ability to deal big damage to Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox. Without Rock Slide, Mamoswine has no way of dealing meaningful damage to Mega Delphox. Life Orb: Life Orb can be used over Focus Sash, increasing Mamoswine's damage at the cost of its survivability. Life Orb allows Mamoswine's Ice Shard to always OHKO Garchomp and its Rock-type coverage to always OHKO Mega Charizard Y. It also allows Mamoswine's High Horsepower to OHKO Archaludon and Incineroar. Without Focus Sash, though, Mamoswine loses its ability to beat Pokemon like Sneasler, Gholdengo, and Mega Raichu Y without speed control. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Mamoswine's poor defensive typing and middling Speed make it susceptible to being outsped and 2HKOed by foes that double target it. It is also susceptible to having its Focus Sash broken by priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Basculegion-M's Aqua Jet, making Mamoswine much easier to deal with. Mega Delphox is an incredibly poor matchup for Mamoswine, since it resists Ice, is immune to Ground, and can 2HKO Mamoswine with Heat Wave or set up a Nasty Plot while Mamoswine can't threaten it. Mega Charizard Y similarly can 2HKO Mamoswine with Heat Wave while not being seriously threatened by variants without Rock Slide. Mega Froslass can outspeed and 2HKO Mamoswine with Blizzard or reduce its damage output with Aurora Veil. Mega Scovillain can redirect any of Mamoswine's attacks, burn it with Spicy Spray, and threaten it with Overheat and Giga Drain. Rain teams often feature Pokemon like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M that can threaten Mamoswine, while it can't do much damage back. Rain teams also commonly feature Grimmsnarl with Reflect to reduce Mamoswine's damage output. Rotom-Wash resists Ice, is immune to Ground, and can threaten Mamoswine with Hydro Pump or reduce its damage output with Will-O-Wisp. Corviknight and Milotic are both too bulky for Mamoswine to comfortably 2HKO and can threaten it with Iron Head and Muddy Water, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies: Since Mamoswine is frail and likely won't stay on the field for long, it fits best on hyper offense teams that appreciate its unique STAB combination and ability to deal strong priority damage. Mamoswine is also a great beneficiary of Tailwind from Pokemon like Whimsicott and Mega Aerodactyl thanks to its great damage output. With Tailwind, Mamoswine can outspeed and OHKO Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl, Garchomp, and Sneasler before they can remove its Focus Sash. Mega Charizard Y is an excellent partner for Mamoswine. Mega Charizard Y resists the Grass-, Fire-, and Fighting-type moves that threaten Mamoswine while threatening strong spread damage, shutting off rain, and threatening Pokemon like Mega Froslass, Mega Scovillain, and Corviknight. In return, Mamoswine can threaten common checks to Mega Charizard Y such as Garchomp, Incineroar, Mega Aerodactyl, and Dragonite. Venusaur in the sun can outspeed and threaten Pokemon like Mega Swampert and Basculegion-M. Incineroar resists the Fire-type attacks that threaten Mamoswine and can safely switch in on any of Mega Delphox's attacks, threatening it with Throat Chop. Toxapex can protect Mamoswine from opposing Heat Wave with Wide Guard and trap Pokemon with a poor matchup into Mamoswine on the field with Infestation. Choice Scarf users like Hydreigon and Garchomp can make up for Mamoswine's middling Speed. Hydreigon is stronger against rain teams and Basculegion-M because it resists Water and threatens the latter with its Dark-type STAB attacks, while Garchomp is stronger into Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Raichu Y because of its fast Ground-type damage. Mamoswine can use Ice Shard to put another Pokemon in range of a KO. For example, Mamoswine's Ice Shard into Choice Scarf Garchomp's Rock Slide can KO Mega Aerodactyl before it can move.

Mega Mawile's offensive typing and coverage let it beat metagame staples such as Mega Floette, Tyranitar, and Sneasler. Its low Speed and high Attack let it function as an effective Trick Room sweeper. Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch allows Mega Mawile to OHKO Basculegion-M and get an attack off if it is about to be outsped and OHKOed. It can pick off low-HP foes that were damaged while Trick Room was up. Hyper Cutter vs. Intimidate: Hyper Cutter ignores Intimidate from Incineroar, and Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks Fake Out; together, they greatly improve the matchup against Incineroar. It can also be convenient to have Hyper Cutter against Kingambit to avoid triggering Defiant with Intimidate. Intimidate allows Mega Mawile to be more comfortable against Garchomp and Mega Swampert, surviving Earthquake from either foe at -1 Attack. Mega Evolving Mawile: If running Intimidate, Mega Mawile can delay Mega Evolution to preserve it. This can help a teammate like Farigiraf set up Trick Room in the face of physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Mega Metagross. It can use Protect while preserving Hyper Cutter in case Incineroar switches in later with Intimidate. Other Options Rock Slide: Rock Slide can replace Iron Head to OHKO Mega Charizard Y, assuming Trick Room is active so Mega Charizard Y cannot OHKO it first. Alternatively, if Mega Mawile's partners already cover Mega Charizard Y, it can keep Iron Head to threaten an OHKO on bulky variants of Mega Floette and Sylveon even at -1 Attack. Swords Dance: Swords Dance boosts Mega Mawile's offense to incredible levels; it can OHKO some Mega Charizard Y and Archaludon with Play Rough at +2 Attack. It can punish the opponent for using Protect with both Pokemon to stall out Trick Room. It is reasonable to replace Sucker Punch and try to set up Trick Room so Mega Mawile will attack first anyway. Protect can also be replaced to keep offensive coverage because Mega Mawile wants to attack most turns anyway. Swords Dance can replace Iron Head to keep Protect; +2 Sucker Punch can OHKO many neutral targets like Mega Charizard Y, allowing Mega Mawile to function well outside of Trick Room. SP Spreads 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 SpD with Brave: A Brave nature is meant for Trick Room teams, and it allows Mega Mawile to underspeed the majority of the metagame. The HP investment allows it to survive Earthquake from Adamant Garchomp and 150-Base Power Last Respects from Jolly Basculegion-M. 19 HP / 32 Atk / 15 Spe with Adamant: Mega Mawile can opt for an Adamant nature on teams with a Tailwind setter like Whimsicott. Under Tailwind with this Speed investment, it can outspeed Mega Floette and Garchomp, with the remaining SPs dumped into HP. Teambuilding Fire-type Weaknesses: Mega Charizard Y threatens to OHKO Mega Mawile with Heat Wave or Weather Ball and resists both of its STAB attacks. Incineroar can almost get an OHKO with Flare Blitz and hinders Mega Mawile's damage output with Intimidate. Hisuian Arcanine threatens an OHKO with Flare Blitz and resists Play Rough. Mega Scovillain resists both STAB attacks and can use Rage Powder to essentially guarantee a burn on Mega Mawile while negating Sucker Punch. Torkoal moves before Mega Mawile in Trick Room and threatens an OHKO with any STAB move. Ceruledge baits out Sucker Punch with Bulk Up, OHKOes with Bitter Blade at +1 Attack, and can run Colbur Berry to survive Sucker Punch. Ground-type Weaknesses: Mega Swampert threatens to OHKO Mega Mawile with High Horsepower or deal heavy damage that cannot be redirected with Earthquake. Excadrill is similarly threatening and resists both of Mega Mawile's STAB attacks. Garchomp runs the same attacks and pairs well with Mega Charizard Y to be even more threatening. Trick Room Partners: Farigiraf is a Trick Room setter that also improves a team's matchup against Incineroar. Mega Mawile can help it set Trick Room against physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Garchomp with Intimidate, OHKO Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch, and switch in on Dark-type attacks targeting Farigiraf like Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Incineroar's Throat Chop. Torkoal improves the rain matchup by overwriting rain with Drought and can even run Solar Beam to take care of Mega Swampert. In Trick Room, Mega Mawile can OHKO Garchomp with Play Rough, helping Torkoal, which cannot KO Garchomp quickly. Sinistcha redirects threatening attacks like Mega Swampert's High Horsepower, nearly OHKOes it with Matcha Gotcha, and functions as a Trick Room setter. Beating Fire-types: Basculegion-M beats Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain and has an advantage against Excadrill. Milotic fills a similar role and punishes Incineroar's Intimidate with Competitive and helps against Garchomp with either Ice Beam or Icy Wind. Garchomp and Hydreigon beat most Fire-types and form a strong defensive and offensive core with Mega Mawile, which covers for their Fairy- and Dragon-type weaknesses. Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Raichu Y beats Mega Charizard Y and has a good matchup against Incineroar. Mega Charizard Y has a better chance than Mega Mawile against rain teams and Ground-types. Both of these Mega Evolutions can be used as an alternative to a Trick Room strategy against teams that have strong ways to shut down Trick Room. Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Tyranitar have a great matchup against Fire-types apart from Mega Scovillain, while Mega Aerodactyl specifically has a better matchup against Garchomp than Mega Mawile, and Mega Tyranitar has better chances against weather setters like Torkoal and Mega Charizard Y.

Mega Metagross boasts good stats and a very beneficial ability in Tough Claws, which allow it to spearhead entire matchups with its raw single-target damage while taking out its checks with its various coverage moves. Mega Metagross's useful Steel typing lets it take on the format's Fairy-type Pokemon such as Sylveon and Mega Floette with ease. Iron Head vs. Bullet Punch: On teams without prominent speed control, Bullet Punch is an alternative to Iron Head that allows Mega Metagross to secure a KO on faster Pokemon at low health, such as Aerodactyl, Whimsicott, and Sneasler after activating Focus Sash. Body Press vs. Ice Punch vs. Stomping Tantrum: These moves allow Mega Metagross to beat Kingambit and Incineroar, Garchomp, and Ceruledge, respectively. Choosing a coverage move largely depends on how well Mega Metagross's partners perform against these Pokemon. For example, if Mega Metagross is partnered with a Garchomp, opting for Ice Punch can help Garchomp consistently win a mirror matchup without relying on a Speed tie, while Garchomp already covers Kingambit with Earthquake. Mega Evolving Metagross: With Clear Body, Metagross is able to shrug off Intimidate from Incineroar. As such, if the opponent has an Incineroar, it is wise to delay Metagross's Mega Evolution until Metagross actually attacks or Incineroar has already switched in, as this prevents Incineroar from easily lowering Mega Metagross's Attack stat. SP Spreads 27 Atk / 14 Def / 25 Spe with Jolly: Generally, this SP spread is only worth running if Mega Metagross is also using Body Press. The Defense investment allows it to always OHKO Kingambit with Body Press, while the Speed investment allows it to always outspeed Garchomp and Mega Floette. 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: This SP spread is used when Mega Metagross is running either Stomping Tantrum or Ice Punch, as Body Press cannot consistently OHKO Kingambit without any Defense investment and is thus not worth running. The extra Attack investment allows it to almost always 2HKO uninvested Basculegion-M with Psychic Fangs, even at -1. The Speed investment allows Mega Metagross to outspeed Alolan Ninetales, letting Metagross OHKO it with Iron Head. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Metagross relies on outspeeding and OHKOing its checks. Basculegion-M poses a problem for this gameplan, as Mega Metagross cannot OHKO it with Psychic Fangs, while Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Metagross and threaten an OHKO with 100-Base Power Last Respects. Mega Metagross can beat non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M only if a partner chips it beforehand. Other Mega Evolutions: Mega Delphox resists both of Mega Metagross's STAB moves while outspeeding Mega Metagross and threatening heavy damage with Heat Wave. Bulky Mega Gengar can threaten a KO on Mega Metagross with Shadow Ball after some chip damage while outspeeding it. Mega Swampert can take any attack from Mega Metagross and has a slight chance to OHKO it with High Horsepower or Earthquake, as well as outspeeding it if the rain is up. Mega Charizard Y is also able to survive Psychic Fangs and can retaliate with sun-boosted Heat Wave or Weather Ball, OHKOing Mega Metagross. Coverage Move Trade-offs: As Mega Metagross cannot fit all of its coverage moves onto its set, it is important to be aware of Metagross's negative matchups depending on the selected coverage option and take these into account when building around Metagross. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Metagross is often used on rain teams, as Drizzle or Rain Dance can make Mega Charizard Y reposition or allow Mega Metagross to survive a Heat Wave or Weather Ball. Common rain staples such as Mega Swampert also boast an excellent matchup against Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, and Mega Charizard Y. Additionally, Ice Punch Mega Metagross can cover Garchomp, which would otherwise threaten Archaludon, a rain staple. Mega Metagross as a Matchup Fixer: On other teams, such as those with Mega Charizard Y, Mega Metagross can be used as a secondary Mega Evolution option to handle foes such as Toxapex and opposing weather setters like Mega Tyranitar and Mega Froslass.

With access to the combination of strong reliable Ice-type STAB attacks and a disruptive ability in Snow Warning, Alolan Ninetales is well-equipped to threaten Ground- and Grass-types in the metagame such as Garchomp and Whimsicott; while also hampering opposing sun, sand, and rain cores. Choice Scarf: With a Choice Scarf equipped, Alolan Ninetales is able to outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp, Modest Venusaur with Chlorophyll active, Mega Blastoise after a Shell Smash and Basculegion-M under Tailwind. Alolan Ninetales is then able to eliminate said threats or slow them down with Icy Wind for an ally to deal with. Freeze-Dry: Freeze-Dry allows Alolan Ninetales to deal heavy damage to common Water-type Pokemon such as Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Mega Blastoise. It is also a way for Alolan Ninetales to hit opposing Garchomp while ignoring potential Wide Guard protection from its partner such as Toxapex or Mega Aerodactyl. Icy Wind: Due to Alolan Ninetales’s blistering Speed with a Choice Scarf equipped, it can make use of Icy Wind to slow down targets that it is unable to OHKO on its own, such as Mega Raichu, for its partner to eliminate instead. This also breaks a potential Focus Sash that fast attackers like Venusaur and Sneasler frequently run. Encore: Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to punish defensive plays by locking opposing Pokemon into Protect. Coupled with Alolan Ninetales’s excellent Speed, this can be especially effective against team reliant on setup moves; not only can Alolan Ninetales outspeed and lock Mega Blastoise and Mega Delphox into Shell Smash and Nasty Plot, respectively, but it also heavily punishes Fake Out from their common teammates in Incineroar and Sneasler. Other Options Moonblast: Moonblast gives Alolan Ninetales an option to hit opposing Incineroar and Kingambit and OHKO Hydreigon and Kommo-o. SP Spreads 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: Maximum Speed investment with a Timid nature is mandatory on Choice Scarf Alolan Ninetales as it allows Alolan Ninetales to outspeed speedy Pokemon such as Chlorophyll Venusaur and Mega Blastoise after a Shell Smash. This spread maximizes Alolan Ninetales’s damage, allowing it to more reliably OHKO targets like Mega Swampert. 5 HP / 7 Def / 22 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: Due to the Defense boost it gets from Snow in conjunction with the HP and Defense investment, Alolan Ninetales is able to survive several important attacks like Wave Crash from Adamant Mystic Water Basculegion as well as 150 Base Power Last Respects from Jolly Choice Scarf variants. In addition, this spread allows Alolan Ninetales to switch in more aggressively to snatch weather control; after changing the weather to Snow, it is able to survive the combination of Wave Crash from Swampert and Weather Ball from Pelipper, as well as Heat Wave from common variants of Timid Mega Charizard Y. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: As Alolan Ninetales typically only run Ice-type attacks, Fire-type Pokemon like Ceruledge, Incineroar, and Hisuian Arcanine can switch in while taking minimal damage; and threatening to OHKO Alolan Ninetales with a strong Bitter Blade or Flare Blitz, respectively. Likewise, Steel-type Pokemon such as Kingambit and Mega Mawile take little damage from Alolan Ninetales’s Ice-type attacks while retaliating with a clean OHKO with Iron Head. Kingambit and Mega Mawile are also often run in Trick Room teams, which turn Alolan Ninetales's high Speed into a liability. Due to Defiant, Kingambit can also deter the use of Icy Wind against common allies like Sneasler and Mega Aerodactyl, significantly lowering the effectiveness of Alolan Ninetales in these matchups. Archaludon, despite not resisting Ice, is frequently built to specially bulky, and it can also easily OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Flash Cannon. When locked into Blizzard or Icy Wind, bulky Water-types like Toxapex and Milotic can sit on Alolan Ninetales while it struggles to do anything meaningful in return. Toxapex is able to use Wide Guard to protect its ally from Alolan Ninetales's Blizzard and Icy Wind while also trapping Alolan Ninetales with Infestation, wearing it down while preventing it from swapping out to switch moves. Milotic, much like Kingambit, is able to use Competitive to deter the use of Icy Wind while also having free turns to set up with Coil. Specially bulky Pokemon such as Mega Floette and Sylveon take little damage from Alolan Ninetales, while being able to retaliate with strong spread moves. Poison-type Pokemon such as Sneasler, Glimmora and Mega Gengar, despite typically bring known for being frail, can survive the 2HKO from Alolan Ninetales’ Ice-type STAB moves and threaten huge damage with Dire Claw and Sludge Bomb. Opposing weather setters like Mega Charizard Y, Torkoal, and Mega Tyranitar can switch into any of Alolan Ninetales’ attacks, shutting off the snow, and deal heavy damage in return with Weather Ball and Rock Slide, respectively. Good Partners and Synergies: Dragon-types like Garchomp and Dragonite make for excellent pairings with Alolan Ninetales, resisting Fire-type attacks from opposing Mega Charizard Y and Incineroar and threatening heavy damage into Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Stromping Tantrum and Low Kick or Superpower, respectively. In return, Alolan Ninetales threatens opposing Dragon-types with Blizzard while using Icy Wind to slow down faster foes such as opposing Sneasler and Dragonite for them to take care of. Since Alolan Ninetales does not enjoy facing Trick Room, Kingambit makes for a great partner, as its powerful Dark-type STAB moves threaten common Trick Room setters in Farigiraf and Sinistcha, and its low Speed allows it to be a formidable threat even if Trick Room were to go up. Its access to Defiant is a deterrent for opposing Incineroar while threatening common partners like Mega Gengar and Mega Floette with Kowtow Cleave and Iron Head, respectively. Kingambit also offers valuable coverage against opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar with Low Kick, Gholdengo with Kowtow Cleave and Glimmora with Iron Head, all of which Kingambit, with some speed investment, can outrun after an Icy Wind drop. Alolan Ninetales greatly appreciates defensive pivoting support from allies to be able to play around the Choice Scarf lock. Incineroar makes for a great pairing, as it is able to come in Fire and Steel-type attacks intended for Alolan Ninetales such as Heat Wave from opposing Mega Charizard Y and Iron Head from Mega Metagross. It is then able use to Parting Shot to bring Alolan Ninetales back onto the field should the opponent bring in their Garchomp or Basculegion-M. Mega Gengar complements Alolan Ninetales with providing Shadow Tag and strong single-target damage, trapping foes like Garchomp and Mega Staraptor for Alolan Ninetales to KO while trapping opposing weather setters, preventing them from switching and allowing Alolan Ninetales to be the dominant weather. In return, Mega Gengar benefits from the removal of Garchomp, one of its more problematic matchups. Mega Gengar is also able to take great advantage of Alolan Ninetales’s speed control from Icy Wind, allowing it to outspeed and eliminate threats such as Chlorophyll Venusaur, Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and Mega Delphox with Sludge Bomb and Shadow Ball, respectively. Shadow Tag also takes the ability of Encore to punish defensive plays like Fake Out and Protect to the next level, effectively turning the game into a two Pokemon against one for the duration of Encore. Sneasler is a strong pairing for Alolan Ninetales by threatening Kingambit and Sylveon with Close Combat and Dire Claw, respectively. Alolan Ninetales's Icy Wind allows Sneasler to outspeed and eliminate these targets even under Tailwind. Sneasler also improves Alolan Ninetales’s matchup into sand teams by threatening to OHKO Tyranitar and Excadrill with Close Combat, while Alolan Ninetales can help preserve Sneasler's Focus Sash by removing the chip damage caused by sand. Sneasler also generates Fake Out pressure, which Alolan Ninetales can take advantage of by locking the opposing Pokemon into Protect. Basculegion threatens Fire- and Rock-types that give Alolan Ninetales trouble such as Incineroar, Mega Charizard Y, and Glimmora with Wave Crash, while Last Respects gives it a strong option into Mega Froslass. Alolan Ninetales’s Icy Wind allows Basculegion to outspeed threats such as the aforementioned Mega Charizard Y and Mega Froslass while freeing it to run a more offensive item such as Life Orb or Mystic Water.

Mega Scovillain functions as a support Pokemon, using the combination of Rage Powder and Spicy Spray to essentially guarantee burns on foes like Basculegion-M, Kingambit, and Garchomp. It has offensive options in Overheat and Giga Drain to threaten metagame staples like Kingambit and Basculegion-M. Combining physical damage reduction from burns with Giga Drain and even a Defense or Special Defense boost from Moody before it has Mega Evolved, Mega Scovillain can become difficult to KO. Rage Powder and Spicy Spray: Rage Powder and Spicy Spray is a combination that is typically used early in a game to scare physical attackers and give teammates a chance to set up and take an early lead. Getting a burn on key foes like Basculegion-M can be crucial to winning a game, so Mega Scovillain should be preserved if these foes switch out. Mega Evolving Scovillain: Protect prior to Mega Evolving to accrue stat boosts through Moody. A Defense boost lets it live 200 Base Power Last Respects from Life Orb Basculegion-M, and a Special Defense boost allows it to survive Sludge Bomb from Mega Gengar. A Speed boost allows it to outspeed Sneasler. A Special Attack boost lets it OHKO Kingambit with Overheat. Additionally, delaying Mega Evolution can force an opponent to consider whether a different Mega Evolution is in the back. Other Options Leech Seed: Leech Seed can be run over Giga Drain to increase longevity and improve the matchup against bulky Pokemon like Archaludon and Toxapex. However, it is hard to pass up the value of Giga Drain because it will put Basculegion-M into range for almost any attack to finish it off. SP Spreads 32 HP / 10 Def / 24 SpD with Bold: With the Defense investment, Mega Scovillain survives Dire Claw from Sneasler and 100 Base Power Last Respects from Life Orb Basculegion-M. The remaining SPs are dumped into Special Defense to maximize the chance to survive Weather Ball from Mega Charizard Y, avoid a 2HKO from Blizzard from Mega Froslass's Blizzard, and always survive Hurricane from Vivillon. Teambuilding Fire-type Pokemon: Fire-types like Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y are immune to burns and wall Mega Scovillain's standard set. Mega Charizard Y can threaten an OHKO with Weather Ball, and Incineroar's Fake Out shuts down Rage Powder for a turn, leaving Mega Scovillain's partner vulnerable and Incineroar's partner safe from Spicy Spray. Hisuian Arcanine threatens an OHKO with Head Smash. Rain Teams: Rain teams are often accompanied by Pelipper, which can threaten Mega Scovillain with massive damage using Hurricane and weaken its Overheat with Drizzle, saving its teammates like Venusaur from an OHKO. Mega Swampert OHKOes it with Wave Crash in rain; although Mega Scovillain will burn Mega Swampert, the trade is typically not in Mega Scovillain's favor. Poison-type Pokemon: Mega Gengar threatens an OHKO with Sludge Bomb, and it can take advantage of Mega Scovillain's passive playstyle with Perish Song. Glimmora and Venusaur can deal heavy damage to Mega Scovillain, if not OHKOing it, with Sludge Bomb. None of these Pokemon particularly mind being burned, though chip damage can be helpful to break Glimmora's Focus Sash. Sneasler nearly threatens an OHKO with Dire Claw. Mega Staraptor: Mega Staraptor is often boosted by its partner Whimsicott, which ignores Rage Powder, using Charm. Mega Scovillain can still force a burn on Mega Staraptor, though it faints in the process and Whimsicott can mitigate burn's Attack drop with Charm. Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M is strong against Fire-types in general and can win the damage trade against Mega Swampert. In return, Mega Scovillain keeps it safe from Sucker Punch from Kingambit and Zap Cannon from Mega Raichu Y, burns Kingambit before it can OHKO Basculegion-M, and OHKOes Sinistcha and Venusaur with Overheat. Lycanroc-D is particularly effective against Mega Charizard Y using Rock Slide; unlike Mega Aerodactyl, it does not need to Mega Evolve to do so. Mega Scovillain can help it handle Basculegion-M, redirecting its attacks or putting it in range of Rock Slide with Giga Drain, and Mega Scovillain improves a team's matchup against Garchomp to Lycanroc-D's benefit. Kingambit punishes Intimidate from Incineroar and Staraptor and handles Rock-types like Glimmora with Iron Head and Mega Gengar with Kowtow Cleave. Mega Scovillain's Rage Powder helps Kingambit set up Swords Dance while burning Fighting-type threats like Sneasler. Less Used Partners: Archaludon handles Rock-types, threatens Pelipper and Mega Charizard Y with Electro Shot, and plays better against rain. It appreciates Mega Scovillain's Rage Powder saving it from Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast while burning Sneasler and Mega Swampert, which threaten it with Close Combat and High Horsepower or Earthquake, respectively. Fairy-type attackers like Sylveon improve the matchup against Mega Staraptor. Sylveon appreciates a burn on Sneasler and Overheat's coverage against Steel-types like Gholdengo. Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Froslass can be brought against rain teams to overwrite Pelipper's Drizzle with Snow Warning and is a better option against Mega Staraptor and Modest Mega Gengar. Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Tyranitar are strong options against Fire-types and, for Mega Aerodactyl specifically, Sneasler. For all three of these Mega Pokemon, Mega Scovillain complements them by doing well against Basculegion-M, Kingambit, and Mega Floette.

Sneasler is a fast yet frail offensive support Pokemon that most notably stops incoming attacks with Fake Out, enabling its allies to safely attack or set up. Its STAB combination helps it check prominent threats like Mega Floette, Whimsicott, and Kingambit. Dire Claw: Beyond threatening Fairy-types like Sylveon and Grimmsnarl, Dire Claw's status effects can help turn the tide of a battle in your favor. Protect vs. Quick Guard: Protect is generally used as the final move, but teams that revolve around setup sweepers like Mega Delphox and Mega Blastoise may prefer Sneasler to have Quick Guard. While giving up Sneasler's ability to defend itself is a notable drawback, Quick Guard's protection against priority attacks like Incineroar's Fake Out and Kingambit's Sucker Punch is incredibly useful to keep the aforementioned sweepers unharmed as much as possible. This is especially important for Mega Blastoise, as it needs to be healthy for Water Spout to hit hard. Unburden: Unburden grants Sneasler unparalleled Speed, ensuring that it will move first unless it is interrupted by Fake Out or facing an opposing Unburden-boosted Sneasler. Activating the ability is important to let Sneasler outspeed weather sweepers like Venusaur, Mega Swampert, and Excadrill. Focus Sash vs. White Herb: Opting for Focus Sash ensures the fragile Sneasler will survive at least one hit, though it will make triggering Unburden harder. White Herb sacrifices Focus Sash's insurance for synergy with Close Combat, simultaneously wiping away the defense drops and activating Unburden. It also lets Sneasler thwart Incineroar's and Staraptor's Intimidate once. Other Options Poison Jab and Poison Touch: Poison Jab can be used over Dire Claw if poison's residual damage is more useful for the team than paralysis or sleep. The secondary effect chance can be enhanced with Poison Touch, which also benefits Sneasler's other attacks, though Unburden's Speed boost is often too valuable to sacrifice. Coaching: Coaching can be slotted over Protect to bolster physical allies like Kingambit and Basculegion-M, as the potential of these attackers with a +1 Attack boost can justify the inability to make defensive maneuvers. Rock Slide: Rock Slide threatens the ubiquitous Mega Charizard Y with heavy damage, and with Sneasler's excellent Speed, it can let Sneasler game for flinches in desperate situations. Rock Slide usually replaces Fake Out on Focus Sash sets, as Sneasler can't afford to drop either of its STAB moves. Gunk Shot: Gunk Shot is a somewhat unreliable alternative to Dire Claw that ensures the OHKO on most physically bulky variants of Sylveon and Mega Floette. Notably, an uninvested Gunk Shot still hits harder than a fully invested Dire Claw, which might prove useful for bulky Sneasler variants. SP Spreads 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly or Adamant: A Jolly nature lets Sneasler outspeed Whimsicott and Modest variants of Mega Delphox and Mega Froslass. An Adamant nature ensures Sneasler OHKOes maximum HP Sylveon with Dire Claw and makes it possible to OHKO Chople Berry Kingambit with Close Combat. 29 HP / 19 Def / 18 Spe with Jolly: A bulky spread can enable Sneasler to survive attacks it otherwise would not without investment, which helps incentivize the use of White Herb. This spread guarantees survival against Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast and grants a good chance to avoid the 2HKO from Adamant Life Orb Dragonite's Extreme Speed, while the Speed investment ensures Sneasler outspeeds Jolly Garchomp and opposing Adamant Sneasler. Even with no Attack investment, Close Combat is favored to 2HKO uninvested Garchomp. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Ghost-types are the most reliable defensive checks to Sneasler because they resist or are immune to its STAB attacks. Sneasler is practically useless against Gholdengo, which is immune to anything it can do and can go for a Nasty Plot as it switches out. Basculegion-M can switch into a predicted attack and proceed to threaten heavy damage with Wave Crash or Last Respects, though it risks getting statused by Dire Claw. Sinistcha can redirect any of Sneasler's attacks and is bulky enough to take its Poison-type moves despite lacking a resistance to them. Mega Gengar can easily trap and eliminate Sneasler, paving the way for an ally like Kingambit to clean up late-game. If it hasn't Mega Evolved yet, Gengar can still force Sneasler out with its presence so that it can Mega Evolve and KO Pokemon with the Perish trap strategy. Ground-types like Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Excadrill easily OHKO Sneasler with their STAB attacks, and they can use Choice Scarf or weather to outspeed it if Unburden isn't active. The former two examples are durable enough to withstand Close Combat, while the last of these usually sports Focus Sash to guarantee survival. Other foes like Mega Metagross and Mega Staraptor can also win against Sneasler one-on-one thanks to their defensive profiles and super effective STAB moves, and Staraptor can weaken non-White Herb sets with Intimidate before Mega Evolving. Without an Unburden boost, faster attackers like Mega Delphox and Mega Aerodactyl can easily threaten Sneasler with an OHKO while generally being bulky enough to take at least one STAB attack from it. Notably, Mega Aerodactyl can bypass Focus Sash's insurance with Dual Wingbeat and neutralize Unburden's Speed boost with Tailwind. Farigiraf also can OHKO Sneasler with Psychic and turn its Speed and ability into hindrances by setting up Trick Room; additionally, Armor Tail prevents it from bothering Farigiraf's team with Fake Out. Toxapex is a sturdy foe that resists Sneasler's STAB attacks and can trap it with Infestation. While Toxapex can't directly damage Sneasler much, the opponent will have an easier time eliminating it with other Pokemon like Garchomp and Mega Charizard Y once it has been trapped. This can force you to make difficult decisions on whether or not to switch Sneasler out. Good Partners and Synergies: Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar are ideal partners for Sneasler, as they can easily handle Ghost-types. Additionally, Kingambit's Sucker Punch allows it to support Sneasler against speedier attackers if Unburden isn't active, notably OHKOing Mega Delphox. Meanwhile, Incineroar's access to Fake Out allows it to work together with Sneasler in shutting down opposing Pokemon, and Intimidate and Parting Shot make it easier for Sneasler to switch in while not getting hurt too much. Sneasler's good matchup against opposing Kingambit enables Basculegion-M to attack mid- or late-game more easily, as it will not have to worry about Sucker Punch. It can help Sneasler out in return by dealing with Fire-, Ghost-, and Ground-types like Mega Delphox, Gholdengo, and Excadrill. These two also pair well with Kingambit, forming an effective core of physical attackers that many players use. Sneasler stands out as a secondary offensive piece in setup-oriented teams based around Mega Evolutions like Mega Delphox, Calm Mind Mega Floette, and Mega Blastoise. It can easily deal with Kingambit, a foe these Pokemon can have trouble beating one-on-one, and it can provide Fake Out and Quick Guard support to let them more easily set up or attack unhindered. In return, Mega Delphox can handle Sinistcha, Toxapex, and Mega Metagross; Mega Floette can deal with Garchomp and Mega Staraptor; and a set-up Mega Blastoise can help out against Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-M. Furthermore, all of these Mega Evolutions have access to spread moves, which help Sneasler out against redirectors like the aforementioned Sinistcha.

Snorlax leverages its impressive bulk and ability to shrug off Fire-, Ice-, and Ghost-type damage from metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Basculegion-M to provide consistent value to its team over several turns through disruption and chip damage. Abilities: Thick Fat is crucial in allowing Snorlax to comfortably take attacks from common threats in the metagame such as Heat Wave from Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox and Blizzard from Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales. Yawn: Yawn allows Snorlax to put opposing Pokemon into the awkward position of either staying in and letting themselves be put to sleep or switching out and giving Snorlax and its partner a turn to do as they please. In either situation, opponents are forced to essentially pause for a turn while their Pokemon either takes time to wake up or switches out. Fissure versus High Horsepower: Fissure is a high-risk, high-reward move that punishes opponents by threatening to remove key pieces from their side if they can't KO Snorlax quickly or opt to ignore it and focus down its partner; it is sometimes able to secure an otherwise unobtainable victory. High Horsepower offers a much more consistent option that deals good damage to Steel- and Rock-types that otherwise resist its Normal-type STAB moves such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Hisuian Arcanine. Double-Edge versus Heavy Slam: Double-Edge is Snorlax's highest damage attack, allowing it to secure KOs against neutral targets that have been worn down by its partners. Heavy Slam deals less damage to neutral targets and is resisted by the Fire-types that Snorlax often finds itself facing such as Mega Charizard Y and Ceruledge, but it threatens Fairy- and Ice-types super effectively while preserving Snorlax's health with the absence of recoil. Other Options Encore: Snorlax can reasonably forgo a coverage move to opt for Encore, further enhancing its disruptive capabilities. Because of Snorlax's low Speed, it can use Encore to lock its foes into moves on the same turn as they use them. This contrasts with Encore users with Prankster or that are fast such as Whimsicott and Alolan Ninetails that give the opponent the window to switch out or Protect to avoid their Pokemon being locked into a move. Additionally, Snorlax can use Encore as a niche counter to Farigiraf and other Trick Room setters, underspeeding them and forcing them to use Trick Room again to undo the field effect. However, slow Encore users often have to correctly guess the move that their opponent is going to use, risking the chance that the opposing Pokemon gets locked into a move that they are more than happy to keep using. SP Spreads 21 HP / 32 Def / 13 SpD with Relaxed: This combination of HP and Defense investment allows Snorlax to survive Close Combat from Adamant Sneasler and Jolly Mega Staraptor. The rest of the SPs are put into Special Defense instead of HP to optimize bulk. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Snorlax struggles to stomach powerful physical Fighting-type attacks such as Close Combat from Mega Blaziken and Mega Staraptor and Low Kick from Kingambit and Dragonite. Toxapex also poses an immense problem for Snorlax, threatening to use Toxic and prevent Snorlax from sitting on the field for several turns. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Gengar pairs fantastically with Snorlax, as it is able to trap foes that Snorlax has targeted with Yawn and isolate and eliminate Fighting-type threats that would otherwise give Snorlax a hard time, while Snorlax is immune to the Ghost-type attacks that would hit Mega Gengar for super effective damage. Snorlax also slots nicely into Perish Song teams, disrupting opponents who aim to try and finish the game before the Perish Song counter reaches zero with Yawn and Protect. Perish Song conveniently also punishes less offensive opponents like Toxapex that Snorlax struggles into. Toxapex also pairs well with Snorlax, using Infestation to trap drowsy targets and chip away at them while they're asleep. Sinistcha complements Snorlax, with the former being able to redirect or switch into threatening Fighting-type moves; meanwhile, Snorlax can switch into the Fire-, Ice-, and Ghost-type moves that threaten Sinistcha. Sinistcha also sets Trick Room to take advantage of Snorlax's low Speed and heals Snorlax with Hospitality and Life Dew to help it stay on the field and continue to put foes to sleep and deal chip damage.

Torkoal serves as an incredible offensive threat in Trick Room, being tied for the lowest Speed in the metagame while having a respectable Special Attack, Drought to power up its Fire-type moves, and strong spread options like Eruption and Heat Wave. Together, these traits make it capable of melting through the likes of Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Maushold. Heat Wave: Heat Wave serves as Torkoal's backup spread damage option once Eruption loses too much power. Earth Power: Earth Power can be used to better threaten opposing Fire-types such as Incineroar and Torkoal while also hitting Toxapex. Weather Ball: Weather Ball deals far more damage than Heat Wave to a single target while also allowing Torkoal to target down foes protected by Wide Guard. Items Charcoal: Charcoal enables Torkoal to get OHKOs it otherwise wouldn't, notably letting Eruption nearly always OHKO Maushold and Heat Wave OHKO Sinistcha and offensive Mega Metagross. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Opposing weather setters like Pelipper and Mega Tyranitar cut heavily into Torkoal's damage while threatening it with their STAB moves, forcing Torkoal out if it wants to retake sun. They are also not too concerned about Torkoal's Fire-type STAB moves even in sun. Bulky Fire-resistant Pokemon such as Milotic, Garchomp, and Mega Delphox can stomach an Eruption and then fire back at Torkoal, greatly crippling its damage output. Wide Guard users such as Aerodactyl, Pelipper, and Toxapex can limit Torkoal's spread damage capabilities and force rough mindgames. Good Partners and Synergies: Torkoal requires Farigiraf to set up Trick Room and block priority that looks to reduce Eruption's power, such as Fake Out and Sucker Punch from Incineroar and Kingambit, respectively. Farigiraf can also use Psychic and Thunderbolt to pressure Water-types such as Toxapex and Mega Blastoise. Vileplume allows Torkoal to work outside of Trick Room thanks to Chlorophyll and After You enabling Torkoal to fire off an Eruption before it gets chipped too much. Vileplume can also target down Water- and Ground-types like Milotic and Garchomp with its Grass-type STAB attacks and spread sleep through Sleep Powder, giving Torkoal free turns to fire off its attacks or reposition. Mega Mawile pairs well with Torkoal, as Torkoal removes Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit for it. In return, Mega Mawile can use Play Rough to clean through Dragon- and Dark-types such as Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Mega Tyranitar for Torkoal and run Rock Slide to pick off Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox. Mega Kangaskhan supports Torkoal by using Fake Out either to stop Wide Guard, allowing Torkoal to cleanly use its spread options, or to help get Torkoal onto the field. Mega Kangaskhan can also use Ice Punch to remove Garchomp and Mega Dragonite.

Venusaur, due to its ability in Chlorophyll and excellent coverage, is a strong offensive threat in the metagame. These traits are complemented by Venusaur's access to Sleep Powder, which lets it put threats it and its partners struggle with like Garchomp and Aerodactyl to sleep. Earth Power versus Grass-type Coverage: Earth Power deals with Steel-types like Archaludon and Kingambit that resist its STAB moves. This coverage pairs well with its best partner in Mega Charizard Y, as Earth Power also deals with Rock- and Fire-types that Mega Charizard Y struggles to deal with, such as Glimmora and Blaziken. However, if the rest of the team is able to handle these threats, Grass-type coverage may be used instead. Sleep Powder versus Grass-type coverage: Sleep Powder has shaky accuracy but makes Venusaur especially terrifying. This is because Venusaur's boosted Speed under the sun lets it shut down checks like Mega Staraptor and Incineroar. If Venusaur is using Life Orb, a third move in Solar Beam or Leaf Storm is preferred to take advantage of the damage boost. Solar Beam versus Leaf Storm: Solar Beam gives Venusaur a more spammable STAB move. When boosted by Helping Hand, Solar Beam OHKOes Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl. On the other hand, Leaf Storm OHKOes threats like Milotic regardless of the weather at the cost of dropping Venusaur's Special Attack. Abilities: Chlorophyll boosts Venusaur's Speed under the sun, letting it outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon, Sneasler, and Mega Aerodactyl and put these threats to sleep or heavily damage them. Items: Focus Sash makes Sleep Powder's inaccuracy easier to handle, as it lets Venusaur at least have another chance to put a foe to sleep in case it misses. Focus Sash can also be crucial to let Venusaur deal some damage or inflict sleep in case the opponent sets up Tailwind. Alternatively, Life Orb boosts Venusaur's damage, letting it take out most Pelipper with Leaf Storm and non-bulky Mega Floette with Sludge Bomb. Other Options Protect versus a Third Attacking Move: Protect may be dropped in favor of a third attacking move to maximize Venusaur's offensive capabilities, as Venusaur will generally go first under the sun and put an opposing threat to sleep or finish it off before it can attack. Furthermore, Venusaur has decent bulk, surviving hits from Kingambit, Archaludon, Garchomp, and can have extra insurance if it's using a Focus Sash. However, dropping Protect leaves it vulnerable to Fake Out disruption. Energy Ball: Energy Ball is not dependent on the weather and does not drop Venusaur's Special Attack while still doing enough damage to remove Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert. However, this leaves Venusaur unable to OHKO bulky Basculegion-M. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: While Venusaur can invalidate most of its offensive checks with Sleep Powder, it can find itself in an extremely bad situation if Sleep Powder misses. Venusaur also fails to OHKO most threats like Mega Staraptor, Mega Metagross, and Hydreigon even with the Life Orb boost and will get OHKOed back. Bulkier Steel- and Grass-types like Gholdengo and Mega Venusaur give problems to Venusaur, as they shrug off its attacks. If Venusaur is lacking Earth Power, Gholdengo can even use it as setup fodder and OHKO it with +2 Make it Rain. Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales, Mega Tyranitar, and Pelipper can swap in and shut down Venusaur's ability, allowing their teammates to outspeed and remove it. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is Venusaur's best partner, as it sets sun to activate Chlorophyll and deals with Steel- and Grass-types that Venusaur struggles with, such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Mega Venusaur. Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott provide an extra Speed boost to match opposing teams' Tailwind. Aerodactyl also deals with opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, while Whimsicott provides more disruption in Encore and can also use Fake Tears to allow Venusaur to pick up surprise OHKOs. Incineroar helps Venusaur put a foe to sleep more safely by using Fake Out, and it also deals with Mega Metagross and Gholdengo. An alternative sun setter in Torkoal may be considered, as it frees up the Mega Evolution slot and allows the rest of the team to utilize other modes of play, such as Trick Room. Torkoal also provides Helping Hand support, which allows Venusaur to OHKO Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Garchomp.

However, if the rest of the team is able to handle these threats, Grass-type coverage may be used instead. Sleep Powder versus Grass-type coverage: Sleep Powder has shaky accuracy but makes Venusaur especially terrifying. This is because Venusaur's boosted Speed under the sun lets it shut down checks like Mega Staraptor and Incineroar. If Venusaur is using Life Orb, a third move in Solar Beam or Leaf Storm is preferred to take advantage of the damage boost. Solar Beam versus Leaf Storm: Solar Beam gives Venusaur a more spammable STAB move. When boosted by Helping Hand, Solar Beam OHKOes Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl. On the other hand, Leaf Storm OHKOes threats like Milotic regardless of the weather at the cost of dropping Venusaur's Special Attack. Abilities: Chlorophyll boosts Venusaur's Speed under the sun, letting it outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon, Sneasler, and Mega Aerodactyl and put these threats to sleep or heavily damage them. Items: Focus Sash makes Sleep Powder's inaccuracy easier to handle, as it lets Venusaur at least have another chance to put a foe to sleep in case it misses. Focus Sash can also be crucial to let Venusaur deal some damage or inflict sleep in case the opponent sets up Tailwind. Alternatively, Life Orb boosts Venusaur's damage, letting it take out most Pelipper with Leaf Storm and non-bulky Mega Floette with Sludge Bomb. Other Options Protect versus a Third Attacking Move: Protect may be dropped in favor of a third attacking move to maximize Venusaur's offensive capabilities, as Venusaur will generally go first under the sun and put an opposing threat to sleep or finish it off before it can attack. Furthermore, Venusaur has decent bulk, surviving hits from Kingambit, Archaludon, Garchomp, and can have extra insurance if it's using a Focus Sash. However, dropping Protect leaves it vulnerable to Fake Out disruption. Energy Ball: Energy Ball is not dependent on the weather and does not drop Venusaur's Special Attack while still doing enough damage to remove Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert. However, this leaves Venusaur unable to OHKO bulky Basculegion-M. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: While Venusaur can invalidate most of its offensive checks with Sleep Powder, it can find itself in an extremely bad situation if Sleep Powder misses. Venusaur also fails to OHKO most threats like Mega Staraptor, Mega Metagross, and Hydreigon even with the Life Orb boost and will get OHKOed back. Bulkier Steel- and Grass-types like Gholdengo and Mega Venusaur give problems to Venusaur, as they shrug off its attacks. If Venusaur is lacking Earth Power, Gholdengo can even use it as setup fodder and OHKO it with +2 Make it Rain. Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales, Mega Tyranitar, and Pelipper can swap in and shut down Venusaur's ability, allowing their teammates to outspeed and remove it. Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is Venusaur's best partner, as it sets sun to activate Chlorophyll and deals with Steel- and Grass-types that Venusaur struggles with, such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Mega Venusaur. Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott provide an extra Speed boost to match opposing teams' Tailwind. Aerodactyl also deals with opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, while Whimsicott provides more disruption in Encore and can also use Fake Tears to allow Venusaur to pick up surprise OHKOs. Incineroar helps Venusaur put a foe to sleep more safely by using Fake Out, and it also deals with Mega Metagross and Gholdengo. An alternative sun setter in Torkoal may be considered, as it frees up the Mega Evolution slot and allows the rest of the team to utilize other modes of play, such as Trick Room. Torkoal also provides Helping Hand support, which allows Venusaur to OHKO Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Garchomp.

Whimsicott leverages its Prankster ability and deep support movepool to help teammates outspeed crucial foes; for example, it allows non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M to outspeed and hit Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash. It is also able to output meaningful chip damage with Moonblast. Moonblast: Moonblast ensures Whimsicott can contribute to the battle even when affected by Taunt or having already set up Tailwind without any good targets for Encore being present. Notably, Whimsicott is able to break Focus Sashes on Pokemon such as Hisuian Arcanine, Sneasler, and Kingambit or threaten foes such as Garchomp, Mega Staraptor, and Dragonite. Encore: Encore allows Whimsicott to essentially bar foes from using any setup moves like Bulk Up and Calm Mind while being a deterrent against moves like Fake Out. This allows Whimsicott to be a very effective member of teams weak to setup strategies, as Whimsicott's Grass typing means Encore cannot be redirected by the likes of Sinistcha. Encore also deters foes from trying to use Protect to stall out Tailwind. Items: Focus Sash allows Whimsicott to get off more than one move in a battle, as it would otherwise quickly drop to foes like Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. This allows players to preserve Whimsicott to get another chance to set Tailwind later in the game, use Whimsicott's borrowed time to put an enemy in range of a partner's attack with Moonblast, or use Encore to deter foes from using moves such as Substitute, Fake Out, and setup moves like Bulk Up. Other Options Charm: Charm is only seen when Whimsicott is paired with Mega Staraptor, as it allows Whimsicott to boost Mega Staraptor's Attack due to Contrary. It also allows Whimsicott to survive certain attacks, such as Flare Blitz from Jolly Hisuian Arcanine, even if its Focus Sash is broken. It is almost always used over Encore. Teambuilding Checks and Weaknesses: Poison-types such as Glimmora and Mega Gengar threaten to bring Whimsicott down to Focus Sash and are potentially able to KO Whimsicott in one turn due to Sludge Bomb's considerable poison chance. Damage Struggles: Whimsicott struggles to contribute damage towards resisted targets such as Mega Charizard Y and Venusaur, while these also threaten it in return with Weather Ball or Heat Wave and Sludge Bomb, respectively. Foes with Dual Wingbeat, such as Mega Staraptor and Mega Aerodactyl, threaten to OHKO Whimsicott through Focus Sash while being able to match Whimsicott's Tailwind. Additionally, Gholdengo threatens Whimsicott with Make It Rain and is able to safely set up in front of Whimsicott because Good as Gold blocks Encore. Additionally, Hisuian Arcanine is able to take down Whimsicott before it can move with Extreme Speed if it had been taken down to Focus Sash beforehand, or it can use Flare Blitz first to so itself. Incineroar is able to use Fake Out to allow partners to bypass Encore on a crucial turn, such as after using Calm Mind. Additionally, Fake Out can break Whimsicott's Focus Sash if Whimsicott does not use Protect, while Incineroar does not fear Encore due to its Dark typing; Incineroar's Flare Blitz also deals significant damage to Whimsicott. Additionally, Armor Tail Farigiraf completely blocks Prankster Encore and can thus safely set up Trick Room in spite of it. Good Partners and Synergies: Pokemon with a middling Speed such as Basculegion-M greatly benefit from Tailwind, as it allows them to invest heavily into their offense and bulk without worrying too much about their Speed stat. It also allows them to outspeed their and Whimsicott's checks and potentially threaten them instead; under Tailwind, Mystic Water Basculegion-M threatens heavy damage onto Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash without getting outsped and OHKOed by Solar Beam. Whimsicott is also able to chip foes for KOs that Mystic Water Basculegion-M barely misses, such as Incineroar after an Intimidate and bulky Mega Charizard Y in the sun. **HyperOffensive Teams **: These teams generally aim to outspeed opposing Pokemon at all times and can struggle if facing a faster foe. Whimsicott can allow these teams to function against opposing teams with speed control, such as Trick Room from Sinistcha and Tailwind from Mega Staraptor, either through using Tailwind itself to maintain the Speed advantage or using Encore to dissuade opponents from using Trick Room or Tailwind. It is also able to effectively disrupt other defensive strategies such as Calm Mind Mega Floette with Encore. Mega Floette: Whimsicott excels with Mega Floette as a partner, allowing bulky Mega Floette to outspeed Pokemon such as Garchomp and Sneasler. Mega Floette also has issues dealing with Bulk Up Corviknight, which Whimsicott can deter from setting up with Encore. Attempts to dampen Mega Floette's damage output with Aurora Veil from Mega Froslass or Ninetales-A are also disincentivized by Encore. In return, Mega Floette boosts Whimsicott's damage output to considerable levels with Fairy Aura, allowing Whimsicott to threaten an OHKO on Garchomp with Moonblast and a 2HKO on Sneasler. This also allows Whimsicott to put bulkier foes such as Kingambit and Archaludon into range of Moonblast or Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette. Other Mega Evolutions: Whimsicott also finds an excellent partner in Mega Charizard Y, as Tailwind allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed threats such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M. Garchomp is threatened by Moonblast, further disincentivising Garchomp from staying in and using Rock Slide on Mega Charizard Y. Mega Charizard Y also threatens the Steel- and Ice-type Pokemon that Whimsicott fears, such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Mega Froslass, with Weather Ball in the sun and Heat Wave. Non-Mega Pokemon: Kingambit and Garchomp check the Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon that threaten Whimsicott. Kingambit is able to resist both of these types while also threatening most relevant Poison-types, such as Mega Gengar and Glimmora, with Kowtow Cleave and Iron Head, respectively, and is able to use Sucker Punch to deal heavy damage to Gholdengo and Mega Metagross before they can move. Garchomp is able to use Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake to OHKO most Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon and can use Rock Slide to threaten opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox. Additionally, Whimsicott checks opposing Garchomp, which could otherwise threaten Garchomp with Dragon Claw. However, Garchomp cannot safely use Earthquake next to Whimsicott, as it would break Whimsicott's Focus Sash.

With excellent typing, Supreme Overlord, and Sucker Punch, Kingambit is a powerful revenge killer and bulky attacker. Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave: Sucker Punch helps pick off weakened attackers and is excellent insurance against late-game Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M and Garchomp. Kowtow Cleave is usually needed as a second Dark-type attack, though, particularly for Substitute users like Mega Gengar that can play around Sucker Punch. Swords Dance: Kingambit's amazing bulk allows it to consistently survive big hits such as Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, letting it set up a Swords Dance and fire back with +2 Sucker Punch. Iron Head versus Low Kick: Iron Head provides the best all-around power and coverage, allowing Kingambit to better threaten Primarina, Mimikyu, and Mega Floette. Low Kick is less flexible and leaves Kingambit vulnerable to Primarina, but it's the best way to take on opposing Kingambit and has a high chance to OHKO offensive Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage. Items Black Glasses: Black Glasses doubles down on making Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave as deadly as possible. When combined with Supreme Overlord, +2 Sucker Punch + Black Glasses will always OHKO offensive Garchomp. Lum Berry: If Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance ahead of time, Lum Berry will prevent Yawn Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W from switching in and completely ruining its momentum. Chople Berry: Chople Berry allows Kingambit to withstand some weaker Fighting-type attacks, such as Close Combat from Aegislash and Scizor and unboosted Body Press from Corviknight. With maximum HP investment, Kingambit also has a high chance to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and an average chance to survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast. Alternate EV Spread 8 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def / 24 Spe with Adamant: This spread maintains enough bulk to almost always survive Adamant Life Orb Mimikyu's +2 Play Rough after Stealth Rock damage as well as Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake from full health. After maximizing Attack, the remaining SPs are invested into Speed, allowing Kingambit to outrun threats such as Mega Clefable with 2 Speed SPs.

Speed SP Benchmarks Moving first means Kingambit can improve certain matchups like Primarina. Generally speaking, it is recommended to sacrifice bulk instead of offensive power if wanting to reallocate to Speed. 3 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed negative Speed nature Aegislash. 11 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested base 60 Speed targets such as Clefable before Mega Evolution, Primarina, and Aegislash. 12 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar. 16 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Scizor before Mega Evolution. 18 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Corviknight, though its superior bulk and access to Body Press mean that it is still overwhelmingly favored in the matchup. 21 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Clefable, though keep in mind that Mega Clefable often receives Speed boosts from Baton Pass Espathra. 26 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

Pelipper is the main facilitator of rain teams, often preferred over fellow Drizzle user Politoed thanks to its Flying typing. It pairs excellently with Mega Swampert and Archaludon, which can take advantage of rain with Swift Swim and Electro Shot. The three also cover for each other's weaknesses, as Pelipper appreciates the two for being able to switch in on Electric-type attacks like Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon, while Archaludon appreciates Pelipper for being a switch-in to Hippowdon's Earthquake with its Ground-type immunity. U-turn: U-turn provides Pelipper with a safe way of bringing in Mega Swampert, Basculegion-M, and Archaludon, since they usually want to maximize their turns in the rain. It can also break Focus Sash in the process of doing so. U-turn allows Pelipper to gain momentum against threats that change the weather such as Alolan Ninetales and Mega Charizard Y. This makes resetting the weather back to rain much easier, as all Pelipper has to do is switch in again. Furthermore, U-turn is helpful for providing momentum against counters like Rotom-Wash. Weather Ball vs. Surf: Weather Ball is generally preferred due to its higher Base Power in the rain. Surf can be used to let Pelipper punish Alolan Ninetales, Hippowdon, and Mega Charizard Y for switching in without risking a Hurricane miss. With Surf, it also does not have to worry about rain running out of turns. Ice Beam: Ice Beam targets Garchomp and hits Archaludon neutrally. It provides coverage against Dragon- and Flying-types in the scenario where rain might not be up, but it only does slightly more damage than Hurricane even against super effective targets. Other Options Roost: Pelipper will sometimes want to use Roost with more defensive sets. This allows it to heal up on Meowscarada, Hippowdon, or even Mega Swampert, granting it better longevity as a physical wall. Tailwind: Tailwind can be very helpful for Archaludon and its middling Speed stat by turning it into a potent sweeper. Other teammates like Mega Metagross and Mimikyu can benefit from it, too. Items Damp Rock: Damp Rock allows Pelipper to have a longer effect on the battle long after it's left the field, making rain turns harder for opposing players to stall out. Focus Sash: Focus Sash provides survivability against Electric-type attacks like Zap Cannon from Mega Raichu Y and Thunder Punch from Mega Metagross and Mega Blaziken, as well as strong special attacks like Draco Meteor from Archaludon. This allows Pelipper to get an attack in and still be able to switch in later. SP Spreads 32 HP / 32 Def / 2 SpD with Relaxed: This spread emphasizes Pelipper's physical bulk; it improves Pelipper's matchup against Triple Axel Meowscarada and Rock Slide Garchomp by making their attacks 3HKOs rather than 2HKOs. The Relaxed nature simultaneously makes it a slower pivot than Corviknight and Scizor. 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: 32 Speed SPs allow Pelipper to outspeed most Primarina, Kingambit, and opposing uninvested Pelipper. A Modest nature boosts Pelipper's damage, notably allowing for a guaranteed 3HKO on Mega Gyarados with Hurricane and an OHKO on Mega Raichu Y with Weather Ball. It also helps against Mega Venusaur, which Pelipper's teammates tend to struggle with.

By utilizing Focus Energy and Scope Lens for guaranteed critical hits, not only can Archaludon ignore its own Draco Meteor's stat drops, but it can also rip through the defensive boosts of tanky threats like Clefable and its Mega Evolution! Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor can still be used as an upfront burst option prior to using Focus Energy, allowing Archaludon to adapt to what works best in each matchup. This can make Focus Energy + Draco Meteor a nasty surprise for anything trying to set up on a "weakened" Archaludon. Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon is for Fairy-types like Mimikyu and Primarina, which can ignore Draco Meteor. After Archaludon uses Focus Energy, it will always OHKO physically defensive Unaware Clefable. Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is more immediately threatening to Primarina than Flash Cannon, and it also prevents Archaludon from getting walled by Corviknight. While Flash Cannon is much more consistent against Clefable overall, Focus Energy + Thunderbolt can still get the job done on Mega Clefable because of its new typing. Substitute: Substitute can block status moves like Yawn from Hippowdon and Umbreon, giving Archaludon an opportunity to set up Focus Energy safely. Stamina versus Sturdy: The choice between abilities comes down primarily to what SP spread Archaludon is running. If Archaludon is using a bulky spread, it should have Stamina; if it's using a purely offensive spread, Sturdy is preferable. Other Options Foul Play and Dark Pulse: Even with a Modest nature and a Focus Energy boost, Archaludon cannot reliably 2HKO HP-invested King's Shield Aegislash with Thunderbolt. Foul Play allows Archaludon to always 2HKO physical attacker Aegislash in Shield forme, and it will also always 2HKO special attacker variants after a Focus Energy boost. Dark Pulse is another option that isn't as efficient against physical attacker Aegislash but makes it possible to threaten Gholdengo, which Foul Play can't do. EV Spreads 32 HP / 32 SpA / 2 Spe with Modest: This is a simple bulky attacker spread that lets Archaludon work particularly well against slower cycle and stall teams; it also helps Archaludon respond better to threats that try to set up while using Focus Energy. For example, maximum HP Archaludon avoids the OHKO from Mega Gyarados's +1 Earthquake. Substitute sets appreciate the HP investment as well, since Umbreon's Foul Play will almost never break Substitute in one hit. 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest or Timid: Focusing on Speed lets Archaludon outrun variants of Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott that have some Speed investment. A Modest nature gives an unboosted Draco Meteor the best shot of OHKOing specially defensive variants of Garchomp, but a Timid nature will allow Archaludon to outrun Adamant Mimikyu and Speed tie at worst with opposing Archaludon.
