With a superb special stat line, Seed Sower, and good moveset coverage, Arboliva can be a deceptively strong and long-living Assault Vest user! Seed Sower: Once activated, Grassy Terrain’s passive recovery and boosting of Grass-type attacks like Giga Drain can help Arboliva survive longer than expected. Grassy Terrain also halving Earthquake’s power is greatly appreciated by bulky teammates like Skeledirge, Arcanine, and Iron Hands. Dazzling Gleam: This move keeps Arboliva from becoming setup bait against foes like offensive Dragonite, and is also your best move into Wo-Chien before Tera. Tera Blast: Tera Blast is a great option for hitting types that Arboliva lacks natural coverage for. Tera Fire lets Arboliva hit Steel-types like Scizor and Tera Electric punishes Tera Flying users like Gholdengo. Both Tera Fire and Tera Electric cover Corviknight as well. Mirror Coat: This set’s massive special bulk can make getting one-shots with Mirror Coat awkward, but it is still a great option, particularly against boosted or super effective hits. Bear in mind though that this won’t work against Chi-Yu as long as it keeps its Dark typing. Leaf Storm: Leaf Storm trades consistency for a single turn of high burst damage and can be worth it if investing in Special Attack. Tera Types Tera Dependency - Medium: Arboliva’s raw special stats make it capable of tanking super effective hits without using Tera. Nonetheless, Tera is still a strong tool to extend Arboliva’s uptime and contest matchups that would otherwise capitalize on its mediocre defensive typing. Fire: Tera Fire can flip matchups against Focus Sash Chien-Pao and Choice Scarf Chi-Yu when healthy. If running Tera Blast, it also gives Arboliva the opportunity to contest Steel-types more effectively. Be aware, though, that this significantly worsens other key matchups, like Rotom-W. Poison: Tera Poison is a solid defensive option, especially into Toxic abusers like Toxapex and Clodsire. Notably, it flips several weaknesses, blocks Toxic, and allows for absorbing Toxic Spikes later in the match. Electric: Tera Electric is Gholdengo's worst nightmare. It gives a resistance to Make It Rain, blocks Thunder Wave from defensive sets, and punishes Tera Flying usage that is meant to get around Earth Power. On top of that, Arboliva still hits Corviknight very hard. Fairy: Tera Fairy is another great defensive option for neutralizing most of Arboliva's weaknesses, and the extra power behind Dazzling Gleam can make it easier to break defensive Dragonite variants. Grass: Tera Grass removes Arboliva’s Fighting weakness while maintaining Spore immunity, letting it check Breloom. If both Tera and Grassy Terrain are active, Modest Giga Drain can even 2HKO Breloom! Ground: While not as strong defensively, invested Tera Earth Power can OHKO uninvested Chi-Yu and Gholdengo. EV Spreads 236 HP / 4 Def / 140 SpA / 124 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This spread balances bulk and power, avoiding the 2HKO from Choice Specs Gholdengo's Make It Rain and almost always surviving Modest Chi-Yu’s Fire Blast before Tera! If running Tera Ground, there are enough Special Attack EV’s to turn Earth Power into an OHKO against uninvested Chi-Yu and Gholdengo. The Speed EV's Speed tie with 4 Speed Gastrodon. 236 HP / 252 SpA / 20 SpD with Modest: This simple spread still provides plenty of bulk while maximizing Special Attack, working nicely with Leaf Storm and Tera Types that boost Arboliva's coverage moves. If Grassy Terrain is present, fully invested Leaf Storm has a 75% chance of OHKOing 4 Special Defense Garchomp. The bulk investment lets Arboliva always avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Mystical Fire after Grassy Terrain recovery. 236 HP / 20 SpD / 252 Spe with Modest: While maximum Speed investment may seem a bit strange, it can be worth it when running Tera Fire Tera Blast to get the jump on Scizor, Corviknight and the rare Timid Amoonguss. 236 HP / 4 Def / 148 SpA / 20 SpD / 100 Spe with Modest: This alternative Speed spread gives Arboliva a nice boost in Special Attack while still letting it outrun 4 Speed Azumarill. This is usually more than enough Speed to outrun Ting-Lu as well.

Baxcalibur is a powerful attacker within the metagame, leveraging its immense Attack and powerful STAB moves to deal massive damage to foes, especially Rillaboom, Dragonite, and Ursaluna. Scale Shot is integral to Baxcalibur's strength, as when paired with Loaded Dice, it's a consistent STAB move that OHKOes Sneasler through Focus Sash while letting Baxcalibur outspeed many common foes, including Whimsicott and Sneasler. Icicle Spear also exploits Loaded Dice to act as a powerful multi-hit STAB option that can hit the many common Grass-, Ground-, and Flying-types in the metagame, such as Amoonguss, Rillaboom, Garchomp, and Dragonite. Ice Shard is a powerful priority option that can finish off low-HP foes, such as Sneasler and Pelipper after being brought down to Focus Sash. High Horsepower can be used to hit Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Kingambit while also super effectively hitting Incineroar. Loaded Dice allows Baxcalibur's Scale Shot and Icicle Spear to be consistently powerful damage options while letting it KO Focus Sash users, such as Sneasler, Indeedee-M, and Tatsugiri. Tera Ghost grants Baxcalibur an immunity to Fighting-type attacks, most notably Close Combat from Sneasler, and Fake Out from Incineroar and Rillaboom as well as Facade from Ursaluna. The Speed investment allows you Baxcalibur to outspeed Adamant Dragonite, while maximum Attack investment is crucial for guaranteeing the OHKO on Sneasler with Scale Shot or Icicle Spear. The defensive investment allows it to survive Eruption from Modest Choice Specs Hisuian Typhlosion and a +2 Body Press from Archaludon.

Teambuilding Baxcalibur works best on predominantly physically offensive teams, which take advantage of Fake Out utility, Defiant Pokemon, and methods of setting up to overwhelm the foe. Rillaboom synergizes with Baxcalibur, as it is able to threaten Water-types, most notably Primarina, as well as bolstering Baxcalibur's field presence with Fake Out and Grassy Terrain healing. In return, Baxcalibur pressures Grass-, Flying-, and Dragon-types like Sinistcha and Dragonite. Sneasler also pairs amazingly with Baxcalibur; Sneasler's most notable trait is the ability to boost Baxcalibur's offensive and defensive capabilities with Coaching, allowing it to potentially sweep entire teams. Furthermore, Sneasler can hit Steel- and Fairy-types like Kingambit and Alolan Ninetales, while Baxcalibur can threaten the Flying-types that check Sneasler, like Dragonite. Redirection from partners like Volcarona and Electabuzz can protect Baxcalibur from foes that threaten it, allowing for it to safely output damage, while in return, Baxcalibur hits the Grass-types immune to Rage Powder and the Flying- and Ground-types that threaten Volcarona and Electabuzz, respectively. Baxcalibur really struggles against Steel-types such as Kingambit and Gholdengo, which resist its STAB combination while threatening it back. The aforementioned Sneasler helps against Kingambit, while an ally Kingambit can handle Gholdengo. Intimidate from Incineroar and Hisuian Arcanine is also problematic, as it greatly weakens Baxcalibur's damage output; partners like Kingambit can punish Intimidate, while special attackers like Primarina can threaten both Pokemon without being weakened by it. Strategy Comments Baxcalibur functions primarily as a bulky physical sweeper, using powerful STAB moves to break through opposing teams while taking many hits in return. It shines early-game by weakening teams such that its partners can clean up easily; it's especially great against balance compositions with Rillaboom and Dragonite and rain teams once opposing Archaludon have been sufficiently weakened. It leverages its immense damage output to outshine other similar attackers like Dragonite against bulkier teams, while Thermal Exchange's burn immunity is crucial against Will-O-Wisp Magmar and Volcarona, which can be very problematic for other physical attackers. As aforementioned, Baxcalibur functions best early-game, using its massive damage to weaken the opposing team such that it can enable its teammates to clean, and it can sweep on its own with Coaching support from Sneasler. It is best used early-game when the opponent's team struggles to KO Baxcalibur, whereas in other matchups, KOing threatening foes like Sneasler and Gholdengo before bringing it in to clean late-game is better. Gholdengo is the most notable counter to Baxcalibur, resisting its STAB moves and dealing massive damage back, as does Kingambit. Stamina Archaludon also easily takes Baxcalibur's multi-hit attacks while accumulating Defense boosts to retaliate with Body Press. Use partners that can threaten these foes like your own Kingambit and Sneasler to OHKO them or force Terastallization into a typing that allows Baxcalibur to OHKO them. Sneasler can outspeed Baxcalibur and OHKO it with Close Combat, so either Terastallizing it to avoid Close Combat and KO Sneasler with Icicle Spear or using other partners like Gholdengo to threaten the foe is vital.

Indeedee-M is a fast Psychic Terrain setter that can both boost its partner's Psychic-type damage and use its Psychic Terrain for itself. Expanding Force is Indeedee-M's main method of dealing damage, while the combination of Trick Room and Imprison lets it both set Trick Room against faster teams and deny it against opposing Trick Room. Choice Scarf sets opt for Dazzling Gleam as a spread damage attack to hit Dark-type Pokemon, Trick to potentially cripple Trick Room setters like Porygon2, and Tera Blast as an option for a Normal-type STAB attack. Protect can be used on Focus Sash sets for increased flexibility. Focus Sash lets Indeedee-M survive at least one strong attack, letting it invest fully in Special Attack and Speed, while Choice Scarf lets it outspeed Pokemon like Sneasler and Dragapult. Tera Psychic guarantees Expanding Force OHKOes Amoonguss, while Tera Blast Fighting lets Indeedee-M threaten Dark-types that otherwise wall it.

Teambuilding Indeedee-M pairs well with speed control or redirection that allow it to use Expanding Force without being KOed. Priority Tailwind setters like Talonflame pair well with Indeedee-M, as they let it move first while also supporting the offensive teammates like Ursaluna-B that can weaken teams before Indeedee-M cleans up. Electabuzz provides speed control with Electro Web and redirects attacks with Follow Me. Gholdengo completely walls Indeedee-M. Partners like Throat Chop Sneasler and Ursaluna-B can help with this, threatening Gholdengo and forcing it to Terastallize out of its resistance to Expanding Force. Strategy Comments Indeedee-M is primarily a cleaner with Expanding Force. It is at its best when the foes are weakened and in range of Expanding Force. Since it wants to clean up, Indeedee-M thrives late-game once a partner like Ursaluna-B has dealt large amounts of damage. Indeedee-M struggles with Psychic-resistant foes, specially bulky foes, or some combination of these like Incineroar, Kingambit, or Archaludon. Partners like the Ursaluna formes can help with the Steel- and Dark-types that resist Expanding Force, directly threatening Steel-types and taking advantage of the fact that most Dark-types are weak to Ground like Kingambit and Incineroar. Sneasler can threaten specially defensive foes like Assault Vest Kingambit and Archaludon with Close Combat or Dire Claw if they Terastallize, letting Indeedee-M finish them off late-game. Rillaboom is another threat, overriding Psychic Terrain and threatening Indeedee-M with Wood Hammer. Sneasler helps with this, pressuring Rillaboom with Dire Claw.

Indeedee-F is a support Pokemon that mainly redirects attacks with Follow Me and sets up Trick Room. The Psychic Terrain that it sets up supports its teammates by protecting them from opposing priority moves like Sucker Punch and Fake Out. Follow Me provides redirection so that an allied Pokemon can safely set up Tailwind or Trick Room or set up with moves such as Annihilape's Bulk Up, Kingambit's Swords Dance, and Kommo-o's Clangorous Soul. Imprison prevents Trick Room from being set up by foes and shuts down the opponent's Follow Me Pokemon. Dazzling Gleam is mainly used to break opposing Pokemon that hold Focus Sash. Safety Goggles provides immunity to Amoonguss's Spore and Rage Powder while allowing Indeedee-F to use Follow Me to redirect Spore. Psychic Seed ensures that it takes attacks like Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon better. Rocky Helmet punishes any Pokemon that attack it with contact-making moves or have said attacks redirected to it. Some of these contact moves are Annihilape's Drain Punch and Rage Fist, Rillaboom's Wood Hammer, and Sneasler's Dire Claw and Close Combat. Rocky Helmet also has the ability to break Focus Sashes and threaten any Pokemon that use multi-hit moves, such as Maushold and its Population Bomb. Sitrus Berry helps out Indeedee-F's longevity by allowing it to survive moves like +4 Archaludon's Body Press and Pelipper's Weather Ball. Fairy is the best Tera type for Indeedee-F. It provides resistances to Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch, Archaludon's Body Press, and Sneasler's Close Combat and Throat Chop and an immunity to Dragon-type moves from Archaludon, Dragonite, Garchomp, and Dragapult. As a little bonus, it offers a STAB boost to Dazzling Gleam. Tera Grass gives Indeedee-F a resistance to Grass-type moves such as Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and Water-type moves such as Basculegion-M's Wave Crash and Pelipper's rain-boosted Weather Ball, which are its partners' most common weaknesses. Tera Grass also provides immunity to Amoonguss's Spore and redirection. However, if Indeedee-F uses Safety Goggles, Tera Grass is not recommended.

Teambuilding Indeedee-F works best on dedicated Trick Room teams, using Follow Me to almost always guarantee its partner to set up Trick Room as well as pairing well with Trick Room sweepers. It sets up Psychic Terrain to prevent Fake Out from disturbing your team's Trick Room setup as well as preventing priority attacks from threatening its partners. Ursaluna and Ursaluna-B are common partners for Indeedee-F. Trick Room can help with the speed control both Ursaluna formes need, and Follow Me can protect them from non-spread moves while allowing them to deal Normal-type damage with Blood Moon and Facade and Ground-type damage with Headlong Rush, Earthquake, and Earth Power. Other Trick Room sweepers, such as Hatterene and Torkoal, are the best Trick Room partners for Indeedee-F. Hatterene can threaten the opponent's team with heavy Psychic-type damage from Expanding Force, and Torkoal can threaten heavy Fire-type damage with Eruption, Weather Ball, and Heat Wave. Gallade can threaten Dark-type Pokemon with Sacred Sword and provide Wide Guard support to protect its side of the field from spread moves. Sneasler pairs nicely with Indeedee-F because Sneasler can hold the Psychic Seed, activating its Unburden ability. Kingambit will decimate any opposing Indeedee-F. Even if Indeedee-F Terastallizes into a Fairy-type, Kingambit will still do significant amount of damage to it. Therefore, a Fighting-type Pokemon like Sneasler should be used to threaten Kingambit, as it can almost always guarantee a OHKO on Kingambit with Close Combat. Rillaboom is another threat to watch out for, as it can set up Grassy Terrain, which can override the Psychic Terrain that Indeedee-F sets up. Strategy Comments Indeedee-F is a support Pokemon. It redirects attacks with Follow Me, provides speed control with Trick Room, provides important chip damage with Psychic or Dazzling Gleam, and helps partners spam Expanding Force. Indeedee-F is best used early-game. As a lead, it is really good to get a head start at initializing your strategy. Sneasler, Ursaluna-B , and Ursaluna are all common Pokemon to lead alongside Indeedee-F. The Sneasler + Indeedee-F lead doesn't require Trick Room to be utilized and does not require any other setup. The Ursaluna-B + Indeedee-F lead does not have to be in Trick Room, depending on the Speed investment of Ursaluna-B, and it unleashes some of the largest amount of special damage in the metagame. Ursaluna and Indeedee-F have to be in Trick Room and need Ursaluna's Guts boost to be utilized thoroughly. However, this lead provides some of the largest amount of physical damage in the metagame. The biggest weakness Indeedee-F has to deal with is the move Taunt. Taunt prevents Indeedee-F from setting up Trick Room and doing its job as a supportive Pokemon. The most reliable way to get rid of Taunt is to switch Indeedee-F out. Sometimes, Indeedee-F has to rely on its ally to set up Trick Room instead. Because it is a Trick Room Pokemon, it is vulnerable to being double targeted, which prevents Trick Room from being set up. Fortunately, it has Follow Me, which can redirect non-spread moves to it, allowing its ally to set up Trick Room.

Pawmot separates itself from Iron Hands by having an excellent support movepool and a good Speed tier. Double Shock and Close Combat: Double Shock and Close Combat are its most important attacks, but note that it can only use Double Shock once without Terastallizing. Once Terastillized, Pawmot you can use Double Shock continuously for big damage, even on foes that resist it. Mach Punch: Priority allows Pawmot to revenge kill better, hitting Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Iron Bundle super effectively. Ice Punch: Ice Punch gives Pawmot coverage against Ground-types, most notably Great Tusk, Clodsire, and Garchomp, in addition to hitting Dragonite for lots of damage before it Terastallizes. Revival Blessing: Revival Blessing's one shot of reviving a teammate gives Pawmot an extremely unique niche in turning battles around, though it doesn't fit all offensive teams. Nuzzle: This is notably one of the few ways to inflict paralysis on Gholdengo. Nuzzle is best when used with a Focus Sash, as Pawmot can paralyze the foe and outspeed it the next turn, getting another move off before it faints. Encore: Encore does a great job of punishing passive play, and prevents easy setup from slower defensive foes such as Garganacl. Other Options Fake Out: This can be used to get an edge against common Focus Sash leads such as Meowscarada. Tera Types Tera Dependency - Situational: Terastallizing is only needed if Pawmot is on the field long enough for repeated uses of Double Shock. Electric: An Electric Tera Type allows Pawmot to continuously use Double Shock, making it an effective late-game cleaner. Items Focus Sash: Focus Sash trades the damage boost from the other items for better opportunities to use support moves. Life Orb: Life Orbs enables easier revenge kills at the cost of recoil. Magnet: Magnet will power up Double Shock without the recoil from Life Orb, and it also frees up Life Orb for a teammate to use instead. Abilities Iron Fist: This boosts the power of Mach Punch and Ice Punch, giving Pawmot more powerful priority and coverage. Volt Absorb: Volt Absorb's Electric immunity stops Magnezone, Rotom-W, and Rotom-H from using Volt Switch to create safe switch-ins. Natural Cure: This allows Pawmot to take status moves more freely, such as Yawn from Dondozo or Will-O-Wisp from Skeledirge.

This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out the format page! If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Assault Vest Rillaboom excels at being a bulky pivot that is able to support its team with Fake Out and Grassy Terrain recovery while having high damage output with Wood Hammer. Rillaboom synergizes very well with setup Pokemon that appreciate the free turns that Fake Out provides as well as the healing from Grassy Terrain. Grassy Glide allows Rillaboom to take care of weakened foes, while Wood Hammer compensates for the low power of Grassy Glide to operate as a nuke. U-turn is usually the last move of choice on Rillaboom, as it allows one of its partners to come in safely while chipping down the foe, but Rillaboom can forgo it for High Horsepower, which allows Rillaboom to hit common Steel- and Fire-types such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Incineroar. Assault Vest is used on Rillaboom, as it enhances Rillaboom's ability to pivot, with the tradeoff being that it is unable to run status moves such as Protect and Taunt. Tera Fire gives Rillaboom an immunity to Will-O-Wisp and a resistance to common Fire- and Steel-type moves from Pokemon such as Incineroar, Hisuian Typhlosion, and Gholdengo. The Speed investment allows Rillaboom to outspeed maximum Speed Tyranitar and uninvested Annihilape, while the Attack investment allows Rillaboom to OHKO both Ursaluna formes with Wood Hammer. The bulk allows Rillaboom to live Flare Blitz from Incineroar, two Ice Beams from Porygon2, and a +1 Fiery Dance from Volcarona. Assault Vest Rillaboom is able to function a lot more effectively as a bulky pivot, as it is able to switch into special moves more easily. This is particularly helpful against teams that are more offensive in nature, such as hard Trick Room teams and Tailwind hyper offense teams that usually use strong specially offensive Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Hatterene to break through teams.

Teambuilding Rillaboom can be used with basically anything, as a lot of Pokemon appreciate its supportive toolkit. However, the Pokemon that Rillaboom synergizes the most with are, as stated before, setup Pokemon. Setup Pokemon appreciate Fake Out and Grassy Terrain from Rillaboom; the former gives them space to set up, while the latter offers residual healing, increasing their survivability. Rillaboom also appreciates partners that can help against Fire-types, such as Incineroar, and Steel-types, such as Archaludon and Kingambit. Primarina and Sneasler are great partners for Rillaboom, as they help with the aforementioned checks, while Rillaboom can help against the Water-types that resist Primarina's Hyper Voice and double Sneasler's Speed by using Grassy Terrain to activate Grassy Seed, triggering Unburden. Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Volcarona are the main setup partners for Rillaboom; Kingambit scares away Incineroar, Gholdengo offers quick setup and spread damage, and Volcarona is able to KO the Grass-types that resist Wood Hammer. Rillaboom's main weakness is its typing. Grass may be good defensively because it lets Rillaboom switch in easily, but it is not great offensively in this metagame, as a plethora of Pokemon resist Wood Hammer such as Amoonguss, Gholdengo, Archaludon, Kingambit, and Incineroar. The main way around this is to utilize Rillaboom's support capabilities when it cannot offer anything offensively in the position and pivot intelligently. Sneasler is another big threat, as it has a faster Fake Out than Rillaboom and can threaten it with Dire Claw. Bulky redirectors, such as Magmar and Electabuzz, can take big hits from Sneasler for Rillaboom. Smart pivoting and chipping Sneasler down throughout the game are how Rillaboom is able to get rid of it. Strategy Comments Rillaboom's role is as a bulky support Pokemon that can still do great damage. Pivot with U-turn to cycle Fake Out, giving its partner free turns, and, when possible, nuke foes with powerful Wood Hammers and Grassy Glides. Rillaboom is usually a valuable part of the team throughout a game. In the beginning, Rillaboom is able to leverage Fake Out to allow its partner to set up early or get early damage off. Rillaboom usually pivots during the middle of the game to get more use out of Fake Out and get Grassy Terrain back on the field. Rillaboom chips down the opposing team throughout the game, but it excels at cleaning up in endgames thanks to its access to priority moves and high damage output. The biggest checks to Rillaboom are Pokemon that resist Grass. When playing against these Pokemon, it is important to pivot out with U-turn to preserve Rillaboom and allow it to get more value later in the game with its attacks. Additionally, partners such as the aforementioned Sneasler and Primarina can help against these Grass-resistant foes.
